item.title: [Post and Courier] Is Shohei Ohtani taking away an American's job?
item.dc:creator: Charles Sauer Columnist
item.description: Vice President JD Vance recently announced the administration was cutting off Microsoft's access to H-1B workers, and — just to put a vile exclamation mark on it —he went ahead and called these workers indentured servants. item.content:encoded:
Vice President JD Vance recently announced the administration was cutting off Microsoft's access to H-1B workers, and — just to put a vile exclamation mark on it —he went ahead and called these workers indentured servants.
For many, the VP's argument makes sense. However, while those people are mostly wrong, they can't really be blamed because they also likely don't know what a job at Microsoft looks like.
On the other hand, we all have sports teams that we cheer for, and it turns out that many of these sports teams employ foreign-born athletes, and not a small number of them either. In the NHL's case almost 70% of the athletes are foreign-born, soccer is almost 60%, the NBA is at 23%, and baseball is at 25%.
It could be argued these athletes are stealing American jobs. But that argument is ridiculous and anyone that watches sports would agree. Without these players, not only would the teams be less competitive, the games would be less entertaining and the leagues would make less money.
For instance, Shohei Ohtani is considered one of the best baseball players to have ever played. What college player would fill his shoes if ICE handcuffed him and deported him at gunpoint? How much worse would the Dodgers be? And with a contract valued at $700 million over 10 years, it is kind of tough to consider Ohtani an indentured servant.
It isn't just Ohtani. Given how competitive the environment is, professional sports leagues have scouts scouring the world in search of the next athlete that could put them over the top. The Miami Heat's Greek Freak, Giannis Antetokounmpo himself, holds dual citizenship in Greece and Nigeria, and lead the Bucks to an NBA championship in 2021.
We have the best sports leagues in the world because we have the best players from around the world.
Now, what do sports teach us if we want to have the best economy in the world? It doesn't teach us that foreign workers are necessarily better, but it does teach us that companies should have access to the workers that they believe give them the best chance at winning. Any restrictions on that means that US businesses are handcuffed. If they aren't allowed to hire the Shohei Ohtani of coding, if they aren't allowed to hire the Giannis of algorithms, they aren't going to perform as well as they could.
Microsoft has 120,000 US employees; the company filed for 6,000 H-1B visas in 2025 and most of those were for employees that were already working for the company. That is less than 1% of their US workforce.
If Vance really wanted to help “create” American jobs by stopping immigrants he would have gone after the NHL, but he would have been chased off the stage if he suggested taking away the visas of professional sports teams. He should have been chased off the stage for suggesting the same for Microsoft.
He wasn't though, which shows that there is a lot of education left to get the US economy back on track.
The same administration claimed tariffs were going to help the economy - by raising revenue, increasing jobs, and providing leverage with our trading partners. Maybe one of those is possible, but all three at the time are impossible. Administration officials have claimed that the war with Iran is going to help the economy, but it's really just raising costs at the gas pump and grocery store. Now the same people claim they can create jobs by sticking itself into Microsoft's HR department. Maybe it's time to take more of a hands off approach.

item.content:encoded:
Nothing beats Father Time, and that includes an aging Dodgers core.
Seven out of the nine regulars within the Dodgers lineup are on the wrong side of 30, with Andy Pages being the only regular under the age of 27. Players such as Freddie Freeman and Max Muncy are both entering the twilight of their careers, and Mookie Betts will turn 35 years of age during the 2027 season.
The Dodgers have plenty of prospects waiting for their chance to shine at the game’s highest level, and outfielder Josue De Paula is the cream of the crop of young talent. The team is hoping to increase his playing time in the outfield as opposed to his fill-in at designated hitter this past season, and that could mean a change of scenery for an aging player such as Teoscar Hernández, per Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
If De Paula can turn himself into a viable everyday left fielder, it could bring about some of the greatest change in what could be a transitional offseason for a Dodgers roster looking to get younger. De Paula’s rise would at the very least reduce Teoscar Hernández to a more limited role, and at most prompt the team to find a trade partner for the veteran outfielder.
Dodgers owner Mark Walter is a controversial name within the Los Angeles sports world, and Major League Baseball is now monitoring him amid a federal probe, notes Valentina Martinez of the California Post. Walter briefly became owner of the Los Angeles Lakers until he sold the team to both Josh Kushner and Bob Iger for a record $12.5 billion.
“As always when we have an investigation, external law enforcement, whatever, we monitor that and that’s where we are right now,” Manfred told reporters.
Larry Holder of The Athletic writes about pro wrestler Arik Cannon, who was lucky to find a one-of-one Shohei Ohtani “Game for the Ages” card. Cannon hopes to sell the card in the hopes of paying off his father’s debts.
“In August 2023, we lost my mom to cancer, and it’s been really, really rough on my dad,” Cannon said. “So the first thing I’m going to do is I’m going pay off all his debt. And then I don’t know what my other options are at, but it’ll be more than enough to take care of him. Whatever’s left over for me, I’m probably just going to put it away and make sure that I don’t become one of those cliché Powerball winners that had money and now it’s gone.”

item.title: [Rising Apple] 1 dream target, 1 realistic target, 1 mistake NY Mets could make in Tarik Skubal backup plans
item.dc:creator: Pat Ragazzo

item.content:encoded:
The New York Mets will surely be in on two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal in free agency. But it won't be easy to land Skubal, who could draw the richest contract for a starting pitcher in MLB history.
The Mets must add starting pitching this offseason, whether they sign Skubal or not. So, if they miss out on Skubal, let's take a look at one dream target, one realistic target and one mistake the Mets could make as Plan B.
The Tarik Skubal backup plans for the Mets
The Dream Target
If the Mets can't lure Skubal to Queens, right-handed starter Michael King would be a dream target for their pivot plan. King has an opt-out in his deal this offseason that he could exercise to test the open market. King is coming off a strong season with the San Diego Padres, where he went 12-10 with a 3.21 ERA, 1.18 WHIP, 127 ERA+. 4.13 FIP, 159 strikeouts and a 4.3 bWAR in 32 starts and 185 innings. He also came up clutch in the postseason with a 0.64 ERA in three appearances (two starts).
King is a proven arm, who has pitched on the big stage and performed well. He began his career with the Yankees, where he spent his first five seasons in the big leagues. Should the Mets not sign Skubal, King would be a dream move and positive veteran presence to add to a rotation that features a trio of youngsters: Nolan McLean, Christian Scott and Zac Thornton.
The realistic target
Why does it feel like a reunion could be brewing between Clay Holmes and the Mets? Holmes, a former All-Star reliever and closer, signed a three-year, $38 million deal to become a starter with the Mets ahead of the 2025 season. The Mets got the most out of Holmes during his time in Queens, posting a 16-12 record and 3.26 ERA in 42 appearances and 40 starts. Holmes had a 2.39 ERA in nine starts to begin the 2026 season with the Mets, but broke his leg in a May outing after getting hit by a comebacker.
The Mets dealt Holmes to the Chicago Cubs at the trade deadline, and he proceeded to produce a 4.25 ERA in his final nine starts. Holmes is known for being a ground ball pitcher, so the Mets should focus on improving their infield defense if they bring him back. It feels like re-signing Holmes is a realistic move for the Mets given his success with the team as a starter. Holmes is expected to opt-out of his deal this offseason.
The mistake
Trading for Tampa Bay Rays ace Drew Rasmussen seems like a good move given recency bias, but it would ultimately be a mistake. Rasmussen has a $20 million club option for 2027 and will be a free agent after next season if it is exercised. The Mets would have to give up multiple prospects to acquire one season of his services, and they just made a similar deal for Freddy Peralta, which didn't work out.
Rasmussen turns 32-years-old next season, has had multiple elbow surgeries and has three good campaigns under his belt across a seven-year career. It would be a mistake for the Mets to give up assets to acquire just one season of Rasmussen via trade. The Mets would be unlikely to re-sign him to a long-term deal following 2027 given his age and injury history.

item.dc:creator: Los Royers

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Alex Vesia thanked Dodgers fans and acknowledged an uncertain future in Los Angeles as the left-handed reliever prepares to enter free agency.
Vesia reflected on the season in an Instagram post Monday, calling 2026 “by far the hardest year” of his career. He referenced battles with confidence, expectations and the mental swings that accompanied the season.
“I don’t know what the future holds, but I do want to say thank you to Dodger Nation for showing me so much love over the past 6 years, especially this year,” Vesia wrote. “I’m just a man on a mission!”
Vesia also thanked his teammates for supporting him through his difficult days and embracing the energy he brought during the better ones. He did not announce a departure or say that his time with the Dodgers is over.
Alex Vesia’s Dodgers future is uncertain
The uncertainty is real because Vesia is set to become a free agent after the World Series. The Dodgers exercised his 2026 club option last offseason, buying out his final year of salary-arbitration eligibility. That option paid him $3.65 million.
Vesia remained one of the Dodgers’ most dependable relievers in 2026. He recorded a 2.64 ERA, 74 strikeouts and three saves across 58 innings and 72 appearances.
The left-hander joined Los Angeles in a February 2021 trade with the Miami Marlins. He has since become a fixture in the bullpen, surpassing 300 appearances with the Dodgers in April.
Vesia thanks teammates and Dodger Nation
Vesia’s message arrived three days after the Milwaukee Brewers eliminated the Dodgers from the National League Championship Series. His post read as both an honest reflection on a difficult season and an expression of gratitude before an important career decision.
The Dodgers can attempt to re-sign Vesia once free agency begins. Until then, his post leaves open the possibility that six seasons in Los Angeles could mark the end of this chapter.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Scott Boras Lays Out Tarik Skubal Free Agency Outlook Ahead of Dodgers Talks
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal is entering free agency, and his renowned baseball agent, Scott Boras, discussed his marquee client’s free-agent status. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal is entering free agency, and his renowned baseball agent, Scott Boras, discussed his marquee client’s free-agent status.
Scott Boras’ reputation
Boras is known for being an aggressive negotiator who typically refuses contract extensions throughout a player’s career, letting them enter free agency and letting the free market decide their ultimate value.
When it comes to getting the best possible deal for his clients, especially the top ones, no one in baseball has a more stellar reputation.
However, while that often benefits his clients, teams can struggle to lock down their players when Boras is in the mix.
With Skubal, Boras is in a position to do what he does best: explore the market, try to spark a bidding war, and land a massive deal that should break records.
How he views Skubal’s market
Skubal’s status as one of the best pitchers alive makes a sales pitch unnecessary. Boras, when speaking to The Athletic’s Andy McCullough, made an interesting statement that relays how he views his client.
“Last time around, everybody talked about Skuby Doo. It’s kind of like, with Skubal now, it’s Skuby Done. He’s proven it at all levels, in different markets, in different environments,” Boras told The Athletic.
How long will it take for Skubal to sign?
Boras is typically not shy about waiting for the best possible deal and letting some teams panic about getting a deal done.
With a lockout coming on December 1st, Boras thinks teams will be highly motivated to secure players before a new set of rules comes into place.
“For many teams, I can make an argument it’s clearly best for them to sign players currently, before the (new) CBA, than it is after,” Boras told The Athletic.
“Because they have more freedom to do what they’re going to do. They can react later. Now they can get the talent. They can get what they want.”
The Dodgers, who will be talking to Boras, and the rest of the league, will need to make their pitches and offers quickly and be ready to negotiate fast, because the best player in free agency may not be available for long.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers' Andrew Friedman Speaks Out About Tarik Skubal's Free Agency
item.dc:creator: Gabe Smallson; Unknown

item.content:encoded:
In an offseason of many transitions for the Los Angeles Dodgers, one decision looms among the largest.
When the two-time defending champions traded for two-time Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline, there was a certain amount of risk attacked to it.
The risk was not necessarily in terms of play as he attained a 2.61 ERA in his 10 regular season starts as a Dodger, but with the fact that Skubal would become a free agent when the season ended.
The season ended far earlier than anyone around the organization would have wanted, and now Skubal is entering free agency as by far the best player available. The team that ends up succesfully courting the soon-to-be 30-year-old Skubal, however, is expected to potentially spend close to $500 million to lock him down.
President of baseball operations Andrew Friedman was asked about Skubal at the team's end-of-season press conference, and praised him for his quick transition to a new team.
“It’s not easy for a guy to get traded in the middle of a season to come to a new city, new clubhouse,” Friedman said. “The way he was able to seamlessly transition, not just in terms of on the field, but in the clubhouse, I can’t say enough good things about the impact that he made in such a short period of time.”
As for Skubal's postseason play, as expected, he excelled.
In two October starts (11 innings), he had a 2.45 ERA, striking out 14 and walking four.
Now Friedman has an opportunity to ensure that those weren't the final two starts of Skubal's Dodgers tenure.
In terms of Skubal's free agency, Friedman avoided much discourse, instead saying Skubal will make a business decision at the end of the day, and all the organization can do is have discussions with his agent, Scott Boras.
“He’s put himself in this position to go out and be a free agent. And for us, it’s [to] continue to talk to Scott," Friedman said. "But he and his family have to make a choice over where they want to spend the next X number of years, and obviously we wish him nothing but the best.”
The hope for LA is that Skubal's talents can be long appreciated at Dodger Stadium, and that he doesn't join the unfortunate list of trade deadline acquisitions who left the following offseason.
Though some worked out more than others, players like Yu Darvish, Manny Machado, Max Scherzer and most recently Jack Flaherty (who also came from the Detroit Tigers) are each a part of a list that Dodgers fans will hope to not see Skubal on.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Gabe Smallson is a sportswriter based in Los Angeles with a focus in sports and entertainment content. Gabe has previously worked at Newsweek and Dodgers Nation. He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.

item.content:encoded:
公式放送局『MLBネットワーク』内の番組「MLB NOW」に出演した元GMが、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手に言及。左翼手へのコンバートを提言した。また、米地元紙『ロサンゼルス・タイムズ』のピル・プラシュケ記者は「大谷のトレードを真剣に検討する必要がある」などと記した。ポストシーズンで鳴りを潜めた二刀流に対し、多くの議論が交わされている。
■DHにフリーマン、ベッツ
大谷はポストシーズン8試合に出場し、打率.192、1本塁打、3打点と不振を極め、チームがワールドシリーズ3連覇を逃す一因ともなった。投手としての負担が、打撃にも悪影響を及ぼしているという論調は根強く、二刀流を断念し、打者専念を求める関係者も少なくない。
この二刀流継続に対する“逆風”は現在も収まる気配はなく、「MLB NOW」に出演したダン・オダウド氏は「私なら大谷を左翼手として起用しますね。そうすればDHの枠が空くので、そこにフレディ・フリーマン内野手やムーキー・ベッツ内野手を入れることができます。彼らは年齢を重ねており、体への負担を抑えながら打席に立つ機会を得られます」と話し、大谷の左翼コンバートを提案した。
同氏はガーディアンズでGM補佐を務め、ロッキーズでは約15年間に渡ってGM職に就いていた。
■「ドジャースは真剣に検討を」
ドジャースの左翼手といえば、34歳のテオスカー・ヘルナンデス外野手だが、守備に不安を抱えている上、打撃も好不調の波が激しい。そのため、今オフの補強ポイントに「左翼手」を挙げる関係者も少なくない。
編成部門のベテランが外野手へのコンバートを提案した一方、地元紙はトレードも視野に入れるべきと主張した。『ロサンゼルス・タイムズ』のピル・プラシュケ記者は、「大谷は今季、フルタイムでは打者と投手を両立できないという揺るぎない証拠を示した。ドジャースは、彼をマウンドから下ろす必要がある」とし、「もし、彼がこの悪影響をもたらす（二刀流という）茶番劇を続けるなら、球団は彼をトレードに出すことを真剣に検討する必要がある」と訴えた。
もちろん、チームも大谷自身も二刀流継続を明言しており、コンバートもトレードも実現可能性は低い。しかし、結果を出さない限り、「投手断念」を求める声が止むことはない。来季、復調した姿を見せることで“雑音”を封じたいところだ。

item.dc:creator: Aaron Coloma
item.description: Former Los Angeles Dodgers infielder Miguel Rojas, who retired after the team fell in the NLCS this season, spoke about the impact his time with the Dodgers had on him. Rojas is currently serving as a correspondent at the World Series between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays, but also spared some time before the game to answer questions about himself. “I told the players, the staff and the front office, not just thank you, they changed my life,” Rojas said. “They got me the opportunity t
item.content:encoded:
Former Los Angeles Dodgers infielder Miguel Rojas, who retired after the team fell in the NLCS this season, spoke about the impact his time with the Dodgers had on him.
Rojas is currently serving as a correspondent at the World Series between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays, but also spared some time before the game to answer questions about himself.
“I told the players, the staff and the front office, not just thank you, they changed my life,” Rojas said. “They got me the opportunity to come back home to LA where I made my debut 12 years ago in 2014 and having the opportunity to live the best four years of my life in baseball.
“It wasn’t just for me, it was for my family, the people that I really care about. My son, they grabbed my son under their wing and they made growth with him. He was shagging balls in the outfield, he was living the dream. …That’s what I told the guys, thank you for changing my life.”
Rojas has sung the Dodgers’ praises the entire year, especially following his retirement. After his last game, the veteran expressed his desire to continue serving the team after stepping away from the sport.
“I want to stay here,” Rojas said. “I want to wear this uniform in a different capacity and continue to make the organization better.”
When Did Miguel Rojas Return to the Dodgers?
Rojas made his debut with the Dodgers in 2014, but the team traded him after his rookie year in a big deal with the Miami Marlins—during which the team also acquired Kiké Hernandez and Austin Barnes.
He stayed with the Marlins for nearly a decade, but the Dodgers decided to bring him back to the team in 2023, sending a minor-league infielder the other way.
Through his 446 games with the team from 2023-26, Rojas hit 22 homers and drove in 117 RBIs for the Dodgers, also posting a .688 OPS and hitting the biggest home run of his life. He stepped up to the plate in Game 7 of the 2025 World Series and hit a solo home run in the top of the ninth to tie the game and swing the momentum in the Dodgers’ favor as they went on to win their second consecutive World Series.
Rojas will forever be a Dodgers legend, and his constant praise of the organization shows how well the team treats their players.

item.content:encoded:
If the Los Angeles Dodgers can get any return value for Alex Call this offseason, they're going to jump on the opportunity.
Recently, The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya and Katie Woo said they expect him to be non-tendered next season, meaning the Dodgers would move on him for nothing.
Both believe they missed their window on trading the 32-year-old, but Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller doesn't believe that's the case.
This would be far from a major trade, but putting together a deal with the Philadelphia Phillies, as Miller suggests, would be a huge benefit to both sides.
Phillies are in the market for a cheap outfielder
If Philadelphia wants to make a move for an inexpensive outfielder who can get the job done, look no further than Call.
The Dodgers will certainly be fielding calls for him once again, pun intended, and he's a super trade-friendly asset to any team he'd join.
Call is still eligible for three more years of arbitration, and he's estimated to only make $1.9 million next season.
For a team like the Phillies, that's absolutely perfect. They'd be getting some much-needed depth, as seen with a near-catastrophic end of the regular season where they were a game away from missing the playoffs.
Miller notes that bringing in Randy Arozarena or Ian Happ is a long shot, even for the Phillies, so they could easily settle for Call, someone who's spent roughly three years in the National League East.
Call has already played for three teams since making his big-league debut in 2022. The outfielder seemingly can't catch a break, though his longest tenure was from the back half of the 2022 season through the start of the 2025 campaign with the Washington Nationals.
Dodgers have nothing to lose by trading Call
Call surpassed 100 games played with the Dodgers this season, and there wasn't much to love about a 0.2 WAR player in 2026.
After appearing in 88 games this year, Call slashed .233/.349/.307 with a brutal .655 OPS.
There's nothing necessarily wrong with having a slugging percentage lower than an on-base percentage, but it's alarming, to say the least.
Defensively, Call was a negative WAR player this season. He's never had a defensive WAR season above 1.0, so it's not like he's stellar in the outfield, which makes up for his numbers at the plate.
Sometimes a change of scenery is necessary, and while Call has had plenty of that these past few years, a potential trade to the Phillies, where he spends the next three seasons, could do him wonders.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Tarik Skubal is rumored, but is he right for Padres?
item.dc:creator: Matt DeWalt
item.description: Tarik Skubal is the top free agent on the market. On top of that he is a left-handed ace that should be the Opening Day starter for any team in the league not named the Los Angeles Dodgers, Atlanta Braves, Milwaukee Brewers or Pittsburgh Pirates… and even those teams would strongly consider putting Skubal on the mound in Game 1 of the 2027 season. item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal is the top free agent on the market. On top of that he is a left-handed ace that should be the Opening Day starter for any team in the league not named the Los Angeles Dodgers, Atlanta Braves, Milwaukee Brewers or Pittsburgh Pirates… and even those teams would strongly consider putting Skubal on the mound in Game 1 of the 2027 season.
The San Diego Padres have been rumored as a possible landing spot for the lefty in at least a few publications, and the argument for the move is that it would echo the commitment new owners Jose E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones made in press conferences and in their end-of-season letter to season ticket holders. The Padres are in need of pitching this offseason and a move to land Skubal would show the Padres fans and MLB the new owners mean what they say.
The question all San Diego fans have to ask themselves is whether or not Skubal is worth the huge payday he is expected to get. Padres fans know all too well how volatile a pitcher can be. Joe Musgrove missed the majority of two seasons with an elbow injury, Nick Pivetta missed most of the 2026 season with an arm injury and Yu Darvish never touched the mound this season as a result of an arm injury. San Diego ace and likely soon-to-be free agent Michael King missed a chunk of the 2025 season because he "slept wrong" and injured a nerve in his shoulder/neck.
Should the Padres want to spread their money around, whatever amount that might be, they may be better served. King is likely to opt-out of his contract and enter free agency. Reliever Adrian Morejon is a free agent and Ty France who many believe is the 2026 team MVP for the Padres is also a free agent. If Skubal wants $400 million-plus, it may be too rich for one player on a team that needs several players in the rotation and in the starting lineup.
San Diego could have a rotation of Pivetta, if the Padres pick up his option, Musgrove and Randy Vasquez. Others who could make a push for the spot like JP Sears are also on the roster, but unlikely to find what is needed to be in the San Diego rotation to start the season. Musgrove is still an unknown in terms of what he can provide and Darvish COULD return, but he could also just as easily retire depending on how he feels once he gets back to throwing competitive pitches off the mound.
This is an important offseason for the new ownership and as flashy as a Skubal signing might be, it may not be the most beneficial move for the team.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Notes: Blake Snell’s Surprise Retirement Timeline, LA Linked to Teruaki Sato, Shohei Ohtani Two-Way Future
item.dc:creator: Gabe Smallson; Unknown
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers left-handed pitcher Blake Snell provided a surprising answer into his personal timeline regarding when he will retire from the game of baseball. He spoke with the California Post's Dylan Hernandez earlier this month about a feeling of being misunderstood, and how much longer he wants to keep playing. “I just wish people would watch me pitch and then understand the work that I put into being a good pitcher, great pitcher, is a lot more than they’ve ever experienced or give me
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers left-handed pitcher Blake Snell provided a surprising answer into his personal timeline regarding when he will retire from the game of baseball. He spoke with the California Post's Dylan Hernandez earlier this month about a feeling of being misunderstood, and how much longer he wants to keep playing.
“I just wish people would watch me pitch and then understand the work that I put into being a good pitcher, great pitcher, is a lot more than they’ve ever experienced or give me credit for,” Snell said. “Because I watch the game, I understand the hitters. I understand who they are right now in the present. I understand who they are as a hitter.”
In other news, the Dodgers have yet again been linked to a star baseball player from Japan. This time, it's slugging third baseman Teruaki Sato.
The Dodgers were recently listed as a top landing spot for the 27-year-old who is coming off a season hitting .306 with 39 home runs and an OPS of .991.
Sato will require a high price tag for not only his posting fees, but for his soon-to-be former team in Nippon Professional Baseball (the Hanshin Tigers) getting a cut of his first contract in MLB (and potentially beyond). Max Muncy is also currently the third baseman of the two-time defending champions, so if Sato made his way to LA, he could theoretically start in the outfield.
Finally, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman spoke on the pitching future of superstar Shohei Ohtani.
The four-time MVP was shut down from pitching this past July and didn't end up pitching for the rest of the season. Friedman made it clear that since a talent like Ohtani hasn't been seen in over a century, managing his two-way talents to the most effective degree (and to ensure Ohtani is on the mound in the postseason) will be another discussion this offseason.
“This is unprecedented, what he’s doing,” Friedman said. “So obviously for us it’s unprecedented. We don’t have any experience to draw from. We can’t go look at how other situations have played out to try to learn from the good and the bad. We have to all just figure it out together."
Here’s all the latest Dodgers news and stories (click the headline for the full article):
Dodgers Tweets of the Day
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Gabe Smallson is a sportswriter based in Los Angeles with a focus in sports and entertainment content. Gabe has previously worked at Newsweek and Dodgers Nation. He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.

item.title: [dailybulletin.com] Alexander: TV ratings do not prove the World Series’ worth
item.dc:creator: Jim Alexander
item.description: The world according to Jim: • And here we go again: Teams that are not from major media markets will compete for a championship, and the narrative leading up to it involves how sickly the TV ratings will be. Just stop. The worth of a sporting event is not measured by the Nielsens, or by the Q Ratings of the teams or stars involved. item.content:encoded:
The world according to Jim:
• And here we go again: Teams that are not from major media markets will compete for a championship, and the narrative leading up to it involves how sickly the TV ratings will be.
Just stop.
The worth of a sporting event is not measured by the Nielsens, or by the Q Ratings of the teams or stars involved. We seem to lapse into this argument before championship events without serious thought, on behalf of the TV networks and advertisers – and believe me, they don’t need our help or sympathy. …
• The Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays are in the World Series by merit. Each team had the best record in its league, kind of a throwback to the way it used to be. These are smart organizations who have succeeded without large payrolls, creatively and with a heavy accent on player development. …
• You want to know the difference between some small payroll teams and others? Some organizations – and particularly their fan bases – grouse about payroll size and revenue and how the deck is unfairly stacked against them. Others work to overcome the obstacles and succeed anyway; thus, the difference between the Milwaukees, Tampas and Clevelands and the Pittsburghs and Cincinnatis of baseball. …
• And it’s probably not a coincidence that Milwaukee president of baseball operations Matt Arnold spent nine years in the Tampa Bay organization. Much of his time in Tampa Bay (2006-15) overlapped with that of Andrew Friedman, the Rays’ president of baseball operations before becoming the Dodgers’ POBO in 2015. …
• Bottom line: If you don’t watch the World Series, that’s your right to avoid it. (And if you’re a Dodgers fan, it’s perfectly understandable. That sweep still hurts, doesn’t it?) But don’t buy into the national narrative that it’s a lesser attraction because the Dodgers or the Yankees aren’t there. …
• Brewers in six, by the way. And with enough Southern California guys on their roster, what do you think the odds are that one of them will be the World Series MVP? …
• The list includes Brice Turang (Corona Santiago), Jake Bauers (Huntington Beach Marina), Christian Yelich (Westlake), Garrett Mitchell (Orange Lutheran and UCLA), Trevor Megill (Marina), Joey Ortiz (Garden Grove Pacifica) and Jo Jo Romero (Oxnard). Plus two-time NL Manager of the Year Pat Murphy (who coached at Claremont-Mudd-Scripps in the 1980s), and owner Mark Attanasio, an L.A. businessman. And former Dodger Dustin May. …
• The Rays have two players with area roots: Pitcher Tyler Wells (Yucaipa High, Cal State San Bernardino) and Jonny DeLuca (Agoura High), a former Dodgers prospect, plus pitcher Cole Sulser from Ramona High near San Diego. (Two other former Dodgers, Gavin Lux and Ryan Pepiot, are on the Rays’ injured list.) …
• This week’s quiz: It has been 44 years since Milwaukee hosted a World Series, when the Brewers were in the American League and lost to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games. When was the last time Milwaukee won a World Series? (Answer below.) …
• Best line on social media after Tampa Bay’s Junior Caminero’s home run and, shall we say, elongated trip around the bases during the Cleveland series: By the time he was done, he’d become Senior Caminero. …
• If you’re a pitcher and you don’t like the celebration? Pitch better. …
• Quiz answer: It was Oct. 10, 1957, when the then-Milwaukee Braves defeated the Yankees in Game 7, 5-0, with Lew Burdette picking up his third victory of the Series – all three complete games – and Eddie Mathews, Hank Aaron and Frank Torre (Joe’s older brother) driving in the runs in a four-run third inning. The Braves were back the next year and lost to the Yankees, and that was it until the ’82 Brewers. …
• OK, Lakers fans, how much do you miss LeBron James, if at all?
He said this before the Knicks-76ers opener this week: “I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden. One of the best places I’ve ever played … I think it’s the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, ‘Hey, I can’t.’ I couldn’t do it.” …
You think LeBron might have been influenced by the accusations of ring-chasing that Kevin Durant received when he left Oklahoma City to sign with the Golden State Warriors in 2016? If so, you’re probably not that far off. …
• There was already championship talk from overexcited Lakers fans following Game 1. And it sounds like people are, um, delusional in Boston as well, where the Globe’s Dan Shaughnessy wrote: “Hate to break it to you all, but only in Boston are the 2026-27 Celtics considered championship contenders.”
Right now in the Western Conference, the Lakers are fifth best behind Oklahoma City, San Antonio, Denver and Minnesota. This reconstituted roster – Luka Doncic’s team, indisputably – will have plenty of opportunities to change that, but right now it still looks like a tall hill to climb. …
• For some reason, the NBA schedule has 13 conflicts this season when both the Lakers and Clippers are at home. Since the Clippers left downtown L.A. and moved into Intuit Dome in Inglewood, the number has steadily risen, from eight in 2024-25 and 10 in 2025-26.
In 2023-24, the last year the teams shared the arena formerly known as Staples Center, there were six dates when both played at home – and the Clippers got the day game on each occasion. No wonder team personnel were so anxious then for Intuit Dome to open. …
• Footnote: For Wednesday’s openers, the Lakers announced a home crowd of 19,057 and the Clippers announced 17,927. We’ll see if that continues. …
• In case you missed this one, somehow the Knicks’ assistant coaches didn’t receive their championship rings on opening night. Worse yet, other team employees – who customarily receive rings when a team wins a title – learned they would get nothing. And worse still, the email they’d received regarding rings turned out to be an in-house phishing scam, and those who clicked on the link were signed up for a cybertraining session instead.
So I think it’s pretty safe to say Knicks and MSG boss James Dolan has again taken his place at the top of the Bad Owners Club. Readers, who are your nominees for that dishonor?
(I can guess at least one in this region whose name will come up, and he’s a short-timer.)
jalexander@scng.com

item.title: [roundtable.io] How Much Playing Time Does Dodgers' Muncy Have Left?
item.dc:creator: Don Strouble

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy is still playing at an All-Star level, but how much longer can he keep it up?
After narrowly defeating the Toronto Blue Jays in the 2025 World Series, the Dodgers knew they were on the cusp of history. They went and added to their already star-studded roster by acquiring Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz in the offseason before trading for back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal at the MLB Trade Deadline.
But the Dodgers, with the most expensive roster and all the championship pedigree in the world, could not get past the young and hungry Milwaukee Brewers. The Brewers got their revenge on Los Angeles for being swept in the 2025 National League Championship Series by returning the favor on the same stage this season.
The thing about the Dodgers is that they were not the powerhouse we were used to seeing throughout the season, and their struggles and injuries eventually culminated in their demise.
Sure, they won 100 games, but the cracks in an aging roster were evident. Now it begs the question of how much time some of the veteran leaders of this team have left to compete for a title.
One such player who is closer to the end of his career than the beginning is third baseman Max Muncy. Let's evaluate the type of season he had.
Strong and stable
The 36-year-old appeared in 149 regular season games and did not serve a stint on the Injured List. Over the course of those games, Muncy took 488 at-bats and posted a .252 batting average, a .348 on-base percentage, a .490 slugging percentage and an .838 OPS with 29 home runs, the most he has hit since the 2023 season.
For his efforts, Muncy earned his third All-Star selection.
For a little while during the playoffs, it seemed as if Muncy would continue to be a catalyst for his team's offense. In four games against the Atlanta Braves in the National League Division Series, Muncy hit three home runs.
However, like the rest of the Dodgers' offense, Muncy lost steam against the Brewers and went just 2-for-12 at the plate while striking out six times.
It is good that Muncy was healthy in 2026, and Los Angeles certainly needed it. But it does not change the fact that he has passed his prime, and eventually a decision will have to be made by both him and the team about where things stand.
In 2027, Muncy is on the payroll for $10.7 million. In 2028, which will be his age-37 season, the Dodgers have a club option. At that point, serious discussions will need to be had.
Muncy has dealt with injuries in the past but has otherwise stayed relatively healthy throughout his career. If he keeps his production up, there is a chance that he could remain in Dodger blue well into his late 30s.
Whatever the future brings, there is no doubting how important he has been to the franchise.

He also acknowledged his struggles with confidence, expectations and the mental highs and lows that ca
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Alex Vesia has shared an emotional message with fans after a difficult 2026 season, leaving his future with the team uncertain as MLB free agency approaches.
Vesia posted the message on Instagram, reflecting on the personal challenges he faced while thanking his teammates and the Dodgers faithful for their support.
“By far the hardest year of my career,” Vesia wrote. He also acknowledged his struggles with confidence, expectations and the mental highs and lows that came with the season.
The left-handed reliever added that he did not know what the future held but wanted to thank Dodger Nation for showing him so much love over the past six years.
Alex Vesia’s Dodgers Future Remains Uncertain After Strong Season
Vesia’s message comes after the Dodgers’ postseason run ended in a four-game sweep by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series. Los Angeles had hoped to capture a third consecutive World Series title but now faces important offseason decisions.
Despite the difficult year, Vesia remained productive on the mound. He recorded a 2.64 ERA, a 1.07 WHIP and 74 strikeouts across 72 appearances and 58 innings during the regular season, according to his official MLB statistics.
His reliability makes his future an important question for the Dodgers as they evaluate their bullpen for 2027. Vesia has also delivered in October, posting a 1.59 ERA across 31 career postseason appearances.
The 30-year-old has been part of the Dodgers organization since 2021 and helped the club win two World Series championships. Losing a familiar left-handed reliever could leave the front office searching for another dependable option in high-leverage situations.
Vesia’s potential contract will also be worth watching. A Sports Illustrated report cited a Spotrac projection of a two-year, $14.2 million deal, although that figure is an estimate rather than a confirmed offer.
For now, Vesia has not confirmed that he is leaving Los Angeles. His message expresses gratitude while acknowledging an uncertain future, leaving Dodgers fans waiting to see whether he returns for another season.

item.title: [Yardbarker] Andrew Friedman: Dodgers Will ‘Spend A Lot Of Time’ Looking Into Offensive Struggles

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers’ offense was inconsistent throughout the 2026 season, ultimately leading to their downfall in October.
During the postseason, the Dodgers hit just .195/.267/.323 with nine home runs, 25 runs scored, 22 RBI and a 63 wRC+. They struggled with runners in scoring position, did not slug consistently, and didn’t draw walks at their usual rate.
The Dodgers also had similar issues from July through August, and after turning things around in September against weaker opponents, those issues resurfaced at the worst time.
“That’s something we have to wrap our arms around more,” Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said of the offensive struggles. “Obviously, throughout the latter part of the year, it was stuff we were talking about and trying to put our finger on.
“And in a lot of ways, it’s a little bit of a game of whack-a-mole, where it can be one thing for some period of time, and then it’s something else, and then it’s something else. Sometimes it’s noise, and sometimes it’s real. And what’s important for us is to be able to sift out the noise and isolate what’s real and what things we can improve upon.
“We’ll spend a lot of time really focusing on that in the offseason. Hitting is really hard, and pitchers make adjustments. In a lot of ways, a lot of the rules are designed for the run prevention side to have a real advantage. And so, so much of our focus has been: how do we try to combat that on the run creation side?
“I think there are ways that we can get better. And even if we were coming off a consistent great year, our mindset would be, how do we get better? But we’ll definitely spend a lot of time trying to wrap our arms around it and figuring out what is actionable and what things we can improve going forward.”
The Dodgers’ offense was also an issue in the 2025 postseason, but they still won the World Series thanks to their pitching staff and timely home runs.
Given the Dodgers have the oldest position player group in MLB, it begs the question of whether the group is just declining, if they’re tired by the end of the season, or if it’s not related to age at all and it’s just some of the randomness of baseball showing up at inopportune times.
“I don’t know the answer,” Friedman said. “I think it’s a good question. It very well could be we need to be more aggressive on the rest side of things, just proactively.
“But there’s a lot of different theories. You could ask me to argue passionately one path or another, and I could do it. Which gets at that it’s very muddied. There’s not a very clear answer.
“So as we’re kind of wrapping our arms around this, we’re going to try to take what we can and improve going forward. And what that means, we don’t know yet.”
The age of the roster being the primary factor for their struggles is a leading theory among fans and analysts. The Dodgers were bullied by fastballs in October, which relates to their lack of elite bat speed as a unit.
If it’s an age issue, that’s a real concern for the Dodgers, given that it would be unrealistic to get significantly younger in a single offseason. Will Smith, Freddie Freeman, Tommy Edman, Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Teoscar Hernández and Shohei Ohtani are all in their 30s and will be under contract for at least the 2027 season.
Although there is at least some correlation with age, Friedman isn’t ready to say that’s the main reason for their offensive issues.
“I mean, there have been some guys who are older who have finished really strong,” Friedman said. “So I don’t think it’s as easy as to paint it with that broad of a stroke.”
The Dodgers don’t have many paths to upgrade their offense, either. Second base seems to be the primary spot they can upgrade while moving Edman into a utility role.
Josue De Paula also seems destined to be the starting left fielder, which should provide an offensive upgrade over Hernández.
But outside of those potential moves, the Dodgers need Ohtani to be healthy, and they need at least a few of Smith, Betts, Freeman and Muncy to hit like they’re capable of, or else the offense is doomed to struggle again in 2027.
A lot of blame has also been placed on hitting coach Robert Van Scoyoc by fans, which is a natural reaction when the offense struggles. However, Friedman said the Dodgers don’t expect to make any changes to their coaching staff.
Along with Van Scoyoc, Aaron Bates also serves as a hitting coach for the Dodgers. But the reality is hitting coaches also make little impact on a club’s offense, and more of the blame lies on the players and front office.

item.title: [FanSided] The latest Tarik Skubal free agency news should leave baseball fans extremely concerned
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman
item.description: Even with the growing possibility of baseball’s longest work stoppage since the 1994-95 players’ strike, there’s no doubt Los Angeles Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal is about to earn big money. Pitchers like Skubal, who owns two Cy Young Awards and a .247 ERA since the start of 2023, aren’t typically available in their prime. What team wouldn’t want to add a perennial All-Star who will pitch all of next season — assuming there is a 2027 season — at 30 years old? (Outside of the Rockies, Rays, and Guard
item.content:encoded:
Even with the growing possibility of baseball’s longest work stoppage since the 1994-95 players’ strike, there’s no doubt Los Angeles Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal is about to earn big money.
Pitchers like Skubal, who owns two Cy Young Awards and a .247 ERA since the start of 2023, aren’t typically available in their prime. What team wouldn’t want to add a perennial All-Star who will pitch all of next season — assuming there is a 2027 season — at 30 years old? (Outside of the Rockies, Rays, and Guardians, of course.)
Owners want a salary cap and competitive balance, but the majority also want championships. The Athletic’s Andy McCullough spoke with Scott Boras, who represents Skubal, and multiple executives, all of whom agreed Skubal should still cash in; an unnamed executive told McCullough they believe Skubal could sign a 10-year, $400 million contract.
“Last time around, everybody talked about Skuby Doo,” Boras told McCullough. “It’s kind of like, with Skubal now, it’s Skuby Done. He’s proven it at all levels, in different markets, in different environments.”
Not even a lockout will stop ace Tarik Skubal from getting paid
In essence, Major League Baseball and its owners want to cut spending where possible. Look no further than the proposed contract limits, which would cap a free agent’s next deal at five years and $202 million. In that theoretical situation, Skubal also would have had the opportunity to re-sign with the Dodgers for no more than six years and $265 million.
On the one hand, we’re personally against teams handing out 10-year deals because they never age well. The best-case scenario is winning a championship in a player’s prime, as the Dodgers did with Shohei Ohtani (10 years, $700 million) and Yoshinobu Yamamoto (12 years, $325 million) the last two years. Otherwise, you wind up watching the player become dead weight on an inescapable contract, as the Padres are learning with Xander Bogaerts.
But that doesn’t mean we’re against players earning those deals. Why would anyone turn down a contract worth that much money, especially with deferrals? Just because we disagree with a team’s reasoning doesn’t mean Skubal or Ohtani didn’t deserve the opportunity.
Plenty of baseball fans, especially those in smaller markets, might disagree. They want a world where the Brewers, Guardians, and Rays compete for championships every year, and the Dodgers and Yankees aren’t guaranteed a World Series appearance. Never mind that the Yankees have had only one pennant since the start of 2010.
But if annual heavy spenders like the Yankees, Dodgers, and Mets want Skubal, they may make their move ahead of the lockout. We imagine it all depends on how quickly the dominant lefty wants to sign, though we’d personally advise him to do so ASAP.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers Make Tarik Skubal Interest Clear Ahead of Free Agency
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Tarik Skubal will reach free agency the day after the World Series, and the incumbent team will be among the first to call. The Dodgers acquired Skubal in August, right at the trade deadline, hoping he would be the final piece to a three-peat, but a struggling offense kept them from reaching that goal. Despite still reeling from the disappointment, Dodgers President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman was not shy about celebrating how well Skubal assimilat
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Tarik Skubal will reach free agency the day after the World Series, and the incumbent team will be among the first to call.
The Dodgers acquired Skubal in August, right at the trade deadline, hoping he would be the final piece to a three-peat, but a struggling offense kept them from reaching that goal.
Despite still reeling from the disappointment, Dodgers President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman was not shy about celebrating how well Skubal assimilated into the Dodgers and their mission.
“It’s not easy for a guy to get traded in the middle of a season to come to a new city, new clubhouse,” Friedman said to Dodgers Nation and the media. “You have set routines, and you have to make those adjustments.
“The way he was able to seamlessly transition, not just in terms of on the field, but in the clubhouse, I can’t say enough good things about the impact that he made in such a short period of time. We have a tremendous amount of respect for him on and off the field.”
The lefty posted a 2.45 ERA in two postseason starts for the Dodgers, down from 2.61 in his regular-season starts.
However, he may have made his last start with the Dodgers, now that superagent Scott Boras controls his future.
Friedman clearly understands what lies ahead, and while he made no promises, he made it clear he’ll talk with Boras.
“He’s put himself in this position to go out and be a free agent. And for us, it’s (to) continue to talk to Scott (Boras),” Friedman told the media, including Dodgers Nation.
“But he and his family have to make a choice over where they want to spend the next X number of years, and obviously we wish him nothing but the best.”
The Dodgers will be in the market for Skubal, and they have the financial means to stay in it for a while, possibly even to the end, and keep their super rotation together.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Shohei Ohtani Sends Direct Message to Dodgers Fans After NLCS Elimination
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are looking ahead to 2027 after their 2026 season ended abruptly. The Dodgers' season ended a week ago after the Milwaukee Brewers swept them. The Brewers returned the favor from last year's National League Championship Series and will now look to win their first-ever World Series title. Nevertheless, the page has turned to the 2027 season for the Dodgers, and considering how Shohei Ohtani played down the stretch, that may be for the better. The 32-year-old two-way supers
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are looking ahead to 2027 after their 2026 season ended abruptly.
The Dodgers' season ended a week ago after the Milwaukee Brewers swept them. The Brewers returned the favor from last year's National League Championship Series and will now look to win their first-ever World Series title.
Nevertheless, the page has turned to the 2027 season for the Dodgers, and considering how Shohei Ohtani played down the stretch, that may be for the better.
The 32-year-old two-way superstar was a shell of himself from mid-August on, as he struggled to do anything right and did more harm than good for the Dodgers. He was clearly not himself.
With the season ending, Ohtani took to Instagram and sent a message to fans, simply saying, "Thank you."
Dodgers Saw the Best of Shohei Ohtani Before His Health Became a Problem
The first half of the season was one to behold for Ohtani.
Ohtani showed his true two-way prowess, as he was elite on both sides of the ball. He pitched in 14 games in the first half of the season on the mound and was elite as he's ever been.
The four-time MVP posted a 1.79 ERA, 95 strikeouts and allowed a .180 batting average to opposing hitters. Ohtani went 8-2 and pitched 85.2 innings.
Ultimately, Ohtani was shut down from pitching after the All-Star break. He made his last start on his 32nd birthday on July 3.
As for the hitting side, Ohtani began to struggle mightily in mid-August as injuries started to flare up.
Ohtani dealt with a combination of left knee irritation and right biceps tightness. His knee injury flared up in late June, and his right biceps tightness popped up multiple times throughout the year.
Ohtani's offensive decline continued through October. He never had enough time to return to his usual form, as he played through those injuries before eventually landing on the injured list in September.
The Dodgers hoped those two weeks off would help Ohtani get back on track, but that proved to be more wishful thinking. He never looked quite the same, and it was clear his struggles hurt the Dodgers in the long run.
Dodgers Expect Shohei Ohtani to Avoid Offseason Surgery
As for 2027, the Dodgers expect Ohtani to return to his two-way status. On top of that, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Wednesday that Ohtani will not require offseason surgery on his left knee or right biceps.
The belief is that Ohtani will heal with rest and be at 100% by the time spring training rolls around.

Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

item.title: [roundtable.io] Dodgers Expect Entire Coaching Staff Back in 2027
item.dc:creator: Anthony Arroyo
item.description: Andrew Friedman expects the Los Angeles Dodgers' coaching staff to return for the 2027 season. The Los Angeles Dodgers are not anticipating major changes to their coaching staff this offseason, with president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman expecting the entire group to return for the 2027 season. Friedman discussed the organization's plans during his end-of-season press conference, indicating that the Dodgers expect to maintain their existing coaching structure as they prepare for anothe
item.content:encoded:
Andrew Friedman expects the Los Angeles Dodgers' coaching staff to return for the 2027 season.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are not anticipating major changes to their coaching staff this offseason, with president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman expecting the entire group to return for the 2027 season.
Friedman discussed the organization's plans during his end-of-season press conference, indicating that the Dodgers expect to maintain their existing coaching structure as they prepare for another championship pursuit.
If the staff returns as anticipated, manager Dave Roberts will enter his 12th season leading Los Angeles with the same coaching group in place.
The Dodgers have built sustained success under Roberts, and retaining the current staff would allow the organization to move into the offseason without an expected overhaul of its coaching personnel.
While Friedman's comments provide an early indication of the club's plans, the expectation of a full return is not necessarily an official confirmation of every coach's status for next season.
Danny Lehmann has drawn managerial interest
Lehmann has previously been considered a potential managerial candidate, putting him among the coaches who could eventually receive opportunities to lead another organization.
His future remains worth monitoring as teams continue evaluating candidates for leadership positions. For the Dodgers, though, the expectation remains that their existing coaching staff will return for 2027.
Maintaining Lehmann and the rest of the group would give Roberts continuity in the dugout as the team begins preparing for the upcoming season.
The Dodgers have relied on an established coaching structure throughout Roberts' tenure, and keeping that group together would allow the organization to concentrate on other offseason priorities rather than making significant changes to its staff.
Dodgers look to maintain stability heading into 2027
Although managerial openings elsewhere could create opportunities for members of the Dodgers' organization, there is currently no public indication that Lehmann is involved in the Houston or Seattle searches.
For now, Friedman's comments suggest that Los Angeles expects to retain its existing coaching group as Roberts prepares for another season.
The Dodgers will have additional offseason decisions to make before the 2027 campaign begins, but the coaching staff does not appear to be an area where the organization anticipates significant change.
If the expectation holds, Roberts and his staff will return together as Los Angeles begins its next attempt to compete for another World Series championship.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dalton Rushing surgery bomb delays possibility of a Dodgers trade but doesn't erase it
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins
item.description: On Wednesday, the Los Angeles Dodgers revealed Dalton Rushing underwent an internal brace procedure on his elbow, sidelining him from catching for approximately nine months. Andrew Friedman said at his postmortem press conference that Rushing could start swinging a bat sooner, but he won't be behind the dish until well into the 2027 season. Luckily, the Dodgers got their scrambling for catching depth out of the way in-season by reacquiring Hunter Feduccia from the Tampa Bay Rays at the trade dea
item.content:encoded:
On Wednesday, the Los Angeles Dodgers revealed Dalton Rushing underwent an internal brace procedure on his elbow, sidelining him from catching for approximately nine months. Andrew Friedman said at his postmortem press conference that Rushing could start swinging a bat sooner, but he won't be behind the dish until well into the 2027 season.
Luckily, the Dodgers got their scrambling for catching depth out of the way in-season by reacquiring Hunter Feduccia from the Tampa Bay Rays at the trade deadline. Although he hit under .200, the Dodgers still preferred him on both of their postseason rosters over Rushing, who was on the IL with elbow inflammation throughout September.
This kills basically any idea that the Dodgers might finally trade Rushing this offseason, unless they're willing to sell very low. But it's still a possibility for the more distant future.
Feduccia fits into the mold of a traditional backup catcher much more neatly than Rushing, who the Dodgers could still fetch a decent return for in a trade when he's healthy.
Of course, the Dodgers would much rather make their roster that much more formidable by having a backup catcher who would be a starter on any other team, but if Feduccia can use Rushing's absence as an opportunity to prove that his bat won't represent a total black hole in the lineup, the Dodgers could be more inclined to let go of Rushing next offseason.
Dodgers catcher Dalton Rushing will be sidelined for nine months
A nine-month recovery timeline would have Rushing back on defense by the end of July — only if all goes according to plan. Even if he's healthy enough to swing a bat before then, opportunities as a pinch-hitter or DH on Shohei Ohtani's off-days will be scarce. The Dodgers could use the rest of the regular season to get Rushing back into a groove behind Will Smith and see if it drives his trade value back up to a point where they're willing to deal him.
The Dodgers would never admit to it outright, but it seems that they've fallen out of love with Rushing. Although concerns about his elbow probably factored into their decision to carry Josue De Paula into the postseason instead, Rushing was very much in that conversation and didn't make the cut.
They could still get a healthy return back for him, too, despite character concerns and injuries. He's too young and controllable, and has too good a pedigree for the Dodgers to give him away for a song.

item.description: Miguel Rojas isn’t done with baseball. But Rojas will represent his home country one last time to play in the Venezuelan Professional Baseball League for the Tiburones de La Guaira club. The Dodgers World Series hero will participate in special games for the team on Nov. 14 and 15 at LoanDepot Park in Miami. Turns out Game 4 of the NLCS
item.content:encoded:
Miguel Rojas isn’t done with baseball.
The veteran infielder announced his retirement from Major League Baseball after the Dodgers were swept in the National League Championship Series by the Brewers. But Rojas will represent his home country one last time to play in the Venezuelan Professional Baseball League for the Tiburones de La Guaira club.
The Dodgers World Series hero will participate in special games for the team on Nov. 14 and 15 at LoanDepot Park in Miami.
Turns out Game 4 of the NLCS won’t be Rojas’ final game of his career.
“One last time on the field. One last time representing Venezuela,” Rojas said in an Instagram caption.
Rojas previously expressed disappointment with the World Baseball Classic after he was not able to participate in the spring tournament due to issues obtaining insurance on his MLB contract. The 37-year-old has never participated in a WBC and the 2026 tournament was his last chance before he retired.
“I didn’t know that my chance to go represent my country for the first and only time, probably as a player, was gonna get blocked because of an insurance problem,” Rojas said. “Even though we know we have to be ready for the season and we have to play and be healthy for our contract, at the end of the day, we didn’t know all those restrictions were gonna be in place the way they are right now.”
Rojas wasn’t able to represent Venezuela in the WBC, but he will play one last time for his home country next month.

item.content:encoded:
ファナティクス・ジャパンは10月20日、MLB公式オンラインショップ「MLB SHOP」のポップストアを、10月24日（土）から東急プラザ表参道「オモカド」に期間限定でオープンすると発表した。
同ストアでは、MLBで活躍する大谷翔平や山本由伸（ともにロサンゼルス・ドジャース）、村上宗隆（シカゴ・ホワイトソックス）らのユニフォームやネーム＆ナンバーTシャツを販売。
今季、目覚ましい活躍を見せたピート・クロウ＝アームストロング（シカゴ・カブス）やジェイコブ・ミジオロウスキー（ミルウォーキー・ブルワーズ）などのアイテムも取り扱う。
さらに、ポストシーズン限定商品や人気の「Under Wraps」シリーズなど、300点以上の商品を取りそろえる。
MLBの“頂上決戦”を彩る記念グッズも注目だ。
同社はMLB公式オンラインショップにて、ミルウォーキー・ブルワーズとタンパベイ・レイズのワールドシリーズ進出記念グッズの販売を開始！
ワールドシリーズ進出記念Tシャツやリーグ優勝記念Tシャツ、両チームの対戦を記念したマッチアップTシャツなどを展開するほか、ブルワーズのミジオロウスキーやレイズのジュニオール・カミネロらの関連商品も販売している。
ファナティクスは、スポーツ関連の公式グッズを企画・製造・販売する世界最大級のデジタルスポーツプラットフォーム企業。
今回のポップストアでは、スター選手のアイテムからポストシーズンの記念商品まで、MLBファンが幅広いグッズを実際に手に取って楽しめる機会となりそうだ。

試合だけでなくユニフォーム、スパイク、スタジアム、ファン・サポーター、カルチャー、ビジネス、テクノロジーなどなど、サッカーの様々な面白さを発信します。現場好き。週末フットボーラー。

item.title: [Motor City Bengals] Scott Boras quote hints Tigers' Tarik Skubal purgatory could end sooner than later
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins
item.description: Tarik Skubal is (almost) officially a free agent, and he's keeping his cards close to his chest. After the Dodgers' exit from the postseason, he declined to comment on his thoughts about going back to LA. Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said that they'll continue having conversations with Skubal and Scott Boras, but it's ultimately up to Skubal to make the best decision for himself and his family. This is just the done thing when a player becomes a free agent. The odds t
item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal is (almost) officially a free agent, and he's keeping his cards close to his chest. After the Dodgers' exit from the postseason, he declined to comment on his thoughts about going back to LA. Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said that they'll continue having conversations with Skubal and Scott Boras, but it's ultimately up to Skubal to make the best decision for himself and his family.
This is just the done thing when a player becomes a free agent. The odds that he goes back to to LA are massive, even as a slate of other teams may be preparing to make their own pitches.
The Tigers have been included on almost every "teams to watch" list when it comes to the Skubal sweepstakes, but fans know better than to get our hopes up about that. With the amount of money coming off the payroll this offseason, it might not be impossible, but the odds are incredibly slim.
There's an elephant in the room, of course: baseball is barreling toward a lockout. The challenge for this crop of free agents will be signing before the CBA expires on Dec. 1 without sacrificing their own value in the rush.
If anyone is equipped to do that for Skubal, it's Boras. He said broadly, "For many teams, I can make an argument it's clearly best for them to sign players currently, before the (new) CBA, than it is after..."
Sounds like we won't have to wait too long to find out where Skubal will end up.
Scott Boras hints it won't take long for Tarik Skubal to sign a new contract ahead of an MLB lockout
Although a salary cap almost certainly isn't going to fly in any world, as much as the owners and a large contingent of baseball fans want it to, players who wait until the smoke clears to sign are at a distinct disadvantage. There will be little runway for those without new homes to negotiate and sign before the start of what figures to be an abbreviated season.
It's hard to see how players might have more leverage before and after a lockout, but if anyone can make the argument, it's Boras. The teams that want Skubal are going to have to come out swinging immediately, and it's hard to envision a world in which the Tigers are one of them.
At least we probably won't be kept in suspense for very long. Anyone who's seriously interested in Skubal is going to have to come out swinging and start the bidding high. The Tigers aren't in a position to compete with the likes of the Dodgers are Mets, nor have they given any indication that they want to be.

item.title: [New York Post] Why Dodgers remain coy on potential Tarik Skubal re-signing: ‘Wish him nothing but the best’
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: When it comes to top free agents, the Dodgers rarely tip their hand. At the outset of Tarik Skubal’s free agency this offseason, that remained the case once again. During an end-of-season press conference on Wednesday, less than a week removed from the team’s sweep at the hands of the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman carefully sidestepped a question about Skubal, saying a lot of words that offered no substantive indica
item.content:encoded:
When it comes to top free agents, the Dodgers rarely tip their hand.
At the outset of Tarik Skubal’s free agency this offseason, that remained the case once again.
During an end-of-season press conference on Wednesday, less than a week removed from the team’s sweep at the hands of the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman carefully sidestepped a question about Skubal, saying a lot of words that offered no substantive indication of the club’s urgency level to potentially re-sign him.
Friedman started by praising the two-time Cy Young Award-winning left-hander, whom the Dodgers acquired in a blockbuster trade deadline deal with the Detroit Tigers in August.
“It’s not easy for a guy to get traded in the middle of a season to come to a new city, new clubhouse,” Friedman said. “You have set routines, and you have to make those adjustments.”
The longtime top executive then complimented the way Skubal acclimated to his new surroundings, and the impact he made even in a year the Dodgers fell short of a World Series three-peat.
“The way he was able to seamlessly transition, not just in terms of on the field, but in the clubhouse, I can’t say enough good things about the impact that he made in such a short period of time,” Friedman said. “We have a tremendous amount of respect for him on and off the field.”
What Friedman didn’t do, however, was say that the Dodgers would be all-in on Skubal this winter, or that they would do whatever it takes to lock him up in a free agency process that is expected to end with the soon-to-be 30-year-old breaking Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s record guarantee of $325 million for a pitcher.
That wasn’t unexpected, of course.
Even in the run-up to this year’s deadline, the Dodgers publicly downplayed how aggressive they would be for the superstar ace.
Still, by playing it coy Wednesday, Friedman allowed a vacuum of speculation to develop about exactly where the Dodgers will stand in the Skubal sweepstakes.
“He’s put himself in this position to go out and be a free agent,” Friedman said, acknowledging only that the club will have conversations with Skubal’s agent, Scott Boras, going into the winter. “He and his family have to make a choice over where they want to spend the next X number of years, and obviously we wish him nothing but the best.”
Granted, it’s still extremely early in the offseason. And as the Dodgers have shown the last couple winters, they can never be counted out for a top free-agent target (remember when they were supposedly not going to break the bank for Kyle Tucker?).
At this point, however, there have been questions from some corners of the industry about the Dodgers’ willingness to give Skubal the lengthy, lucrative contract he will be seeking.
The team already has ample future financial commitments tied up to Yamamoto, Shohei Ohtani, Mookie Betts and others. Even without Skubal, they will have one of the majors’ best rotations next year, assuming Justin Wrobleski and Roki Sasaki continue to develop, and Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow can avoid the injury problems that have plagued them the past few years.
Much could depend on the league’s looming CBA negotiations, which might result in a salary cap –– or some other drastic changes to the sport’s economic structure –– following a lockout all but certain to commence on Dec. 1.
It’s unclear if Skubal will try to sign a new contract before then; with the Mets, Cubs, Angels and Yankees all seen as potential suitors, among others.
It’s also unclear how the Dodgers’ approach to long-term payroll might change depending on what the new CBA entails.
That’s why, for now, the club will remain the ultimate wild card in his free-agency process.
They have the resources to swing a record-breaking deal if they want. They have a track record of getting aggressive for players they feel swing their World Series chances. But if they are planning an all-out press to re-sign Skubal, they aren’t tipping their hand yet.
“We’re still wrapping our arms around our off-season plan and strategy and timing of things,” Friedman said.
His cards, once again, were staying glued to his chest.

item.title: [Bolavip US] Dodgers GM reaffirms commitment to Kyle Tucker, Edwin Diaz heading into next season
item.dc:creator: Santiago Tovar
item.description: Two of the Los Angeles Dodgers’ premier additions last offseason, Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz, endured turbulent 2026 regular seasons. Despite those struggles, General Manager Brandon Gomes expressed strong confidence in both players looking ahead to 2027. “So much of that was betting on the true talent of those guys and while the regular season did not go the way anyone expected, their contributions in the postseason were massive,” Gomes said. “Really looking forward to next year for those guys.
item.content:encoded:
Two of the Los Angeles Dodgers’ premier additions last offseason, Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz, endured turbulent 2026 regular seasons. Despite those struggles, General Manager Brandon Gomes expressed strong confidence in both players looking ahead to 2027.
“So much of that was betting on the true talent of those guys and while the regular season did not go the way anyone expected, their contributions in the postseason were massive,” Gomes said. “Really looking forward to next year for those guys.”
With both players anchored in Los Angeles—alongside ace Tarik Skubal, whose long-term future remains a key storyline—the Dodgers aim to rebound in 2027 and recapture World Series glory following their back-to-back titles in 2024 and 2025.
Another major focal point in Los Angeles was the late-season performance of Shohei Ohtani. The Japanese superstar struggled to find his dominant form in October after racing back from an injury sustained in the closing weeks of the regular season.
Edwin Diaz #3 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts.
Diaz and Tucker’s performances in the 2026 MLB season
Across 21 regular-season appearances, Diaz struggled to an inflated 8.68 ERA and a 1.98 WHIP over 18.2 innings, battling command issues and giving up crucial late-game hits. While he managed to secure seven saves, he frequently pitched through traffic on the basepaths. However, the fiery reliever found redemption in October, delivering multiple scoreless relief outings to stabilize the back end of the bullpen when the Dodgers needed it most.
For Tucker, the 2026 campaign was marked by flashes of production bookending a lengthy middle-of-the-season injury absence. Tucker finished his abbreviated regular season hitting .239 with 70 hits, seven home runs, and 44 RBIs across 80 games.
His refined plate discipline and smooth left-handed swing remained vital assets, allowing him to maintain a solid on-base percentage and deliver timely hits with runners in scoring position.
Key takeaways
- Brandon Gomes praised Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz’s postseason contributions despite regular-season struggles.
- Edwin Diaz recorded a 8.68 ERA and a 1.98 WHIP across 21 regular-season appearances.
- Kyle Tucker posted a .239 batting average with 7 home runs and 44 RBIs.
