item.content:encoded:
During Spring Training, Hyeseong Kim was in the running to be the Los Angeles Dodgers’ starting second baseman while Tommy Edman was out. Instead, the job went to Alex Freeland.
Kim opened the year in Triple-A and didn’t spend much time with the Dodgers. He appeared in just 43 games and didn’t produce much when given the opportunity.
Kim hit just .259/.323/.328 with one home run, 16 runs scored, 11 RBI, five stolen bases and an 83 wRC+. In the Minors, he wasn’t much better either, slashing .262/.330/.345 with a 77 wRC+ in the hitter-friendly Pacific Coast League.
After a poor season, Kim shared a message on Instagram apologizing for his struggles on the field, thanking fans and the Dodgers for their support, and committing to be better in 2027.
Hello, this is Hyeseong Kim!
Looking back on this season, I’m sorry I couldn’t show you better performances, and I was deeply disappointed in myself as well. Still, I sincerely thank everyone who supported me through it all.
I love the Dodgers, and I have never once been disappointed in this team. It was my choice, and I haven’t regretted it for a single moment. My only disappointment was in myself. I have nothing but gratitude for the team and all the Dodgers fans!
Next year, I will strive to become a better person and a better baseball player. Thank you!😊👍
Kim enters an important year for both his future with the Dodgers and potentially his MLB career. The 2027 season is the final year of his three-year, $12.5 million contract before the Dodgers have club options in 2028 and 2029.
The Dodgers would certainly move on with another poor season from Kim, and there’s no guarantee he even makes it through the offseason in the organization.
If he hits like he did in 2026, other organizations may also just view him as just Minor League depth, putting a lot of pressure on him heading into the new season.
However, the Dodgers have open spots on their bench with Miguel Rojas retiring and Kiké Hernández reaching free agency with the club likely to move on. The additional roster spots could bode well for Kim’s chances of sticking around.
The Dodgers also need to get younger, and Kim will be just 28 years old entering the 2027 season. In addition, he provides a speed element to the roster that no one else does.
Kim’s ability to play the middle infield could also help his chances of sticking around with the Dodgers losing two infielders who served bench roles, but he would also compete with Freeland once again for that role.
But even with his speed and defensive ability, Kim still needs to hit to be on a Major League roster, and his production from 2026 won’t cut it.
In 2025, Kim was still a below-league-average hitter, but he had the benefit of the doubt after moving from South Korea to the United States and facing tougher competition. Now, Kim doesn’t have any excuses, and it’ll be up to him to prove himself as a Major Leaguer.
Dodgers working with Hyeseong Kim’s swing mechanics
Since signing Kim, the Dodgers have been working on his swing mechanics to develop more consistency and pop. That has been ongoing for two seasons now, and they believed his mechanics were the cause of some of his 2026 struggles.
An offseason of working on his swing and resetting could prove beneficial, but with the impending lockout, Kim will not be able to work with Dodgers hitting coaches once it begins, adding another obstacle.
If you love our reporting, choose DodgerBlue.com as a preferred source on Google.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Blake Snell wastes no time putting together a Dodgers recruiting pitch to Tarik Skubal
item.dc:creator: Colin Keane

Snell provided multiple quotes on Skubal, and each soundbite communicated his clear desire for the two-time Cy Young award-winner to stay in LA. “I would love nothing more than for him to be back," Snell said. “The goal is to win a World Series, and we weren’t able to do that ... so now that it’s over, don’t leave," Snell added about Skubal. item.content:encoded:
In the difficult moments following the Los Angeles Dodgers' elimination last week, Blake Snell didn't hesitate to share his thoughts on Tarik Skubal. Snell provided multiple quotes on Skubal, and each soundbite communicated his clear desire for the two-time Cy Young award-winner to stay in LA.
“I would love nothing more than for him to be back," Snell said. “The goal is to win a World Series, and we weren’t able to do that ... so now that it’s over, don’t leave," Snell added about Skubal.
But Snell didn't stop at locker room chatter. He's now taken to social media in his attempts to keep Skubal around.
Blake Snell keeps publicly expressing his desire to keep Tarik Skubal on the Dodgers
Snell's efforts are light-hearted, though earnest, but it'll take something far more serious (in the form of hundreds of millions of dollars) for the Dodgers to ensure that the No. 1 free agent on the market returns to Los Angeles in 2027.
There's no doubt that Skubal fit into LA's clubhouse seamlessly in 2026. It also makes a ton of sense that Skubal and Snell get along, seeing as they are both Cy Young award-winning lefties who share an agent in Scott Boras.
Surely, Skubal can see himself happily returning to the Dodgers next season and moving forward with the organization. Nonetheless, he knows it wouldn't be wise to share his personal thoughts on his free agency, which is exactly why he's been mostly mum on the topic since the season ended. The lefty didn't get into his future at all following LA's elimination, even when prompted on multiple occasions by reporters.
The Dodgers will face multiple challenges when it comes to signing Tarik Skubal to a new deal
Beyond the looming lockout possibility and the uncertainty about the next collective bargaining agreement, the Dodgers will face sturdy competition for Skubal's services, most likely in the form of New York Mets owner Steve Cohen's deep pockets.
How will Andrew Friedman and the rest of LA's front office approach the Skubal situation? Will having fallen short of a three-peat add extra motivation to Friedman's mindset about getting a deal done for Skubal, or might he go in a different direction? Given how Friedman's operated in recent years, one assumes he'll go all-in on Skubal and do what he can to out-joust Cohen.
It's hard to imagine the Dodgers not playing a crucial role in the upcoming Skubal sweepstakes. It's also scary from a baseball perspective to think about how much more effective Skubal might be on the Dodgers next season once he's more comfortable with his new organization.
Per usual, the National League is hoping that the Dodgers don't get their guy. That's all good and fair, but Friedman probably has other plans. In other words, Snell's wishes have a good chance of coming true this winter.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Even in Defeat, the Dodgers Remain Must-See TV
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers gave their fans a painful October ending. They also gave baseball a television audience it hadn’t seen at this stage of the postseason in more than a decade. According to FOX Sports figures reported by Sports Illustrated, the Dodgers-Brewers NLCS averaged more than 7.53 million viewers across FOX and FS1. That was the highest average for a League Championship Series on any network since 2015, and a 77 percent increase over the 2025 ALCS. That comparison is to last y
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers gave their fans a painful October ending. They also gave baseball a television audience it hadn’t seen at this stage of the postseason in more than a decade.
According to FOX Sports figures reported by Sports Illustrated, the Dodgers-Brewers NLCS averaged more than 7.53 million viewers across FOX and FS1. That was the highest average for a League Championship Series on any network since 2015, and a 77 percent increase over the 2025 ALCS. That comparison is to last year’s American League series, rather than the previous Dodgers-Brewers NLCS.
For Dodgers fans, those numbers offer little comfort after a sweep. They do, however, support something that gets lost amid all the complaints about this team: the Dodgers make people care enough to watch.
A Team People Have Strong Feelings About
Some viewers wanted to see the Dodgers take another step toward a third straight championship. Others surely wanted to see Milwaukee end that chase. The ratings don’t tell us how many belonged to either camp, but both kinds of interest make for compelling television.
That is part of the Dodgers’ drawing power. Shohei Ohtani stepping into the box brings the chance of something worth seeing. Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman bring their own followings. Put those players in an October game with a championship run at stake, and there are plenty of reasons to keep the television on.
The spending debate adds another layer. Fans who resent the Dodgers still have a reason to follow them, especially when an opponent has them on the ropes. Rooting against a team can hold an audience’s attention as firmly as rooting for one.
Milwaukee Earned Its Share of the Spotlight
The Brewers deserve credit for the audience, too. These were their games and their pennant to win, and they gave viewers a team worth watching.
A series audience belongs to both clubs. These figures alone cannot tell us how much of the interest came from Milwaukee’s appeal, the Dodgers’ star power or the chance to watch the defending champions fall. The matchup brought all of those stories together.
From a Dodgers perspective, though, the broader point holds. Los Angeles remains one of baseball’s biggest attractions, with enough talent, history and public interest to make its postseason games feel like events.
We would gladly trade the television numbers for another week of Dodgers baseball. But even as their season came to an end, people were watching. The Dodgers lost the series. Their place among the sport’s top draws looks secure.
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.title: [MLB.com] What Dodgers can learn from Ohtani's injury-plagued 2026
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- As lingering injuries began to take their toll on Shohei Ohtani during the regular season, the Dodgers frequently returned to the same refrain: What mattered most was him feeling the best he could in October. He broke out with his first homer in nearly two months in Game 4 of the NL Champions
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- As lingering injuries began to take their toll on Shohei Ohtani during the regular season, the Dodgers frequently returned to the same refrain: What mattered most was him feeling the best he could in October.
Coming off extended rest from his time on the IL and the bye during the Wild Card round, Ohtani neither performed nor looked like he was feeling as good as he could during the postseason run. He broke out with his first homer in nearly two months in Game 4 of the NL Championship Series, but it was too little, too late as the Dodgers' season came to an abrupt end in a sweep at the hands of the Brewers last Thursday.
Ohtani was one of several L.A. hitters going through an ill-timed slump, but his ongoing right biceps and left knee injuries could have been managed better by the Dodgers, and perhaps himself. Learning from what went wrong this year will be critical as Ohtani plans to return to a full two-way role for the 2027 season.
"I haven't been able to really come to grip in terms of what I've learned overall this season," Ohtani said through interpreter Will Ireton following the Dodgers' elimination. "It's something that I'm going to kind of go back to the drawing board in terms of treatment, training program, and see what I can come up with for next season."
There is no blueprint for handling a two-way player, so the Dodgers have had to rely heavily on conversations with Ohtani to manage his workload and his health. But as is common with star players, the team had to take Ohtani's self-assessment with a grain of salt.
"The communication back and forth has been awesome," president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said after Ohtani came off the IL. "The fully sharing exactly how he's feeling, maybe not as awesome."
The Dodgers were proactive with Ohtani's health at times, separating his pitching and hitting workloads or giving him a full day off after his starts on the mound. But they did not skip his pitching starts or place him on the IL until it became abundantly clear that he was physically compromised.
Here's a timeline of some of the key injury-related events from Ohtani's 2026 season, including some of the inflection points where the Dodgers could have acted differently:
June 11: Ohtani exits with left knee inflammation
Ohtani's knee injury first became public knowledge the night after a start on the mound in Pittsburgh. The Dodgers initially believed he aggravated his knee on a stolen-base attempt, but Ohtani later said that something awry with his pitching mechanics may have been the cause.
July 3: Ohtani exits with right biceps tightness
Ohtani made a quality start on the mound, but he was later pinch-hit for due to biceps discomfort that he said had also bothered him "a couple months ago." This was Ohtani's final pitching start of the season. After recording a 0.74 ERA through his first 10 starts, he recorded a 4.38 ERA through his last four starts, which all came while he was dealing with the knee injury.
July 19: Ohtani out of rotation indefinitely
Citing his ongoing knee irritation, the Dodgers scratched Ohtani from his scheduled final first-half start on July 10. They were hopeful that he would make his first start after the All-Star break after receiving a lubricating Orthovisc injection, but they changed their plans after he continued to experience knee discomfort.
July 25: Ohtani shut down from throwing
Three days after Ohtani threw a full bullpen session in Philadelphia -- which seemed to take some Dodgers personnel by surprise -- he was indefinitely shut down from throwing due to regression with his knee.
Aug. 8: Ohtani starts throwing progression
After going more than two weeks without throwing, Ohtani started playing catch to begin a ramp up to get back on the mound. He seemed to be making linear progress, advancing to a bullpen session on Aug. 14 and facing hitters on Aug. 23. But this is when his production as a hitter began to drop off, as he hit .205 with a .666 OPS through his final 29 regular-season games beginning on Aug. 8.
Aug. 29: Ohtani's return to mound pushed back
Sept. 3: Ohtani misses the first of four straight games
After a game where Ohtani looked particularly physically compromised at the plate, the Dodgers decided to rest him indefinitely. They went back and forth about whether putting him on the IL made sense, with general manager Brandon Gomes saying it "hasn't even been something that we've discussed" on Sept. 3. When Ohtani returned to the lineup on Sept. 7, he said he would focus exclusively on hitting for the rest of the season, the first definitive comments from him or the team on whether he would pitch again in 2026.
Sept. 11: Ohtani placed on 15-day IL
After missing six of the Dodgers' previous seven games, Ohtani was placed on the IL. Manager Dave Roberts admitted that, with the benefit of hindsight, he would have preferred to have put him on the IL earlier. Ohtani was sidelined for a minimum-length stint and returned for the final five games of the regular season.
Oct. 13: Dodgers discuss sitting Ohtani in NLCS Game 3
Ohtani went 3-for-20 with no extra-base hits through his first six postseason games, leading the top Dodgers brass to have a conversation with Ohtani about whether he should play in NLCS Game 3. Ohtani convinced them that he felt good enough to play -- and indeed, looked better in Games 3 and 4. But his brief turnaround did not change things for the Dodgers.
If anything could have changed how the season ended for Ohtani, it may have been more proactivity back when his injury saga began.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers must decide whether to offer their breakout star, Andy Pages, a new contract.
Andy Pages’ amazing 2026 season
Pages made the 2026 All-Star team after a stellar regular season, starting extremely hot and leading the team in hitting.
As the season progressed, Pages’ production cooled but stabilized at an above-average level, while his defense remained stellar all year and earned him a Gold Glove nomination.
He finished the season slashing .274/.343/.468, with a 4.5 fWAR, 15 offensive rating points above average, and 10.3 defensive rating points above average.
It was his best season by far, and his overall production was more consistent than in 2025.
In the postseason, Pages took his biggest strides. He went 7-for-26 with two walks and four RBIs, becoming one of the few players to drive in runners with men on base.
His pitch recognition, plate discipline, and vision, all of which improved during the regular season, shone in the postseason.
Pages shook off the growing perception that he would struggle in October, and now few major questions remain when analyzing the outfielder.
As he enters arbitration for the first time, the Dodgers need to decide whether to give Pages an extension.
Why the Dodgers will consider an extension
At only 25, Pages is one of the youngest players on an admittedly old team, and his defense is a major asset.
His center field play can help offset some corner weaknesses, given his range and speed.
As such a well-rounded player, Pages’ arbitration figure will keep rising, and since he has unlocked Super Two arbitration, he gets four years rather than the standard three.
In 2027 alone, MLB Trade Rumors projects Pages to earn $4.9 million.
An offseason extension could buy him out for those four years, plus some of his free-agent years, keeping him locked in for the foreseeable future.
The Dodgers did something similar with Will Smith, extending him during his second arbitration year to a 10-year, $140 million deal.
In the process, they bought out two years of arbitration and eight years of free agency.
Pages, with three years of arbitration left and entering free agency in his physical prime at 29, will cost a pretty penny as an outfielder with good contact skills and outfield defense.
A similar case is Pete Crow-Armstrong, who signed a six-year, $115 million contract this year.
The contract buys out all four of his arbitration years and two free-agent years. This deal came before his MVP-caliber season, which would have dramatically raised the deal’s value.
Uncertainty around the salary cap and what the next collective bargaining agreement could look like remains, but regardless, locking up Pages for a while may be smart business to avoid a serious rise in value, as the Cubs did.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Rare Shohei Ohtani Jersey Fetches Eye-Popping Price in Auction
item.dc:creator: Aaron Coloma
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani's signed jersey from the 2025 Tokyo Series, featuring the first ever Gold Logoman worn in an MLB game, an autograph on the back and a Tokyo Series patch on the left arm, just sold for $2,055,700 in an auction. The price of the auction is more than the Dodgers for the 2026 season, as $68 million of his $70 million contract is deferred. What's So Special About Shohei Ohtani's Jersey? The jersey is a one-of-one piece of merchandise, and anything belonging
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani's signed jersey from the 2025 Tokyo Series, featuring the first ever Gold Logoman worn in an MLB game, an autograph on the back and a Tokyo Series patch on the left arm, just sold for $2,055,700 in an auction.
The price of the auction is more than the Dodgers for the 2026 season, as $68 million of his $70 million contract is deferred.
What's So Special About Shohei Ohtani's Jersey?
The jersey is a one-of-one piece of merchandise, and anything belonging Ohtani will fetch a massive price on the open market. Scott Keeney (aka DJ Skee) of The Realest, who managed the auction, explained the importance of this specific jersey.
"For Ohtani, Japan is everything," he said. "This was his homecoming, his first Major League game ever played in Japan, sandwiched between his two World Series wins and the first game of an MVP season. There can never be another one of those," he said. "More than 25 million people in Japan watched it—the most-watched MLB game ever in Japan—and he got his first hit of this milestone season in this jersey.
"And then there's the Gold Logoman! This is the first Gold Logoman ever worn in a Major League game. Not only the first for Ohtani, but the first one ever in MLB history, and it's still intact on the jersey.
"…Add his kanji signature and his inscriptions, 'Opening Day Tokyo Series,' 'GU 3-18-25,' and '25 NL MVP,' and there just isn't another Ohtani jersey like it- and I believe it will go down as his most important jersey ever.
"…There are other Ohtani jerseys and so many Ohtani milestone moments. This one has perfect provenance: Ohtani in his prime coming home to Japan, and the first Gold Logoman ever. That combination is unstoppable. Whatever it sells for now, I think people will look back and see it as the steal of a lifetime. Over time, while we will sell items for more money, this may be looked at as the greatest jersey to come to market when looked back in history."
Ohtani's jersey is one of his most important pieces of memorabilia thus far into his career, and the winner of the auction is sure to go home happy with their new acquisition.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Philadelphia Phillies Predicted to Trade for Dodgers World Series Champion
item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: The Philadelphia Phillies are expected to be active in the MLB trade market this offseason. One potential player the Phillies could inquire about is Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Alex Call. Recently, BR.com's Kerry Miller urged the Phillies to trade for Call in a predictions piece: "Unless Bryce Harper is moving back to right field on a more permanent basis, Philadelphia's outfield plans for 2027 appear to be Brandon Marsh in left, Justin Crawford in center and Derek Hill in right with Bryan De
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies are expected to be active in the MLB trade market this offseason.
One potential player the Phillies could inquire about is Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Alex Call.
Recently, BR.com's Kerry Miller urged the Phillies to trade for Call in a predictions piece:
"Unless Bryce Harper is moving back to right field on a more permanent basis, Philadelphia's outfield plans for 2027 appear to be Brandon Marsh in left, Justin Crawford in center and Derek Hill in right with Bryan De La Cruz as the primary reserve. But with an estimated 2027 cash payroll that is already the highest in the majors, signing a Randy Arozarena or Ian Happ to improve that situation hardly seems like an option. Bringing Alex Call back to the NL East could work, though. He struggled in 2026, but had an .800 OPS between the 2024 and 2025 campaigns."
Miller notes that the Phillies could be targeting an 'Inexpensive-yet-impactful' outfielder.
Should the Phillies Trade for Alex Call?
The one caveat to this 'trade idea' is that Alex Call could have his contract non-tendered, which essentially means being released from the organization into the open market.
Alex Call is still in his arbitration years, so he is projected to earn a contract salary of $1-2 million in 2027.
However, speaking to the Dodgers side of this, they have strong outfield prospects, so why would they hold onto Call if there's younger talent within their organization?
And the flip for the Phillies is: why would they trade for Alex Call in the first place if he could just be able to be claimed?
Alex Call fits the bill of what Miller notes that the Phillies need, but Philadelphia would need Call to have a bounce-back season to make it worth it.
He batted .233 in 163 at-bats in 2026 with just one home run, and an OPS+ of 84.
In 270 at-bats in 2025, Call posted an OPS+ of 111 with 20 XBH.
Call earned a 2025 World Series ring with the Dodgers, but didn't see much playing time during their 2026 playoff run. He has experience in MLB and can provide the Phillies with some veteran leadership in the outfield group.
Taking a Quick Look at Alex Call's MLB Career
Alex Call made his MLB debut in 2022 with Cleveland.
He has played with the Washington Nationals, Los Angeles Dodgers, and Cleveland.
Across 1021 at-bats, his lifetime batting average is .241 with 22 home runs, 48 doubles, and an OPS+ of 98, which suggests he has been a league-average hitter since debuting.
Call can also provide smart baserunning and strong defensive.
Phillies fans, would you be open to a trade for Alex Call? And how much capital would you be willing to offload in a potential deal?
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Philadelphia Phillies Predicted to Trade for Dodgers World Series Champion appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Max Muncy compares Tarik Skubal to Clayton Kershaw on start days
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Abdón Ibarra
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers took a big swing at the trade deadline to acquire Tarik Skubal, and although they fell short of a three-peat, the left-hander was instrumental to success they did have in the meantime. Not only was Skubal extremely valuable on the mound, but he also become a popular figure in the clubhouse. Part of that stems from how Skubal interacted with his teammates, even on days when he was the starting pitcher. But how Skubal presents himself now was not always the case during his
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers took a big swing at the trade deadline to acquire Tarik Skubal, and although they fell short of a three-peat, the left-hander was instrumental to success they did have in the meantime.
Not only was Skubal extremely valuable on the mound, but he also become a popular figure in the clubhouse. Part of that stems from how Skubal interacted with his teammates, even on days when he was the starting pitcher.
But how Skubal presents himself now was not always the case during his career. Instead, he often emulated behavior he saw from veterans in the Detroit Tigers’ clubhouse. That typically involved having headphones in and keeping to themselves. But at a certain point, he decided it would be more beneficial to be his authentic self instead.
“I just found it to be exhausting. I don’t think that’s who I am. It’s kind of putting on a facade,” Skubal recently explained. “You’re just not yourself. I didn’t feel like myself when I was doing that, putting headphones in and trying to be focused. I found myself mentally exhausted in the second or third innings of games.
“And I’m like, ‘Why am I tired today? I should be ready to go.’ When I got hurt in ’22, I decided enough is enough. I’m caring way too much about all the little things that don’t really matter, don’t really impact the game of baseball.
“I don’t know if it’s like superstitious, but like making sure the music is the right setting, making sure the music is the right songs at the right time, and you’re just caring about all the wrong things, I think. For me it was mentally freeing to take my headphones off and just be who I am and interact with guys.
“As it gets closer to game time, you get ready to go and you’re going to go out there and compete. But I just didn’t really find much of a benefit of trying to be locked in four hours before a game. I want to be myself. Then I’ll lock in as the game gets closer.”
Max Muncy compares Tarik Skubal to Clayton Kershaw
For the Dodgers players who have been around awhile, including Max Muncy, Skubal’s approach represented a drastic departure from what they would normally see from a pitcher like Clayton Kershaw.
“For me with starting pitchers, when it’s their start day, it’s always kind of an interesting debacle, we’ll call it,” Muncy began when asked about Skubal’s demeanor.
“With him, I’ve never seen somebody be so normal on a start day. To me that’s really refreshing and really awesome to see. He doesn’t change his attitude or his mind, the way he acts in the clubhouse with the other guys. For a guy to be as competitive as he is on the mound and as fiery as he is, it’s really awesome to see how he goes about every other day exactly the same. That’s pretty rare to see.”
Muncy noticed a difference between the two pitchers from Skubal’s first start for the Dodgers.
“[Skubal] came up to me and started asking me questions and talking about something that wasn’t even involved in the game. I don’t remember what it was, but he was talking about something and it just completely threw me off,” Muncy recalled. “Like you said, playing with Kersh for all those years, it’s the complete opposite.
“That’s where I go to the word ‘debacle’ a bit. Us position players always laugh about the starting pitchers just because could you imagine if we acted that way every time we had to start on the field? Those are the main guys. They have their routines, and they’re that way for a reason. You can’t win games without them.
“So you really need the starting pitching. Whatever routine they want to go with and whatever show they want to put on, we’re here for all of it. Yeah, Scoobs and Kersh couldn’t be more opposite in terms of their start day routine.”

item.dc:creator: Gabe Smallson; Unknown

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers made one of the most anticipated moves of 2026 ahead of the trade deadline by trading for two-time Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal, the ace of the Detroit Tigers.
Since Skubal was traded on an expiring contract, there is no guarantee that he will be back on the Dodgers in 2027. LA has been predicted to compete with six teams that would potentially offer the southpaw a deal this offseason — one that is expected to potentially exceed $400 million.
Skubal spoke after last week's postseason exit on what it meant to play for the Dodgers this summer, and though it is no indication of what the financial side of things will look like this offseason, provided a glowing review on the organization.
“I mean, incredible organization, incredible teammates, incredible fanbase,” Skubal said. “Honored to wear the LA across your chest and on the hat. Doesn’t make this feel any better. It sucks, but I think everybody in here gave it everything they had, and sometimes that’s just baseball."
Skubal made 10 regular season starts after the trade and totaled a 2.61 ERA in that span. Over 11 postseason innings (two starts), he had a 2.45 ERA, throwing 14 strikeouts to four walks.
In other news, veteran utility star Kiké Hernández recently spoke on his future as he becomes a free agent once again this offseason. The fan favorite made his intentions known when speaking to reporters after last week's National League Championship Series elimination.
"I would love to have one more try, trying to win another one," Hernández said. "But I don't really know what's going to happen. I hope I'm back, and if I'm not, I hope that I get to play for a winning team."
Finally, among the many free agents on the team, there is one that the Dodgers simply can't afford to lose. Alternatively, there is also one that, according to the team at Dodgers On SI, LA can afford to let walk.

Qué dijo Ohtani sobre volver al montículo El versátil pelotero abordó la pregunta después del último juego de la Serie de Campeonato y aseguró que volverá a hacer todos los esfuerzos para lanzar con los Dodgers la
item.content:encoded:
La temporada de los Dodgers terminó abruptamente con la barrida ante los Brewers durante la Serie de Campeonato. Rumbo a un receso invernal de muchas interrogantes, una de las preguntas principales para la gerencia es saber: ¿Shohei Ohtani volverá a lanzar la próxima campaña en la MLB?
Qué dijo Ohtani sobre volver al montículo
El versátil pelotero abordó la pregunta después del último juego de la Serie de Campeonato y aseguró que volverá a hacer todos los esfuerzos para lanzar con los Dodgers la próxima temporada.
“Sí, definitivamente”, dijo Ohtani a través de su intérprete Will Ireton. “Y buscando seguir adelante para tener una mejor temporada el siguiente año”.
Shohei Ohtani finally made his Dodgers pitching debut ????
Ohtani went one inning and gave up one run in his first time pitching in nearly two years‼️ (via @mlb, @sportsnetLA) pic.twitter.com/lQlCqvyEvO
— SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) June 17, 2025
Ohtani declinó hacer cualquier comentario si, en su camino de regreso al montículo, se tendrá que someter a alguna cirugía durante la temporada baja.
Una temporada de claroscuros para Shohei
Shohei comenzó la temporada en la rotación abridora inicando un juego por semana, al mismo tiempo que bateaba como primero en el orden de la alineación de los Dodgers. En sus primeras 10 presentaciones tiró para un récord de 6-2, con efectividad de 0.74, ponchando a 67 bateadores al mismo tiempo que solo daba 18 bases por bolas.
Además, bateando para .301 con 14 dobles, 10 jonrones, 33 carreras impulsadas y 41 anotadas, Ohtani se perfilaba como el candidato para ganarse el premio al Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Nacional.
Desafortunadamente para él y los Dodgers, Ohtani se vio mermado por una lesión en la rodilla izquierda y el bíceps derecho, así como una molestia en el cuello. Aún con sus problemas físicos, intentó mantenerse en la rotación un mes más consiguiendo una marca de 2-0 y efectividad de 4.38 en sus siguientes cuatro aperturas, hasta que finalmente las lesiones le impidieron seguir.
Estuvo un mes trabajando en su rehabilitación, al mismo tiempo que permaneció como bateador designado, y parecía que todo retomaba su curso a finales de agosto. Una recaída un día antes de su primera salida de regreso lo relegó hasta el final del calendario.
What a pitch from Didier Fuentes to strike out Shohei Ohtani ????????
????: FS1 pic.twitter.com/IqktzZdmK4
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 5, 2026
Sus lesiones también le habrían pasado factura a la ofensiva pues bateó su último jonrón de la temporada regular el 18 de agosto y volvió a volarse la cerca hasta el 16 de octubre, durante el Juego 4 de la Serie de Campeonato.
En postemporada bateó para .192 con 4 bases por bolas y 10 ponches en 32 apariciones al plato.

item.title: [The Korea Herald] Dodgers swept out of NLCS, management under fire
item.dc:creator: Edwin Choi
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers' bid for a third straight World Series title ended abruptly with a four-game sweep by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, putting manager Dave Roberts back under scrutiny despite one of the most successful managerial runs in baseball. Milwaukee advanced to the World Series for the first time since 1982 after winning all four games of the NLCS. Los Angeles, widely viewed as a championship favorite entering the season, struggled to turn early l
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' bid for a third straight World Series title ended abruptly with a four-game sweep by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, putting manager Dave Roberts back under scrutiny despite one of the most successful managerial runs in baseball.
Milwaukee advanced to the World Series for the first time since 1982 after winning all four games of the NLCS. Los Angeles, widely viewed as a championship favorite entering the season, struggled to turn early leads into wins and was eliminated without taking a game in the series.
Roberts drew criticism for several decisions during the series, including his use of pinch hitters and his willingness to stay with players who were struggling offensively.
Brewers manager Pat Murphy, however, said the expectations surrounding the Dodgers make Roberts' job unusually demanding.
"Anything short of a championship is considered a failure," Murphy said, according to DodgerBlue.
Murphy said the Dodgers remain a team he respects, pointing to their star power and consecutive World Series championships in 2024 and 2025. He said beating a club of that stature made Milwaukee's own run more meaningful.
He also noted that Roberts operates under constant pressure because of the Dodgers' payroll, roster and recent success.
"I don't think there's anyone in a tougher or lonelier position than Dave Roberts," Murphy said. "When anything other than winning it all is viewed as failure, that is a very difficult standard to live with."
Roberts has nevertheless built a lengthy record of success in Los Angeles.
The Dodgers have reached the postseason in each of his 11 seasons as manager, winning 10 division titles. They have recorded six 100-win seasons, finished with the National League's best regular-season record five times and won three World Series championships during his tenure.
Roberts also has 72 postseason victories, the second-most by a manager in major league history. His .621 career winning percentage is the highest among managers since Jackie Robinson broke Major League Baseball's color barrier in 1947, according to DodgerBlue.
The Brewers' sweep was notable because Los Angeles scored first in every game but failed to hold those advantages. Milwaukee repeatedly rallied and ultimately controlled the series both offensively and defensively.
Murphy said that persistence was central to Milwaukee's success.
He described his roster as a group that continued to compete regardless of the Dodgers' reputation or collection of star players, and said the Brewers entered the series determined to prove they could beat the two-time defending champions.
For Roberts, the result means another offseason in which his decisions will be examined closely. But Murphy argued that the Dodgers' loss should not erase the consistency Roberts has maintained over more than a decade in charge.
(This article was produced with the assistance of AI. — Ed.)

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Hyeseong Kim Reflects on His Difficult 2026 Season
item.dc:creator: Los Royers
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — Hyeseong Kim closed his second season with the Los Angeles Dodgers by candidly assessing his performance. He also thanked the organization and its fans. In an Instagram post published Sunday, Kim acknowledged that he did not make the impact he expected in 2026. He said he was disappointed in himself, but rejected any suggestion that his frustration extended to the Dodgers. “I love the Dodgers, and I have never once been disappointed in this team,” Kim wrote. “My only disappoint
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Hyeseong Kim closed his second season with the Los Angeles Dodgers by candidly assessing his performance. He also thanked the organization and its fans.
In an Instagram post published Sunday, Kim acknowledged that he did not make the impact he expected in 2026. He said he was disappointed in himself, but rejected any suggestion that his frustration extended to the Dodgers.
“I love the Dodgers, and I have never once been disappointed in this team,” Kim wrote. “My only disappointment was in myself.”
Kim thanked the fans who continued supporting him and said he has no regrets about choosing Los Angeles. He finished his message by promising to return as a better person and player next season.
Hyeseong Kim’s uneven 2026 season
Kim appeared in 43 major league games, batting .259 with a .323 on-base percentage. He added one home run, 11 RBI and five stolen bases. The Dodgers optioned him to Triple-A Oklahoma City in late May. He remained with the Comets for the rest of the regular season.
The 27-year-old played 85 games for Oklahoma City. He batted .262 with three home runs, 31 RBI and 15 stolen bases. Los Angeles brought him back for the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves. Kim made one appearance as a defensive replacement.
Kim did not make the Dodgers’ National League Championship Series roster. His defensive versatility and speed remained useful. However, his limited major league opportunity made 2026 a step backward after he appeared in 71 games as a rookie.
Kim remains committed to the Dodgers
The strongest part of Kim’s message was his insistence that he remains committed to the organization. He described joining the Dodgers as his choice and said he had not regretted the decision for a moment.
Kim is guaranteed $3.75 million in 2027. It is the final guaranteed season of the three-year contract he signed before the 2025 campaign. The Dodgers also hold club options for 2028 and 2029.
After a season spent moving between the majors and Triple-A, Kim will enter the offseason trying to earn a larger role on a crowded Dodgers roster.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] New York Yankees Prediction Reveals Likelihood of Tarik Skubal Acquisition
item.dc:creator: Maria Aldrich
item.description: The New York Yankees have several paths they could take in free agency this offseason. If history repeats itself, they will be quite successful. One of the top names floating is that of Tarik Skubal of the Los Angeles Dodgers. Do the Yankees stand a chance? Yankees Prediction Points To Skubal Opportunity Christopher Kline of FanSided unveiled his latest rankings of Skubal's potential landing spots. Of the eight teams he mentioned, New York comes in at No. 4. This isn't a bad spot to be for an or
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees have several paths they could take in free agency this offseason.
If history repeats itself, they will be quite successful.
One of the top names floating is that of Tarik Skubal of the Los Angeles Dodgers. Do the Yankees stand a chance?
Yankees Prediction Points To Skubal Opportunity
Christopher Kline of FanSided unveiled his latest rankings of Skubal's potential landing spots.
Of the eight teams he mentioned, New York comes in at No. 4.
This isn't a bad spot to be for an organization that generally thrives on its perfectly imperfect starting rotation.
But that certainly doesn't mean they're the most likely ballclub to acquire to veteran southpaw.
"It would require Hal Steinbrenner and the front office to basically sign off on a blank check, but the Yankees' ALDS loss to the Rays was a sobering defeat," Kline explained. "There are cracks in the foundation. Many of those cracks are injury-related and concentrated in the lineup; Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodón is as strong a four-man gauntlet as any rotation in MLB. The Yankees also have Ryan Weathers, Will Warren and top prospects like Elmer Rodríguez and Carlos Lagrange for depth.
"Still, the Yankees know the importance of depth, especially as their non-Schlittler core ages and becomes more injury-prone. Skubal provides stability and instantly lends credibility to any postseason aspirations. Schlittler-Skubal becomes the most fearsome pitching duo in baseball. Never say never."
Sobering is perhaps the best way to describe how their campaign ended.
Taking it a step further, the value of depth became all the more clear for the Yankees after their star slugger Aaron Judge was sidelined for much of the season.
This forced New York to rely on their younger stars who tend to play in the shadows.
This article was originally published on HEAVY

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Kyle Tucker makes promise to Dodgers fans
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: Kyle Tucker struggled for the better part of his first season with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but he was able to finish the year on a strong note. The four-time All-Star emerged as arguably the team’s most productive hitter in October, batting .333/.419/.519 with two doubles, one home run and two RBI across 31 plate appearances. He reached base safely in all eight postseason games and recorded at least one hit in seven of them. Tucker finally looked like the player the Dodgers expected when they s
item.content:encoded:
Kyle Tucker struggled for the better part of his first season with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but he was able to finish the year on a strong note.
The four-time All-Star emerged as arguably the team’s most productive hitter in October, batting .333/.419/.519 with two doubles, one home run and two RBI across 31 plate appearances. He reached base safely in all eight postseason games and recorded at least one hit in seven of them.
Tucker finally looked like the player the Dodgers expected when they signed him to a four-year, $240 million contract ahead of the 2026 season. He largely underperformed up until the playoffs, batting just .233/.330/.385 with 23 doubles, four triples, 17 home runs and 70 RBI in 154 regular-season games.
Tucker thanked Dodgers fans for their support in an Instagram post and vowed to come back stronger next season.
Tucker’s first season with the Dodgers was nothing short of disappointing, but he found some success when it mattered most and will now look to build on that momentum in 2027.
While the Dodgers’ roster could undergo some changes during the offseason, Tucker remains an important part of their potential success going forward. He is unlikely to be traded this offseason due to his contract and uncertainty over the looming MLB lockout.
However, Tucker could potentially reach free agency after the 2027 season by exercising a player option. That may only be feasible if he is able to bounce back and have a year that’s more up to his standards.
Kyle Tucker made key adjustments
Tucker first started showing some signs of a turnaround on Sept. 4, when he crushed a home run on a 99 mph fastball at the top of the strike zone. He continued to have success down the stretch, which Dodgers manager Dave Roberts attributed to figuring out his swing mechanics.
“I’m not a person that’s talking about mechanics too often, but I do think in this particular situation, he’s cleaned up his bat path and he’s staying in the hitting zone a lot longer,” Roberts said at the time. “Whereas before, breaking balls, he wasn’t staying on. Fastballs, he was underneath.
“But I think right now, he’s in a great spot mechanically and with the confidence he has in his swing.”

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dodgers have one major advantage the Mets can't offer Tarik Skubal
item.dc:creator: Drew Koch
item.description: Tarik Skubal will get a head start in free agency after the Los Angeles Dodgers were unable to find a way to overcome the Milwaukee Brewers during Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Thursday night. The loss ended the Dodgers' aspirations of a three-peat, and effectively started Skubal's free agency clock. The Dodgers traded for Skubal at this year's deadline, shipping top outfield prospect Zyhir Hope and pitcher River Ryan to the Detroit Tigers in exchange for the two-time Cy Y
item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal will get a head start in free agency after the Los Angeles Dodgers were unable to find a way to overcome the Milwaukee Brewers during Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Thursday night. The loss ended the Dodgers' aspirations of a three-peat, and effectively started Skubal's free agency clock.
The Dodgers traded for Skubal at this year's deadline, shipping top outfield prospect Zyhir Hope and pitcher River Ryan to the Detroit Tigers in exchange for the two-time Cy Young award-winner. Though most observers expect LA to be heavily involved in his free agency during the offseason, they won't be the club vying for his services.
SNY MLB insider Chelsea Janes is reporting that the New York Mets are expected to match whatever offer Skubal receives this winter. This is hardly surprising, as most intel has linked the Dodgers and Mets as the two most likely teams to sign the left-hander this offseason. A dark horse or two is sure to emerge, but for all intents and purposes, the pursuit of Skubal will end with one of these two teams.
Both Los Angeles and New York have deep pockets, and Skubal will undoubtedly be seeking to sign the largest deal for a starting pitcher in the history of Major League Baseball. Look for the eventual deal to be worth upwards of $400 million, surpassing the 12-year, $325 million deal Yoshinodu Yamamoto signed in 2024.
But the Dodgers can offer something the Mets can't — a consistent opportunity to win a World Series championship.
While LA's hopes of a three-peat were dashed by Milwaukee, Dodgers fans know that Andrew Friedman will be quick to restock the roster with hopes of returning to the Fall Classic in 2027.
The Dodgers are better positioned than the Mets for long-term success
Regardless of how the upcoming Collective Bargaining negotiations turn out, it's difficult to see any type of resolution between the owners and the Players Association that drastically affects LA's chances to compete for a world title for the foreseeable future. The Dodgers still have the best player in baseball (Shohei Ohtani) under contract, and rotation (Yamamoto, Ohtani, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow) is already top-notch, even without Skubal.
The Mets, on the other hand, haven't won a World Series since 1986. Even last season, with All-Stars like Juan Soto, Francisco Lindor, and Pete Alonso, New York was beaten out by a Cincinnati Reds team that won just 83 games to qualify for the playoffs. The Mets came into this season with high expectations, but ended the year in the NL East basement.
It's highly unlikely that Skubal will find that type atomsphere enticing, espeically if there are similar offers on the table from the Dodgers or another high-dollar suitor.
Despite Steve Cohen's excessive spending, few organizations in Major League Baseball are less appealing than the Mets. New York has endured six losing seasons over the last 10 years. While some stars don't mind playing second fiddle to the New York Yankees and getting bounced from the postseason during the second week of September, Skubal seems to enjoy LA's winning culture.

item.content:encoded:
Earlier this week, the Los Angeles Dodgers had their season come to an end when they lost to the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS.
They lost the final game by a score of 6-4 (at home).
ESPN’s Jeff Passan wrote (on October 15): “The Milwaukee Brewers are going to the World Series after sweeping the two-time defending champion Dodgers. The Brewers came back from down 4-0 to advance to their first World Series since 1982 and exact revenge on the Dodgers’ NLCS sweep last year.”
Dodgers Star Sends Out Heartfelt IG Post
After their season ended, Kyle Tucker sent out a heartfelt post to Instagram (on Saturday).
He wrote: “Through every high and low, thank you to our fans for riding with us all season. We appreciate the love and support more than you know. This isn’t the end — we’ll be back. 💪🏻”
There were over 7,000 likes on his post in less than two hours.

item.title: [FanSided] Ranking Tarik Skubal suitors from favorites to dark horses
item.dc:creator: Christopher Kline
item.description: Tarik Skubal and the Los Angeles Dodgers were swept out of the NLCS by the 103-win Milwaukee Brewers, a refreshing change of pace after two years of Dodgers dominance — and a helpful reminder to the MLB owners that payroll alone does not determine winning. It also leaves Skubal with a more difficult decision in free agency than many expected. The Dodgers will not re-sign Skubal before the lockout in December, as there's simply too much risk without knowing how the salary cap will function come 2
item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal and the Los Angeles Dodgers were swept out of the NLCS by the 103-win Milwaukee Brewers, a refreshing change of pace after two years of Dodgers dominance — and a helpful reminder to the MLB owners that payroll alone does not determine winning. It also leaves Skubal with a more difficult decision in free agency than many expected.
The Dodgers will not re-sign Skubal before the lockout in December, as there's simply too much risk without knowing how the salary cap will function come 2027. Really regardless of how MLB's labor dispute plays out, however, Los Angeles will hope to retain Skubal, who is still rightly regarded as the most bankable ace in baseball. The question is: Are the Dodgers the favorites for his services? Let's rank all realistic suitors, from least to most realistic.
8. Philadelphia Phillies
The Phillies are desperate and the Phillies typically spend money. Not necessarily as liberally as fans would like, but it's not impossible to imagine Dave Dombrowski — with the World Series window closing rapidly on this aging core — deciding that Skubal is worth an all-in push.
It would give Philadelphia the most talented rotation in MLB between Skubal, Zack Wheeler, Cristopher Sánchez, Jesús Luzardo and Aaron Nola, four of whom could compete for NL Cy Young next season. There's also Andrew Painter, a former top prospect who came into his own down the stretch and delivered big outs in the postseason, to provide depth.
The Phillies probably have enough money wrapped up in that rotation (and in Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber and Trea Turner) to be turned off of paying Skubal top dollar, but it's a fun thought for a team hoping to lean even more on run prevention moving forward.
7. Boston Red Sox
The Red Sox wielded one of the deepest and most reliable rotations in MLB last season; that was with top ace Garrett Crochet on the IL. Upon Crochet's return, Boston will have a compelling blend of experience (Crochet, Ranger Suárez) and emerging youth (Payton Tolle, Jake Bennett) to throw at their opponents.
Then again, they know the toll injuries can take, and Sonny Gray — probably their best regular season starter this past season — is now a free agent. The Red Sox could simply line up a new contract for Gray and be content, but why not aim higher? Skubal has proven remarkably durable over the years and he offers Boston a much longer window as Crochet's partner in crime. Suddenly, the Red Sox have the best one-two punch in baseball and it wouldn't be especially close.
After the Yankees lit them up in the Wild Card round (and after Boston's top arms couldn't pitch deep into either postseason game), there's pressure for a big swing.
6. Chicago Cubs
There's no doubting the Cubs' ability to generate offense, but the rotation has been a sore spot for years now. Jed Hoyer has shown a great appetite for spending in free agency of late; the Alex Bregman signing was a real flex. That said, Chicago needs to allocate more resources toward pitching. The Edward Cabrera trade went belly up. Shōta Imanaga is a free agent now, as are trade deadline pickups Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes.
Chicago will get help internally with both Cade Horton and Justin Steele returning from season-long elbow injuries; Ben Brown, who finally broke out in 2026, should also be back in the mix. Beyond them, however, it's pretty grim. Matthew Boyd and Javier Assad can eat innings in the regular season, but neither has proven able to pitch deep in October — at least not consistently.
Skubal would deliver Chicago the frontline ace it has long lacked, with a solid scaffolding of talent behind him. The Cubs would be much better positioned to challenge Milwaukee in the division and potentially emerge from a crowded National League field.
5. Detroit Tigers
Skubal has made it clear he would've spent his entire career in Detroit if it was up to him. All the Tigers need to do is come through with a competitive offer. While last year's surprise Framber Valdez signing was a positive indication of the front office's competitive intent, there's a reason no Skubal extension ever came to fruition — or even remotely close.
A client of Scott Boras, Skubal was never inclined to sign an extension. But the Tigers' offers weren't even in the parking lot, much less the ballpark. Detroit will need to scale up its ambition significantly if it wants to lure Skubal back to the midwest.
All that said, Skubal has an affection for Detroit that's worth mentioning. The Tigers also desperately need a frontline ace in Skubal's mold. Young bucks like Troy Melton, Keider Montero, Jackson Jobe and River Ryan are very talented, but the Tigers don't really have an established vet besides Valdez, who was a mess last season.
4. New York Yankees
The Yankees tend to flex their muscles in free agency, although with diminishing returns in recent years. New York is no longer the most lucrative destination for a lot of A-tier stars. Juan Soto a couple years ago, Kyle Tucker last winter; the Yankees are getting outbid pretty consistently these days. That has not stopped New York from stockpiling stars, though, especially in the rotation.
It would require Hal Steinbrenner and the front office to basically sign off on a blank check, but the Yankees' ALDS loss to the Rays was a sobering defeat. There are cracks in the foundation. Many of those cracks are injury-related and concentrated in the lineup; Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodón is as strong a four-man gauntlet as any rotation in MLB. The Yankees also have Ryan Weathers, Will Warren and top prospects like Elmer Rodríguez and Carlos Lagrange for depth.
Still, the Yankees know the importance of depth, especially as their non-Schlittler core ages and becomes more injury-prone. Skubal provides stability and instantly lends credibility to any postseason aspirations. Schlittler-Skubal becomes the most fearsome pitching duo in baseball. Never say never.
3. Toronto Blue Jays
The Blue Jays have steadily become the most aggressive front office in the American League. After finishing runner-up in the Juan Soto and Shohei Ohtani sweepstakes, Toronto extended Vladimir Guerrero Jr. at a $500 million price point and signed Dylan Cease in the early days of free agency last winter. A disappointing season should not preclude Toronto from maintaining its all-in approach; if anything, it's more motivation for the Blue Jays to stack talent. This team was in the World Series a year ago.
Toronto is a great market, with a vibrant local culture and an entire country behind the Blue Jays. That ought to appeal to the vanity of a star like Skubal, who would team up with the projected AL Cy Young runner-up in Cease. The Jays also made a savvy trade for José Soriano at the deadline, adding another premium arm in his prime. Trey Yesavage, once healthy, could resume his ascent to stardom. The talent is there.
Skubal solidifies Toronto as a legitimate World Series contender coming into 2027. Moreover, the Jays have a lot of money coming off the books, which should free up the front office to spend recklessly where it counts. Toronto is always the "dark horse" in these top-dollar bidding wars, but ruling out the Blue Jays would be foolish.
2. Los Angeles Dodgers
It's impossible to rule out the incumbents. Los Angeles made the Skubal trade in part because of their deep farm system — and in part because it set the stage for a potential long-term partnership. There's a reason small-market front offices were unwilling to match L.A.'s outgoing package (see: Brewers). The Dodgers could afford to trade two of the 50ish best prospects in baseball because the team can feel reasonably good about both competing for a World Series this season (oh well) and re-signing Skubal when he hits the open market.
An NLCS loss does complicate the situation somewhat, not to mention the unknowability of upcoming labor disputes. The Dodgers' loss was a direct result of investing hundreds of millions of dollars in stars who are beginning to decline. Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman, Shohei Ohtani, Will Smith, Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell are all on the wrong side of 30; Tucker will join that list next season. Los Angeles will endure more and more diminishing returns.
That said, nothing (besides a strict salary cap) can really stop the Dodgers from compensating for declining stars by signing more expensive stars, even if it leaves the cap sheet in utter chaos five years from now. That has been L.A.'s strategy to date; it was part of the logic behind the Skubal trade. The Dodgers still arguably represent Skubal's best chance to win a World Series, which will no doubt be part of the calculus if another team can't dramatically outspend them.
1. New York Mets
If any team can blow L.A.'s offer out of the water, it's the Mets. Steve Cohen is baseball's richest owner and New York has consistently tossed its hat in the ring for MLB's premium free agents. Juan Soto's $765 million contract set a new record; Skubal very well could set a record for pitchers.
The Mets are coming off of a last-place season, too, which only fuels anxiety in the fan base. It should also fuel aggression in the front office. David Stearns is under pressure to prove that he has what it takes to win in New York. Skubal would join an emerging ace in Nolan McLean, plus other whippersnappers like Zac Thornton and Jonah Tong. The Mets need depth besides, as Kodai Senga and Sean Manaea look more like bullpen arms these days. New York, however, is the one non-Dodgers team with enough money to sign Skubal and pursue other targets.
If the Dodgers get spooked by the shadow of their own payroll, which is more likely than ever, the Mets are the logical team we can expect to swoop in and win the Skubal bidding war outright.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] "I’ll Die on That Hill”: Dodgers Face a Tough Shohei Ohtani Call After World Series Dreams Fall Apart
item.dc:creator: Utsav Gupta
item.description: Shohei Ohtani, the two-way star for the Los Angeles Dodgers, posted a 1.79 ERA as a pitcher but managed just five hits in 26 postseason at-bats. One Dodgers analyst believes the path forward requires a radical shift in how the team uses its star as the Dodgers face an uncomfortable choice: keep Ohtani as a two-way star or unlock his full potential as a hitter. The Brewers' NLCS sweep eliminated the Dodgers from World Series contention, forcing the organization to reassess Ohtani's role. Doug McK
item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani, the two-way star for the Los Angeles Dodgers, posted a 1.79 ERA as a pitcher but managed just five hits in 26 postseason at-bats. One Dodgers analyst believes the path forward requires a radical shift in how the team uses its star as the Dodgers face an uncomfortable choice: keep Ohtani as a two-way star or unlock his full potential as a hitter.
The Brewers' NLCS sweep eliminated the Dodgers from World Series contention, forcing the organization to reassess Ohtani's role. Doug McKain (@DMAC_LA), a Dodgers personality, said in this Thursday night episode of Dodgers Dugout.
"So I will take it to my grave. I will die on that hill. If the Dodgers had the best version of Shohei Ohtani, the hitter, like we saw last year, they would have beaten the Brewers. They would have won the World Series," McKain said.
The sweep revealed a struggling batter who had lost his form. Ohtani hit just .160/.284/.253 in 88 plate appearances following August 18, striking out ten times in October. His Game 4 three-run shot was his first long ball in 26 games.
Two-way players historically struggle with workload management. Ohtani's June knee injury, followed by poor hitting, suggests the dual role may have contributed to his decline.
Ohtani offered a more measured perspective following the loss. According to MLB.com, Ohtani responded through interpreter Will Ireton.
"Yes, definitely. And looking forward to having a better season next year," Ohtani said.
His ERA stood at 1.79 with a .179 opponent batting average over 85 2/3 innings, and only Jim Palmer, Jacob deGrom, and Clayton Kershaw have a lower ERA than Ohtani in their careers.
However, Ohtani's pitching durability became a concern when knee problems emerged on June 11, and over his next four starts, he allowed 12 earned runs in 24 2/3 innings after allowing just five in his first 61.
Ohtani has started and ended an MLB season as a two-way player only twice, in 2021 and 2022. Injuries derailed him in 2018 and 2023, with elbow problems in both seasons.
McKain took this logic further during the same Dodgers Dugout broadcast by saying, "If getting the best version of Shohei Ohtani the hitter means he's a one-way player, then that's what's best for the Los Angeles Dodgers."
The argument gains weight because the lineup, not the rotation, sank this club. The Dodgers have a .148 batting average with runners in scoring position during the NLCS. They were out-homered 7-1, and their catcher, Will Smith, went 3-for-31 in the postseason.
However, the pitching record remains valid. Dodgers' right-handed Tyler Glasnow and left-handed Blake Snell threw only 116 2/3 innings during the regular season, while Yoshinobu Yamamoto is the only pitcher qualified for the rotation.
The rotation picture could shift again this winter. Tarik Skubal, the left-handed pitcher acquired at the deadline, might depart in free agency, leaving Yamamoto and the unpredictable Ohtani to lead a rotation already short on innings.
The Dodgers are well aware of this dilemma. According to Katie Woo of The Athletic, Andrew Friedman, the president of baseball operations, commented before the playoffs that Ohtani's historic position takes a great toll on the organization.
"What he's doing is unprecedented, and it takes a real toll," president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said before the postseason. "It's unprecedented for all of us, and we're kind of feeling our way through it together."
There might be another way. The Dodgers could rest Ohtani for several months before ramping him up to full participation, even though there is still uncertainty about the surgery he may need for a knee or biceps injury.
Timing is key. Ohtani turns 32 soon, has seven years remaining on his deal, and the Dodgers need him healthy for the playoffs, not just April.

item.content:encoded:
Kiké Hernandez may have played his final game with the Dodgers.
The fan favorite acknowledged the uncertain future he faces as he enters free agency in an Instagram post in which Hernandez expressed his gratefulness for fans.
“LA, we fell short of our big goal. But looking at the big picture, what a ride these last three years were!!” Hernandez wrote in the Instagram caption.
“If this is it for us…. Once again, I will always be thankful for you guys & I will forever love ya! ♾️ #JustAKidFromPR,” Hernandez said.
President of baseball operations Andrew Friedman brought Hernandez back on a one-year deal last offseason, saying the “door was always open” for the utilityman. It remains unclear whether that will be the case this winter as Hernandez hits free agency again.
Hernandez has built his career as an electric personality in the Dodgers’ dugout and a clutch bat every October. His postseason numbers are simply mystifying with Hernandez coming to life every fall.
But as the Dodgers look to get younger, the front office may go in another direction this offseason. The Dodgers assembled the most expensive roster in baseball, which also happened to be the oldest.
While the Dodgers won 100 regular-season games with their veteran core, the back-to-back World Series champions were swept by a hungrier, younger Brewers team.
The four-game sweep in the National League Championship Series may alter the Dodgers’ plans as the front office attempts to build another winning roster.
Only time will tell whether Hernandez is a part of that group.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Kyle Tucker sends promising message to Dodgers fans after atrocious debut season
item.dc:creator: Valentina Martinez
item.description: The Dodgers face several questions after an early postseason exit in the National League Championship Series. The dynasty that the Dodgers have put together is in jeopardy of ending within the next few seasons if the front office can't assemble another winning roster. Kyle Tucker, who was signed to a four-year, $240 million deal ahead of the 2026 season, addressed fans as the future of the franchise is in limbo. "Through every high and low, thank you to our fans for riding with us all season. We
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers face several questions after an early postseason exit in the National League Championship Series.
The dynasty that the Dodgers have put together is in jeopardy of ending within the next few seasons if the front office can't assemble another winning roster. Kyle Tucker, who was signed to a four-year, $240 million deal ahead of the 2026 season, addressed fans as the future of the franchise is in limbo.
"Through every high and low, thank you to our fans for riding with us all season. We appreciate the love and support more than you know. This isn't the end — we'll be back," Tucker wrote in an Instagram post.
For most of 2026, the four-time All-Star was far from full form. Tucker ended the regular season with a .233 batting average, 17 home runs and 70 RBIs. He entered October with a .715 OPS, the lowest mark since his debut season in 2018 when he played 28 games.
Tucker's struggles became a point of contention among the fan base, but the star outfielder came to life in the postseason. The 29-year-old averaged .333 with a .967 OPS in October, which was perhaps the only highlight of his inaugural Dodgers season.
The Dodgers, who face an uncertain future after the failed quest for a three-peat, will need Tucker to play at All-Star strength the entire 2027 season as one of the many veterans on the roster. While Tucker's performance next year can't be known, one thing is certain, the Dodgers will surely try to get younger this winter.

item.title: [Full-Count] “不可解スルー”された山本由伸のSOS ド軍の命運を分けた一幕…判明したルールの盲点
item.dc:creator: Full-Count編集部
item.description: “不可解スルー”された山本由伸のSOS ド軍の命運を分けた一幕…判明したルールの盲点 球審が見落とした“側頭部タップ”MLB公式の見解を米名物分析官が明かす ドジャースの山本由伸投手が見せた“チャレンジ要求”を巡り、現地で波紋が広がっている。山本が判定に不服を示して頭を叩く仕草を見せたものの、球審に認められずチャレンジが実施されなかった場面について、米名物アナリストがMLBへ直接取材を敢行。なぜ認められなかったのか、その真相とルールの盲点を明かしている。 注目を集めているのは、米名物アナリストのジミー・オブライエン氏が手掛ける「ジョムボーイ・メディア」の解説動画。山本がカウント3-2の勝負所で投じた1球の判定を巡る一幕を詳細に分析した。 オブライエン氏によると、山本は三振を奪いたい重要な場面で判定に納得がいかず、側頭部あたりを軽く数回叩く仕草を見せたという。投手自身がABS（自動ボール・ストライク判定システム）のチャレンジを要求する際、頭を叩くジェスチャー自体は認められているものの、捕手のウィル・スミスはこのとき、同様の動きを見せていなかった。 なぜ山本の訴えはスルーされてしまったのか
item.content:encoded:
“不可解スルー”された山本由伸のSOS ド軍の命運を分けた一幕…判明したルールの盲点
球審が見落とした“側頭部タップ”MLB公式の見解を米名物分析官が明かす
ドジャースの山本由伸投手が見せた“チャレンジ要求”を巡り、現地で波紋が広がっている。山本が判定に不服を示して頭を叩く仕草を見せたものの、球審に認められずチャレンジが実施されなかった場面について、米名物アナリストがMLBへ直接取材を敢行。なぜ認められなかったのか、その真相とルールの盲点を明かしている。
注目を集めているのは、米名物アナリストのジミー・オブライエン氏が手掛ける「ジョムボーイ・メディア」の解説動画。山本がカウント3-2の勝負所で投じた1球の判定を巡る一幕を詳細に分析した。
オブライエン氏によると、山本は三振を奪いたい重要な場面で判定に納得がいかず、側頭部あたりを軽く数回叩く仕草を見せたという。投手自身がABS（自動ボール・ストライク判定システム）のチャレンジを要求する際、頭を叩くジェスチャー自体は認められているものの、捕手のウィル・スミスはこのとき、同様の動きを見せていなかった。
なぜ山本の訴えはスルーされてしまったのか。疑問に思ったオブライエン氏はMLBに直接問い合わせを行ったという。
同氏によると、MLB側は選手たちに対し「頭頂部を叩き、実際に言葉（口頭）で伝えるように」と指導・説明しているという。そして、「グラウンド上の審判の注意を惹く必要があるので、実際には（あのジェスチャーだけでは）認識するのが難しい。フィールド上の審判は基本的にキャッチャーの動きを見ている」との回答が得られたという。
オブライエン氏は「審判によっては（山本の動きを見て）『今タップしたな』と気づいて拾ってくれた可能性もある。そうなっていればドジャースにとっても助かったはずだ」と指摘。さらに「ルール上は頭頂部を叩き、口頭でしっかりと伝えないとダメなんだ」と語り、アピールとして不十分だった現実を解説した。
（Full-Count編集部）

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Padres Predicted to Land Tarik Skubal in Blockbuster Offseason Move
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine
item.description: The San Diego Padres were able to get into the playoffs after what was a shaky start to the 2026 MLB season, but the team fell short of its goal to win the World Series. San Diego lost in four games to the Milwaukee Brewers, seeing another year go by without a title, sending this team into a crucial offseason. The Padres' front office will have a lot to figure out this offseason, especially within the starting rotation, with key players hitting free agency. Padres Linked With Tarik Skubal One na
item.content:encoded:
The San Diego Padres were able to get into the playoffs after what was a shaky start to the 2026 MLB season, but the team fell short of its goal to win the World Series.
San Diego lost in four games to the Milwaukee Brewers, seeing another year go by without a title, sending this team into a crucial offseason. The Padres' front office will have a lot to figure out this offseason, especially within the starting rotation, with key players hitting free agency.
Padres Linked With Tarik Skubal
One name that has started to generate some buzz around the Padres as the offseason gets going is ace Tarik Skubal, who split time with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Detroit Tigers. San Diego could look to go after Skubal, giving their rotation a major boost for the future.
MLB analyst Zachary D. Rymer of Bleacher Report recently ranked landing spots for Skubal in a new piece. Within this, Rymer listed the Padres as a top landing spot, and the fit does make a lot of sense.
"If ever there was a way to show they mean business, it's by signing Skubal away from those darn Dodgers. Maybe it wouldn't totally undo the little brother vs. big brother dynamic between the two NL West powers, but it would give the Padres a real trump card: the best pitcher in baseball.
"Besides, the Padres are going to need Skubal if Michael King declines his $28 million player option for 2027 and becomes a free agent. Skubal is one of the few pitchers in MLB who would represent an upgrade over King, even if signing him would likely cost more than $40 million per year," Rymer wrote.
The Padres have spent a lot of money in the last few offseasons, which has backfired on this franchise at times. It has seen the team allow multiple stars to leave town, pushing back what the ceiling of this organization could be.
Skubal could change the entire starting rotation for the Padres this offseason, but he is expected to receive a deal over $300 million, if not closer to $400 million. San Diego has given out large contracts in the past, but this would be a new precedent for this team.
Should the Padres Go After Tarik Skubal?
On the field, the Padres should absolutely do whatever it takes to bring Skubal to San Diego. But the money is will be another question that this organization is going to have to grapple with.
With the new ownership in place, the Padres are expected to keep spending, but giving Skubal what he wants could be tough. San Diego has a lot of heavy contracts on the books already, and handing out another could be a big swing for this team.
Overall, the Padres will be involved in the Skubal sweepstakes, especially with how president of baseball operations A.J. Preller operates. Nobody can count out San Diego in this process, but other teams could present an easier path to give the lefty ace the type of deal that he is looking for this winter.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Padres Predicted to Land Tarik Skubal in Blockbuster Offseason Move appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] “Blake Snell Is NOT Beating The Ring Chasing Allegations” – MLB Fans React After Dodgers Veteran’s ‘Don’t Leave’ Message To Tarik Skubal
item.dc:creator: Nancy Singh
item.description: MLB fans have taken a dig at Blake Snell after the Dodgers pitcher urged Tarik Skubal to remain in Los Angeles following the team's National League Championship Series elimination. The Dodgers' bid for a third consecutive championship ended with a four-game sweep by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS. Skubal, who was traded to Los Angeles from the Detroit Tigers earlier in the season, is now set to become one of the most sought-after free agents this offseason. Following the Dodgers' elimination,
item.content:encoded:
MLB fans have taken a dig at Blake Snell after the Dodgers pitcher urged Tarik Skubal to remain in Los Angeles following the team's National League Championship Series elimination.
The Dodgers' bid for a third consecutive championship ended with a four-game sweep by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS. Skubal, who was traded to Los Angeles from the Detroit Tigers earlier in the season, is now set to become one of the most sought-after free agents this offseason.
Following the Dodgers' elimination, Snell shared his thoughts on Skubal's future in an interview with the California Post. The left-hander expressed his desire to continue playing alongside his friend and urged him not to leave the team.
"I just said, he can't leave me, especially on these terms. The goal is to win a World Series, and we weren't able to do that … So now that it's over, it's like, 'Don't leave. He's just a great human, great pitcher. Fun to learn from. Fun to have conversations with. Just talk baseball with. I would love nothing more than for him to be back," said Snell.
However, his comments drew a skeptical response from some fans on Reddit, with one user suggesting Snell was more interested in keeping a talented teammate around to improve the Dodgers' championship chances.
"Snell is NOT beating the ring-chasing allegations."
Mocking Snell's message, another user wrote:
Suggesting that Snell wants to make the chase easier, another follower penned:
Along similar lines, a few other fans chimed in:
Skubal split his 2026 season between Detroit and Los Angeles after undergoing elbow surgery that sidelined him for six weeks. Across 26 appearances, he recorded a 12-7 record with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts over 158.2 innings.
Blake Snell reflected on the Dodgers' NLCS elimination
Following the Dodgers' 6-4 loss to the Brewers in the deciding game of the NLCS on Thursday, Blake Snell acknowledged that Milwaukee had played better baseball throughout the series during his post-game interview. He also admitted that the elimination was painful but expressed confidence that the team could learn from the defeat.
"You know, we got everything we had, they're just the better team and, yeah, it's pretty true. I mean, they played really good baseball, they played better baseball than us, and no, it's just, it was a good series, you know, that was everything we had, and they're just better, but losing is never fun, and it definitely hurts, but it'll make us better. I mean, I love our team, I love everything about it honestly, so I just think we are gonna get better," said Blake Snell.
The Dodgers pitcher also expressed confidence that the team would use the offseason to improve and prepare for the 2027 campaign.

item.dc:creator: 横山尚杜

item.content:encoded:
米大リーグ、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手（32）は、ワールドシリーズ3連覇の夢が道半ばで途絶えた。3年ぶりに開幕から二刀流で臨み、紆余曲折を経たメジャー9年目のシーズン。優勝が義務付けられる強豪球団で求められる二刀流の光と影に迫る。第2回は影の部分に焦点を当てる。
大谷の左膝に異変が表面化したのは突然だった。ただ、投球では春先とは違う変化も見られていた。6月10日パイレーツ戦で二刀流出場した翌11日に打者として出場するも、左膝の違和感を訴え、七回途中で退いた。大谷はのちに、左膝の不調が投球フォームに起因することを明かした。
開幕当初は直球を軸に多彩な変化球を織り交ぜるスタイルだったが、徐々にスイーパーの割合が増加。6月10日は直球（50％）とスイーパー（37％）が9割近くを占めた。月間MVPに選出された4月は、全投球平均で35度だった腕の角度は6月に33度、最後の登板となった7月3日には31度まで低下した。4月28日に「腕が下がり気味なボールの動き方だった」と大谷自身も変化を自覚していたが、6月10日には腕の角度が下がっていることについて「直球がカット気味でゴロを打ち取れる」と肯定的な部分を強調していた。
後半戦はポストシーズンでの投手復帰を見据え、投球リハビリと並行して打者としての出場継続を決断。大谷は「出ない選択肢が一番、悪化もしない。ただ、誰しも万全な状態ではやっていない。リスクを最小限に抑えながら貢献してポストシーズンに進む」としたが、8月30日の投手復帰を見据えた2日前のブルペン投球でも違和感を拭いきれず、登板を断念した。
打者に専念した期間も打撃成績は伸びず、左膝と右上腕の不調による影響は無視できないレベルに達していた。だが、球団の〝介入〟は明らかに遅かった。8月下旬の敵地タイガース戦では、両腕が連動せず、上体が浮き上がるようなスイングに明白な危険信号が表れていた。それでも球団は出場を続けさせた。9月上旬に負傷者リスト（IL）入りする頃には、ポストシーズンまでに回復する時間も十分に残されていなかった。
