However, they have never beaten their postseason final boss during this era, getting eliminated by the Dodgers in seven games in the instant classic 2018 NLCS before getting swept in the 2020 NL Wild Card Series and 2025 NLCS. MLB Playoff Roundup: Bauers leads Brewers’ bl
item.content:encoded:
Is this finally the year the Brewers exorcise their playoff demons and advance past the Dodgers on the Senior Circuit side of the bracket? Alongside LA, Milwaukee has been the class of the NL regular season for the last decade. However, they have never beaten their postseason final boss during this era, getting eliminated by the Dodgers in seven games in the instant classic 2018 NLCS before getting swept in the 2020 NL Wild Card Series and 2025 NLCS.
MLB Playoff Roundup: Bauers leads Brewers’ blasts on brink of World Series
Milwaukee is on the cusp of sweeping the Dodgers and making their second World Series appearance in franchise history.
That finally looks set to change, the Brewers taking a commanding 3-0 lead in the series on a brilliant start from Robert Gasser and home runs from Jackson Chourio, Jake Bauers, and Garrett Mitchell. With one more win, they’ll not only avenge those losses, but also win their first pennant in 44 years, when Harvey’s Wallbangers led the 1982 Brewers to the AL flag. Only the Pirates and Mariners have waited longer for a World Series berth. Could this be the year at last for dreams of a first Brewers championship to truly ignite?
They have one more win to go. Here’s how they got to the doorstep.
NLCS Game 3
Milwaukee Brewers 5, Los Angeles Dodgers 2
(Milwaukee leads, 3-0)
There is no better start to the game as a visiting team than a leadoff home run to put the home starter and crowd immediately on the back foot. Chourio said “hold my beer” as he homered on the first pitch of Game 3, ambushing a center-cut four-seamer from Blake Snell and lining it oppo just over the wall in right-center to instantly deflate a raucous crowd at Chavez Ravine who had been desperate to energize their wounded Dodgers. It is already the third postseason leadoff home run in the young career of the Brewers’ star left fielder, Chourio the hero of the NLDS against the Padres with six RBIs in four games.
Gasser typifies a Milwaukee Brewers player — a gamer with plenty of talent but not a name a baseball fan outside of Wisconsin is likely to recognize. He was part of the 2022 deadline trade that sent Josh Hader to San Diego. He debuted in 2024 but missed most of that and the next season to Tommy John surgery. He spent the first month-and-a-half of 2026 at Triple-A but didn’t look back after a mid-May call-up, starting 20 games and posting a 5-5 record, 3.87 ERA, 4.23 FIP, 103 strikeouts and 1.5 fWAR in 109.1 innings.
With the Brewers unsettled on their postseason rotation plans, Gasser allowed one or fewer runs in his final four starts of the regular season to cement his starting role in the playoffs. The 27-year-old lefty held the Padres to a run on three hits in four innings of Game 4 of the NLDS as the Brewers punched their ticket to the next round. Against this backdrop of hitting his stride once the games really started to matter, Gasser pitched possibly the best start of his life last night.
He’s not going to blow you away with velocity, but the unique way he hides the ball until the last moment of his delivery let his mid-90s sinker play up in LA. The Dodgers had no answer for the pitch as Gasser was able to paint both sides of the plate, getting the ball by the dangerous hitters in their lineup as if they collectively were not ready to hit the fastball.
Gasser waltzed through five scoreless innings allowing just three hits and a walk, but cameras curiously spotted handshakes in the dugout between the fifth and sixth innings. Gasser hadn’t had to make a stressful pitch all game and seemed to have plenty in the tank at just 72 pitches, but trainers did appear to be tending to a blister on the ring finger of his pitching hand. Practically every button that Brewers manager Pat Murphy has pushed this season and postseason has worked, seeing the team pace MLB with 103 wins and easily brush aside the Padres in the NLDS before taking a 2-0 lead over the two-time reigning champions, but this one blew up in his face.
Whatever the case, Murphy called on Abner Uribe for the sixth inning and it backfired spectacularly. He walked Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker, and Shohei Ohtani (batting a rare sixth amid his awful slump) to load the bases with one out. Despite a pair of relievers hot in the Milwaukee bullpen, Murphy allowed Uribe to face the struggling Will Smith — 1-for-23 in six games this postseason. Smith ambushed a first pitch sinker right down the pipe, the deep fly ball clanging halfway up the wall in left-center to plate a pair and give the Dodgers their first lead of the series, 2-1.
Murphy belatedly called on flame throwing lefty DL Hall to clean up Uribe’s mess, and he struck out Kiké Hernández and Tommy Edman to strand runners on second and third and limit the damage to the two runs.
Murphy was perhaps vindicated in lifting his starter earlier than it seemed necessary, because we witnessed the flip side of that debate two innings later. It is perhaps fitting that Snell was the starter opposite Gasser in this game —the Rays’ Kevin Cash memorably removed Snell in the sixth inning of Game 6 of the 2020 World Series against the Dodgers despite Snell having struck out nine and not allowed a run on just 73 pitches — Gasser removed with his pitch count at 72.
After the Chourio leadoff blast, Snell was untouchable for six innings, allowing one hit and one walk while striking out nine as his four-seamer had some extra juice en route to racking up a gaudy 46-percent whiff rate. Dave Roberts allowed his dominating starter to come back out for the seventh, and it is amazing how the tide turned in an instant. He issued a leadoff walk to Andrew Vaughn, but with two lefties due up in Bauers and Mitchell, Roberts stuck with his southpaw starter.
The fatigue was apparent against Bauers, Snell’s misses occurring over the heart of the plate instead of outside of the zone, and the Brewers’ regular season home run leader won the monumental 11-pitch battle by blasting a middle-middle full count four-seamer 412 feet to right to put the Brewers back on top, 3-2. Mitchell then jumped on a 1-0 mistake changeup right down the middle, going back-to-back with Bauers to almost the exact same spot of the ballpark.
It was the first time in Snell’s entire career that he had allowed back-to-back homers to lefties and just the second time that he’d ever allowed two lefty-hitter homers in the same game (let alone inning). He’d allowed one lefty-hitter homer since Juan Soto took him deep for the Yankees in June 2024 in San Francisco.
That fully sucked all of the air out of Dodger Stadium, and the team nor their fans could will the comeback. Milwaukee added a pair of valuable insurance runs in the eighth and ninth. Brice Turang and William Contreras reached in the eighth on consecutive one-out singles to put runners on the corners where a Justin Wrobleski wild pitch allowed Turang to score the Brewers’ fifth run. Rookie Cooper Pratt lined a one-out single in the ninth, stole second, and scored on a Joey Ortiz single to make it 6-2. Hall and closer Trevor Megill combined to pitch a scoreless final 3.2 innings to seal the win and put the Brewers on the brink of sweeping the champions of the last two seasons.
Game 4 is tomorrow with first pitch scheduled for 8:00 pm ET. Tyler Glasnow will look to keep the Dodgers’ season alive while Milwaukee has yet to name a starter. The Brewers now have four chances to clinch the series and advance to the Fall Classic, where they will look to win their first ever title as one of five teams to have never won a ring. No expansion team has waited longer. It may finally be the Brew Crew’s year.

item.title: [Sports Business Journal] Dodgers’ Alex Call gets cheers after Sydney Sweeney ad remarks stir debate
item.description: Dodgers LF Alex Call “received a warm welcome from fans” at Dodger Stadium hours after he “made some controversial remarks about risqué advertisements that have been running during MLB games,” according to Edward Lewis of the N.Y. POST. Call was introduced to the crowd before Game 3 of the NLCS on Wednesday, and several fans “got out of their seat to cheer him on.” Call first “pleaded for an end to the racy MLB advertisements, some of which featured a nearly nude Sydney Sweeney promoting predict
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers LF Alex Call “received a warm welcome from fans” at Dodger Stadium hours after he “made some controversial remarks about risqué advertisements that have been running during MLB games,” according to Edward Lewis of the N.Y. POST. Call was introduced to the crowd before Game 3 of the NLCS on Wednesday, and several fans “got out of their seat to cheer him on.”
Call first “pleaded for an end to the racy MLB advertisements, some of which featured a nearly nude Sydney Sweeney promoting prediction market Novig, on his Twitter page” on Tuesday. He described them as “soft porn.”
Call wrote: “Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB? My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked women [sic] could come on screen anytime??” The post was “met with mixed reviews,” and Call has “yet to further address his statement” (N.Y. POST, 10/14).

item.title: [Yahoo] Fans de los Dodgers apoyan la postura de Alex Call tras la polémica con Sydney Sweeney
item.dc:creator: Tom Malley
item.description: Los fanáticos de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles no permitieron que los recientes comentarios de Alex Call sobre los comerciales de "pornografía suave" afectaran su apoyo hacia él antes del Juego 3 de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional el miércoles, ya que lo vitorearon como de costumbre durante la presentación de los jugadores. Call, de 32 años, causó revuelo esta semana cuando comentó una publicación viral de X que criticaba los anuncios que se emiten durante los partidos de los playoffs de
item.content:encoded:
Los fanáticos de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles no permitieron que los recientes comentarios de Alex Call sobre los comerciales de "pornografía suave" afectaran su apoyo hacia él antes del Juego 3 de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional el miércoles, ya que lo vitorearon como de costumbre durante la presentación de los jugadores.
Call, de 32 años, causó revuelo esta semana cuando comentó una publicación viral de X que criticaba los anuncios que se emiten durante los partidos de los playoffs de la MLB, afirmando que los padres no deberían tener que preocuparse de que "una mujer semidesnuda" aparezca en la pantalla en cualquier momento.
Las declaraciones del jardinero derecho de los Dodgers se producen tras semanas de controversia en torno a las atrevidas campañas publicitarias de la actriz de primera línea Sydney Sweeney con la empresa de pronósticos Novig, en las que aparece con poca ropa, y en algunos casos completamente desnuda, mientras se cubre estratégicamente con equipamiento deportivo.
Esta semana, los aficionados que sintonizaban los playoffs de la MLB se vieron expuestos a un anuncio sobre disfunción eréctil protagonizado por Megan Fox y el spot de Novig de Sweeney, respaldado por los dueños de la compañía, lo que provocó varias quejas de padres en internet.
Una de esas quejas llamó la atención de Call, quien respondió con su propia publicación argumentando que la MLB no necesitaba trucos para atraer a los espectadores más jóvenes, sino simplemente una transmisión que las familias pudieran seguir viendo cómodamente.
Dodgers outfielder Alex Call was cheered during the player introductions of Game 3 of the NLCS in the wake of his recent comments about MLB ads. https://t.co/9pePuNriDK pic.twitter.com/lXB5pT8hAZ
— California Post Sports (@capostsports) October 15, 2026
"¿Podemos, por favor, quitar los anuncios sugerentes de las transmisiones de los playoffs en TBS, Fox, NBC y la MLB?", escribió Call. "Mi hijo quiere ver béisbol con papá, pero ¿cómo lo justifico cuando una mujer semidesnuda podría aparecer en pantalla en cualquier momento? Este es el pasatiempo nacional de Estados Unidos. Los padres no deberían tener que preocuparse por esto".
Call recibió mucho apoyo por su mensaje, con muchos fanáticos de acuerdo con su postura y exigiendo que algo cambiara, y esos sentimientos hacia la estrella de los Dodgers ciertamente se transmitieron a las gradas el miércoles antes del choque del Juego 3 de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional de su equipo contra los Milwaukee Brewers.
En un video grabado desde las gradas y publicado en X, se podía ver a Call, quien no había aparecido en un partido de postemporada hasta el momento, a pesar de estar en la plantilla activa de los Dodgers, alineándose junto a sus compañeros en el campo del Dodger Stadium mientras se leían los nombres de los jugadores.
Tras una gran ovación para el tercera base de los Dodgers, Max Clusty, el nombre de Call fue el siguiente en la lista a ser anunciado, y se podía oír claramente a los aficionados dándole una cálida bienvenida mientras él saludaba cortésmente a la multitud.
Poco después, algunos aficionados acusaron a Joe Davis, de FOX Sports, de haber hecho la "peor narración de la historia" tras ser sorprendido en plena presentación cuando Jackson Chourio conectó un jonrón en el primer lanzamiento del tercer partido de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional.
El comentarista de FOX estaba dando sus palabras de apertura antes del partido cuando Chourio sorprendió al primer lanzamiento del juego, enviando una bola rápida de 98 mph de Blake Snell a las gradas del jardín derecho para darle a los Brewers una ventaja de 1-0.
Desafortunadamente para todos los seguidores de Los Ángeles, el equipo no pudo lograr la victoria contra los Brewers, cayendo 6-2 y quedando abajo 3-0 en la serie al mejor de siete, al borde de la eliminación.
Eso convierte el cuarto partido de esta noche (jueves 15 de octubre), programado en el Dodger Stadium, en una victoria imprescindible para los Dodgers si quieren tener alguna posibilidad de lograr una remontada memorable, ya que otra derrota confirmaría el final de su temporada.

item.title: [The Daily Beast] MLB Star Hits Out at Sydney Sweeney’s ‘Soft Porn Ads’
item.dc:creator: Reagin von Lehe
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Alex Call called on Major League Baseball and its broadcast partners to remove what he called “soft porn” ads from 2026 playoff telecasts. The callout was in response to an MLB fan on X, Taylor Murphy, who went viral after posting that the MLB could get younger kids watching if it aired ads that made parents comfortable leaving the TV on unattended. “Wanna get more kids watching baseball? Maybe start with the commercials,” Murphy said. When trying to watch the prog
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Alex Call called on Major League Baseball and its broadcast partners to remove what he called “soft porn” ads from 2026 playoff telecasts.
The callout was in response to an MLB fan on X, Taylor Murphy, who went viral after posting that the MLB could get younger kids watching if it aired ads that made parents comfortable leaving the TV on unattended.
“Wanna get more kids watching baseball? Maybe start with the commercials,” Murphy said.
When trying to watch the program with his kids, ads of Megan Fox selling erectile dysfunction pills in a red bodysuit, “the scariest movie trailer you’ve ever seen,” and Sydney Sweeney in “zero clothes” promoting sports betting aired between plays.
He continued, saying the MLB doesn’t need a Savannah Bananas gimmick or a Nickelodeon-style game. The league can simply “show baseball in a way I can leave on in my house.”
Call, a father of two, agreed with Murphy on X.
“Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts—TBS, Fox, NBC—@MLB?” Call wrote. “My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked woman could come on screen anytime?”
This is the sports world’s latest snub of Sweeney over her ad for the sports-prediction market Novig. She’s filmed talking about the “just sports” betting platform and covering her naked body with various sports equipment.
Female athletes and celebrities have responded, calling the ad “damaging” to women’s sports.
Four-time Olympic swimming champion Ariarne Titmus said it “monetizes” women’s bodies, while former UCLA gymnast Gracie Kramer said female athletes have long fought to be seen for their performance rather than their bodies.
Sprinter Amy Hunt, water-polo player Tilly Kearns, and rugby player Sofie Fella also all pushed back on the ad.
Novig CEO Jack Fortinsky defended the campaign, saying the company is “hugely supportive of women’s sports,” never intended to portray female athletes, and viewed Sweeney simply as an actress delivering a sports-focused message.
Though she hasn’t responded to Call directly, Sweeney publicly said she filmed the ad because she believes in the company’s leadership and message.
Murphy and Call received mixed responses, with parents supporting the take and others saying kids “aren’t the target audience” and the MLB doesn’t control the ads that play between programming. To which Murphy replied with a highlighted screenshot from a 2024 MLB advertising standards document.
The MLB reserves the right to “reject or instruct” any partner to cease the use of any ad “during, or in connection with, any Baseball Programming Transmission,” according to the document.
Call concluded his X rant with, “This is America’s Pastime. Parents shouldn’t have to worry about this.”
Obsessed with pop culture and entertainment? Follow us on Substack and YouTube for even more coverage.

"Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB?" the Los Angeles Dodgers player wrote on X Wednesday, Oct. 14, in response to a
item.content:encoded:
NEED TO KNOW
- Alex Call is taking issue with suggestive ads that air during MLB games
- The Dodgers outfielder shared his outrage on X in a post
- "Parents shouldn't have to worry about this," Call, who is not on the team's postseason roster, said
Alex Call is calling foul on recent commercials that he says feature "half-naked women."
"Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB?" the Los Angeles Dodgers player wrote on X Wednesday, Oct. 14, in response to a post discussing the trend. "My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked women could come on screen anytime?? This is America's Pastime. Parents shouldn't have to worry about this."
Call's response was to a post in which a Utah-based X user shared his displeasure with commercials that star Sydney Sweeney and Megan Fox.
Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB? My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked women could come on screen anytime?? This is America’s Pastime. Parents shouldn’t have to worry about this. https://t.co/7YAWSZgo5d
— Alex Call (@ACAD_27) October 14, 2026
In addition to the 32-year-old outfielder, female athletes are among those outraged by Sweeney's sports-betting ad for Novig.
In the commercials, the Euphoria actress, 29, bares almost all while posing in provocative positions.
"Just you, your takes and sports," Sweeney, topless and holding her breasts, says into the camera.
Call — who was left off the Dodgers' postseason roster — has had time to watch games at home with his family amid the team's playoff run.
The right fielder also made headlines earlier this season for his position — in which he nearly injured Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani.
In July, Call clipped Ohtani's right elbow with his cleat while jumping over the dugout railing to celebrate the team's win against the Philadelphia Phillies.
Ohtani, 32, briefly clutched his elbow before the two players laughed off the near-miss.
Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!
On Wednesday night, the designated hitter managed a single in two at bats amid a self-owned slump triggered by lingering injuries.
"The symptoms shouldn't be the reason why I can't hit," Ohtani told reporters through his interpreter on Tuesday, Oct. 13. "The results, [I] take full responsibility."
The Dodgers will try to stave off elimination on Friday, Oct. 16 for Game 5, when they face the Milwaukee Brewers, who will earn a trip to the World Series with a win.

item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are facing an uphill battle in the 2026 National League Championship Series after Blake Snell failed to rescue his team in Game 3 on Wednesday. The Dodgers ace struggled to silence Milwaukee’s relentless bats, and perhaps no one personified that better than Brewers slugger Jake Bauers. The Milwaukee first baseman put on a batting masterclass in the seventh inning at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles, Calif., battling Snell in an epic 11-pitch at-bat that featured five foul ba
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are facing an uphill battle in the 2026 National League Championship Series after Blake Snell failed to rescue his team in Game 3 on Wednesday.
The Dodgers ace struggled to silence Milwaukee’s relentless bats, and perhaps no one personified that better than Brewers slugger Jake Bauers.
The Milwaukee first baseman put on a batting masterclass in the seventh inning at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles, Calif., battling Snell in an epic 11-pitch at-bat that featured five foul balls before launching a go-ahead home run.
Every pitch from that UNREAL Jake Bauers at-bat 😤 11 pitches. One unforgettable moment. https://t.co/QpDMUMMPFP
— MLB (@MLB) October 15, 2026
That home run was followed by another solo blast off Snell from Brewers outfielder Garrett Mitchell.
That prompted Snell’s exit from the mound, as the Brewers went on to win the game, 6-2, for a commanding 3-0 series lead.
Despite his struggles against the Brewers, Snell gave props to his former teammate.
“I’ve known him since he got drafted with San Diego, then he was with the Rays. I was with him for
probably four years, something like that,” Snell said of Bauers, via Alden González of ESPN.
“I’ve seen all the ups and downs he’s been through and it’s been a lot of downs. So for him to go through this right now, he’s earned it. Hat’s off to him. I mean, what an at- bat. I threw everything I had. Fastball down the middle. If I can locate that better, who knows what would happen. It’s the best I’ve ever seen him play. It’s a good at-bat. Hat’s off to him.”
In six innings of work, Snell allowed four earned runs on four hits (three home runs), but racked up nine strikeouts through 101 pitches.
Unless the Dodgers find a way to overcome a 3-0 series deficit against Milwaukee, Snell has likely thrown his last pitch of 2026.

item.title: [FanSided] Freddie Freeman’s October collapse should put any Braves regret to bed
item.dc:creator: Zachary Rotman
item.description: In the 2021 offseason, the Atlanta Braves made the controversial decision to let Freddie Freeman, a franchise legend who had just led the team to a World Series title, walk in free agency. Freeman received a six-year, $162 million offer from the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Braves famously did not want to give the legend a sixth guaranteed year. Even though the Braves acquired an All-Star, Matt Olson, to replace him, many Braves fans were infuriated with the organization for letting a player of
item.content:encoded:
In the 2021 offseason, the Atlanta Braves made the controversial decision to let Freddie Freeman, a franchise legend who had just led the team to a World Series title, walk in free agency. Freeman received a six-year, $162 million offer from the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Braves famously did not want to give the legend a sixth guaranteed year. Even though the Braves acquired an All-Star, Matt Olson, to replace him, many Braves fans were infuriated with the organization for letting a player of Freeman's stature go.
There have been times when letting Freeman walk has looked bad. He's been a great player in L.A. most of the time he's been there, and has had several iconic moments in Dodger Blue, including a pair of walk-off home runs in the World Series. How's this decision looking now, though? The decision to let Freeman walk and replace him with Olson looks better and better by the day, with Freeman's decline playing a major role.
Freddie Freeman is not the superstar he once was
Freeman was performing at a superstar level in the first four years of his contract with the Dodgers, hitting .310 with a .907 OPS with more postseason moments to remember than we can count. This season, however, he hit .288 with a career-low .792 OPS in the regular season, and somehow, it feels like only been regressing as the year has progressed. Freeman hit just one home run and had a .681 OPS in the second half of the regular season, and while he hit a couple of home runs in the NLDS against Atlanta, he's 5-for-26 (.192 BA) in the postseason overall, and 1-for-11 in the NLCS. Freeman has no-showed when the Dodgers have needed him most, alongside many of his star teammates.
It's easy to blame Freeman for his performance, but it's also worth noting that he's 37 years old. Father Time is undefeated at the end of the day, and that's exactly why the Braves were hesitant when it came to giving Freeman, who was already over the age of 30 while playing a position that historically doesn't age well, such a long deal.
Now, the Dodgers not only have to watch Freeman look overmatched with their season and three-peat on the line, but they have Freeman locked in for another year. If Freeman is declining at age 37, how will he look when he's a year older? Meanwhile, the Braves have Matt Olson, who is very much in his prime.
Matt Olson is making it easy for the Braves to forget all about Freddie Freeman
Olson has been just as good, if not better, than Freeman since the two changed teams ahead of the 2022 campaign. Sure, he isn't the contact hitter Freeman is, but Olson has hit at least 29 home runs, driven in 90 runs, and appeared in 162 games in each of his five seasons in Atlanta. He quite literally hasn't missed a single regular-season game since joining his hometown team. Since being traded to the Braves, Olson leads the majors in games played (810), ranks fifth in home runs (187) and third in RBI (528). Is that good? Oh, he's also made three All-Star teams, won a Silver Slugger, and he's a finalist to win his second Gold Glove in a Braves uniform. Again, is that good?
His postseason numbers have admittedly not measured up, and that's absolutely an issue, but is there really an argument regarding who the better player is overall right now? Olson is better, five years younger, cheaper (Olson makes $21 million annually while Freeman makes $27 million per year), and he's signed for longer, giving Atlanta more stability. Freeman will be a free agent after the 2027 campaign, while Olson is locked in through 2029 (with a club option for 2030). By that point, Olson will be 35 or 36 when he hits free agency, while Freeman is already older than that right now.
It's never easy to watch a franchise legend walk, and Braves fans have had to do just that with Freeman, Max Fried and Dansby Swanson, to name a few, in recent years. However, while you can argue that Fried and Swanson should've been brought back, can Braves fans really deny that Olson is an upgrade over Freeman at this point?
There're plenty of things the Braves should regret. Having Olson, a 32-year-old who might be the best overall player at his position right now, over Freeman, a 37-year-old in a steep decline, is not one of them.

item.title: [1069thefox.com] Brewers stun Dodgers with back-to-back homers in 7th inning and ride 6-2 win to 3-0 lead in NLCS - 106.9 The Fox

Maybe they were saving their biggest swings for the Los Angeles Dodgers. item.content:encoded:
By BETH HARRIS AP Sports Writer
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Milwaukee Brewers hit the second-fewest home runs in baseball during the regular season, even as they topped the majors with 103 wins.
Maybe they were saving their biggest swings for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell launched back-to-back homers off Blake Snell in the seventh inning, and the Brewers beat the Dodgers 6-2 on Wednesday to build a 3-0 cushion in the National League Championship Series.
Jackson Chourio also went deep on the first pitch of the game to help the Brewers close within one win of their first NL pennant. Milwaukee was in the American League when the franchise reached its only World Series, a seven-game loss to the St. Louis Cardinals in 1982.
“Job’s not finished yet,” Mitchell said.
Game 4 is Thursday at Dodger Stadium, where the Brewers can become the first major league club to complete a postseason sweep after getting swept by that same opponent in the previous postseason.
Los Angeles took all four games against Milwaukee in the NLCS last year.
The Dodgers had just gone ahead 2-1 in the sixth inning before getting stunned by the Brewers in their three-run seventh. The loss pushed the two-time defending World Series champions to the brink of elimination.
“All three games we’ve played so far, and hopefully that continues, where just every time they score, we come back and score,” Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy said. “That’s not easy to do in baseball.”
It was the fifth comeback victory in seven postseason games for the Brewers, who have never beaten Los Angeles in three previous playoff series.
The only other time the Dodgers trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series, they were swept by the Baltimore Orioles in the 1966 World Series.
The lone team in big league history to come back from a 3-0 deficit to win a best-of-seven postseason series was the Boston Red Sox in the 2004 AL Championship Series against the New York Yankees.
“We’ve won four in a row a number of times this year,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “We’ve got to win tomorrow. That’s our only focus.”
Coming into the seventh, Snell had retired 14 batters in a row. But the first pitch of the game thrown by the two-time Cy Young Award winner was hit for a home run by Chourio, and his last pitch was Mitchell’s solo shot.
Andrew Vaughn drew a seven-pitch walk to open the seventh and was replaced by pinch-runner Christian Yelich. Bauers followed with a 412-foot drive to right field on the 11th pitch of his at-bat for a 3-2 lead as most of the players in Milwaukee’s dugout came onto the field to celebrate.
“I was looking for a fastball, and I didn’t want to miss it,” said Bauers, who had a team-leading 26 of Milwaukee’s 154 regular-season homers.
It was his latest relentless plate appearance, too, after Bauers drew a 12-pitch walk from Yoshinobu Yamamoto that helped the Brewers go ahead early in Game 2.
“I think what changed for me this year was I stopped caring about results,” Bauers said. “I started caring about competing. I started caring about being in the moment and getting out of my own way.”
Watching Bauers work over Snell was “super sick,” Mitchell said.
And then it was his turn.
Mitchell’s drive traveled 428 feet to right-center. That chased Snell, who hadn’t given up a home run in 46 1/3 innings this year entering the game. It was the first time in his career he served up back-to-back homers to left-handed hitters and only the second time he gave up multiple longballs to left-handed batters in one game.
Bauers and Mitchell became just the third pair of left-handed hitters with consecutive postseason home runs off the same left-handed pitcher. Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper did it for Philadelphia against Atlanta reliever Dylan Lee in an NL Wild Card Series this year, and Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig connected for the New York Yankees off Bill Sherdel of the St. Louis Cardinals in the 1928 World Series.
Milwaukee has five homers in the NLCS and eight this postseason.
Snell gave up four runs and four hits in six-plus innings. He struck out nine and walked two.
The Brewers extended their lead to 5-2 in the eighth on Justin Wrobleski’s wild pitch that scored Brice Turang, who reached on an infield single and advanced to third on William Contreras’ single. They added another run on Joey Ortiz’s two-strike RBI single in the ninth.
The offensively starved Dodgers took a 2-1 lead on Will Smith’s two-run double off reliever Abner Uribe in the sixth.
After rookie starter Robert Gasser pitched five shutout innings, Uribe entered and loaded the bases on walks to Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Shohei Ohtani. Smith, who was 1 for 25 in the playoffs, doubled off the left-center fence with one out for his first hit of the NLCS.
DL Hall took over from Uribe and stranded runners at second and third by striking out pinch-hitter Kiké Hernández and Tommy Edman.
Hall allowed one hit in 2 1/3 scoreless innings to improve to 3-0 in these playoffs. Trevor Megill got four outs for his second save of the series and fourth this postseason.
The Dodgers played from behind again after the 22-year-old Chourio connected for his third career leadoff homer in the postseason as fans were still heading to their seats.
After that, Mitchell walked and Cooper Pratt singled in the second before Snell retired 14 in a row — six on strikeouts — before getting hammered in the seventh.
The Dodgers had runners on base in all but three innings, but couldn’t get enough across. They have yet to homer in the NLCS and are 3 for 32 with runners in scoring position this postseason.
Ohtani was 1 for 2 with a walk while hitting sixth in the order, the lowest he’s batted since joining the Dodgers three years ago.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here

item.title: [amNewYork] Mets rumors: Is Tarik Skubal a legitimate target? | amNewYork

item.content:encoded:
The prospect of Tarik Skubal becoming the Mets’ next big free-agent signing is already dancing in the head of some members of the organization.
Zac Thornton spoke with Mike Puma of the New York Post earlier this week and admitted that it’s a hot topic of conversation with his teammates.
“I talk to [Nolan McLean] all the time about it, and he had some good talks with Skubal when they were in the [World Baseball Classic] together,” Thornton told Puma. “It would be awesome to bounce ideas, especially coming from another left-handed pitcher. Sean [Manaea] and I talk a lot, just about being lefties — there are not many around here, so it would be awesome to have another powerhouse left-handed pitcher around here.”
Even with a young core of promising arms like McLean, Thornton, Christian Scott, and Jonah Tong, president of baseball operations David Stearns made it clear in his end-of-season availability that “it is necessary for us to add to our rotation.”
Skubal would provide the bona fide veteran ace Freddy Peralta never became after his half season in Queens—though he certainly looks the part with the Tampa Bay Rays, who are battling the Cleveland Guardians in the ALCS.
Regardless, the left-handed Skubal will be the crown jewel of the free agent market this winter. The two-time defending American League Cy Young Award winner was dealt from the Detroit Tigers to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the trade deadline and remained his dominant self, going 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA and 1.048 WHIP.
Over his last three seasons, Skubal is 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA and 655 strikeouts in 546 innings pitched.
With a lockout looming, which could potentially carry a salary cap that will limit player salaries, Skubal will likely sign quickly — and that deal will be historic. He is projected to sign the richest contract for a free-agent pitcher ever, which should exceed $300 million.
Whether Stearns would be intrigued by doling out such an offer might not be as cut-and-dry as many might initially think.
Yes, the Mets’ president of baseball operations has had an aversion to handing out long-term big-money contracts to pitchers, which is understandable given the fragility of many major-league arms and the seemingly never-ending onslaught of injuries that come with it.
Skubal himself missed a month earlier this season when he had to undergo surgery to remove loose bodies from his pitching elbow.
But Stearns has gone to the negotiating table with a big-money contract offer for a starting pitcher while with the Mets. He offered Yoshinobu Yamamoto a 12-year, $325 million deal in December of 2023, but the Japanese superstar took an identical deal to join the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Skubal would certainly fit the mold of coaxing such an offer from Stearns, especially if it means that the Mets are that much closer to legitimate contention in 2027, if there is baseball.

item.description: The Dodgers are one loss away from getting swept in the postseason for the first time since the 2023 NLDS against the Diamondbacks. No matter how you want to slice it, they’ve looked inferior in every facet of the game in this series, from situational hitting to defense, bullpen work, and so on—now it’ll be up to Tyler Glasnow to at the very least delay what appears to be an unavoidable postseason exit for the reigning back-to-back champs. item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are one loss away from getting swept in the postseason for the first time since the 2023 NLDS against the Diamondbacks. No matter how you want to slice it, they’ve looked inferior in every facet of the game in this series, from situational hitting to defense, bullpen work, and so on—now it’ll be up to Tyler Glasnow to at the very least delay what appears to be an unavoidable postseason exit for the reigning back-to-back champs.
Although the Brewers have yet to formally announce a starter, all signs point towards Dustin May taking the ball in Game 4 of this series—it might be with an opener, or it might be with him as a starter; either way, the bulk innings role will belong to the former Dodger.
When it comes to lineup decisions, Max Muncy figures to regain a starting role at third base, and you have to wonder if Will Smith remains in the seventh spot—the Dodger catcher was responsible for the only big hit the home team had in a Game 3 loss. Speaking of hitters who moved down in the order, although it amounted to very little, Shohei Ohtani reached safely in three of his four plate appearances in a 6-2 defeat.
Neither Evan Phillips nor Roki Sasaki had especially lengthy appearances off the bullpen, so apart from Justin Wrobleski, there’ll be no one else unavailable in the bullpen for Game 4. With nothing to lose and following the seventh-inning debacle of leaving Blake Snell in too long, expect potential aggressive calls to the bullpen at the first sign of trouble for Glasnow.
NLCS Game 4 info
- Teams: No. 2 seed Dodgers vs. No. 1 seed Brewers
- Series: Milwaukee leads, 3-0
- Ballpark: Dodger Stadium, Los Angeles
- Start time: 5:08 p.m.
- TV: FS1 (Joe Davis, John Smoltz, Ken Rosenthal, Tom Verducci)
- National radio: ESPN Radio (Jon Sciambi, Doug Glanville)
- Local English radio: AM 570 (Charley Steiner, Rick Monday)
- Local Spanish radio: KTNQ 1020 AM (José Mota, Luis Cruz)

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Max Muncy Puts Dodgers' Problems Plainly
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are now down 3-0 to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, and Dodgers veteran Max Muncy knows exactly why that is. Wednesday night was a frustrating loss in which the Dodgers finally seemed to fix their offensive woes, only for star pitcher Blake Snell to implode with back-to-back home runs in the seventh inning. Max Muncy sounds off on the Dodgers Muncy, the third baseman, was asked by reporters what has been going on with the team’s offensive
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are now down 3-0 to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, and Dodgers veteran Max Muncy knows exactly why that is.
Wednesday night was a frustrating loss in which the Dodgers finally seemed to fix their offensive woes, only for star pitcher Blake Snell to implode with back-to-back home runs in the seventh inning.
Max Muncy sounds off on the Dodgers
Muncy, the third baseman, was asked by reporters what has been going on with the team’s offensive struggles, and he pulled no punches.
“It’s a pretty simple answer. We’re playing like s—. They’re playing great,” he said, as reported by the California Post’s Jack Harris and other reporters.
In case you think Muncy is being hyperbolic, he’s not.
As detailed by Newsweek baseball writer J.P. Hoornstra, the Dodgers are one of 274 teams too play at least seven postseason games in a season since 1903.
Their team OPS of .572 isn’t just in the lower end of that group; it’s almost dead last.
The 2026 Dodgers are 268th, meaning only six teams have had a worse OPS in more than a century.
It’s a far cry from the powerful lineup fans expected from the back-to-back World Series champions.
In fact, the Dodgers haven’t hit a home run at all in this series against the Brewers, despite boasting power hitters like Muncy, Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and plenty of others.
What’s next for the Dodgers?
The Dodgers will try to avoid “playing like s—” for a fourth straight game on Thursday, knowing that a loss will end their season.
Tyler Glasnow is the mound for the Boys in Blue as they look to avoid the sweep.
The game will begin at 5 p.m. PT, an hour earlier than the previously announced start time of 6 p.m. PT.
Pitcher Blake Snell, who started Game 3 and gave up a pair of back-breaking home runs in the seventh inning, told reporters the team is focused on winning Thursday’s game.
“Yeah, it sucks, but it’s part of it,” he said. “How do we bounce back, how do we fight? I think that’s the most important thing, us coming together and finding a way to win.”
Do you think the Dodgers can stave off elimination on Thursday?

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dave Roberts' Blake Snell decision was the tip of the iceberg in mortifying Dodgers Game 3 loss
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins
item.description: Dave Roberts has not been at his best in the NLCS, with the Los Angeles Dodgers facing the league-best Milwaukee Brewers in a best-of-seven that's making LA's NLDS against the Atlanta Braves look like the smallest of potatoes. Contreras hit a go-ahead single on the
item.content:encoded:
Dave Roberts has not been at his best in the NLCS, with the Los Angeles Dodgers facing the league-best Milwaukee Brewers in a best-of-seven that's making LA's NLDS against the Atlanta Braves look like the smallest of potatoes.
In Game 2, Roberts had Brock Stewart intentionally walk Brice Turang in the sixth to get to the Brewers' hottest hitter in William Contreras, for seemingly no other reason than that the righty-righty matchup looked favorable on paper. Contreras hit a go-ahead single on the first pitch Stewart served him.
That was small potatoes in contrast to Game 3, where Roberts seemed to make the worst possible decision at every conceivable turn. There is, of course, leaving Blake Snell in after he walked Andrew Vaughn to lead off the seventh, which then turned into a go-ahead, two-run homer for Jake Bauers ... and then a solo homer for Garrett Mitchell for some insurance.
The Dodgers went down 6-2, and their backs are now firmly against the wall. Roberts' Snell decision is the one that's going to be remembered least fondly, but there was a parade of other choices that all but doomed LA's three-peat hopes.
Dave Roberts' Blake Snell decision is obscuring smaller mistakes that doomed the Dodgers in NLCS Game 3
Roberts' next greatest sin, perhaps, was burning Josue De Paula in the bottom of the sixth. After Will Smith broke out of his slumber to hit a bases-loaded, go-ahead double, Roberts replaced Miguel Rojas with left Josue De Paula to face righty Abner Uribe. Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy countered by bringing in lefty DL Hall, so Roberts figured he would do play 3D chess and instead offered up righty Kiké Hernández, rendering De Paula unavailable for the rest of the game. Hernández struck out swinging.
There's the fact that Roberts started Tommy Edman, who had a single hit coming into Game 3. He went 0-for-4 on Wednesday night. There's the fact that he put Justin Wrobleski, who had a 6.13 ERA in the second half and was briefly demoted to Triple-A, in the game with the Dodgers down by two. Wrobleski quickly threw a wild pitch that allowed the Brewers' fifth run to score.
It might be going a little too far to say that this showing was legacy-threatening ... but it sure does feel like that right now. Roberts, no doubt, will be appropriately self-critical if the Dodgers' postseason road comes to an end after this series, but that doesn't erase how inexplicable his decisions in Game 3 were, and that they, alone, might've doomed LA.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Max Muncy gives blunt assessment of Dodgers' performance vs. Brewers in NLCS: 'We're playing like s***'
item.dc:creator: Chris Cwik
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are suddenly in big trouble. After yet another loss Wednesday, the Dodgers find themselves down 3-0 in the National League Championship Series. With another loss, they'll be eliminated from the postseason. This wasn't the way it was supposed to be. In year's past, the Dodgers' depth and financial muscle won out against the best teams in the game. Something is different this time around and Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy thinks he knows exactly what's going on. When asked
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are suddenly in big trouble. After yet another loss Wednesday, the Dodgers find themselves down 3-0 in the National League Championship Series. With another loss, they'll be eliminated from the postseason.
This wasn't the way it was supposed to be. In year's past, the Dodgers' depth and financial muscle won out against the best teams in the game. Something is different this time around and Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy thinks he knows exactly what's going on.
When asked, Muncy summed things up succinctly saying, "We're playing like s***."
"It's a pretty simple answer: We're playing like s*** they're playing great."
Max Muncy after the Dodgers dropped Game 3 of the NLCS. pic.twitter.com/0MRmqhpnDk
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 15, 2026
Muncy, of course, made sure to give the Milwaukee Brewers credit. After lamenting his own team's struggles, Muncy added, "[The Brewers] are playing great. It's as simple as that."
Much has been made of the struggles of Dodgers two-way star Shohei Ohtani this postseason, but he wasn't the problem Wednesday. After being dropped to sixth in the batting order, Ohtani reached base three times in the contest.
His overall numbers, however, are still a problem, as Ohtani is hitting just .182 in the series. Many of his teammates have similar batting averages, including Freddie Freeman, Teoscar Hernandez and Muncy, none of whom is hitting above .192. Catcher Will Smith is hitting under .100.
While those struggles can be written off as small-sample outcomes … the NLCS is a small sample. All it takes is a few bad games from your star players to decide the outcome of a series. The Dodgers are experiencing that phenomenon right now.
Because of that, though, it won't take much for the Dodgers to claw their way back into the series. While 3-0 comebacks are highly unlikely, they are not impossible. All it would take is the Dodgers' stars hitting like they should.
Even then, that might not be enough. In order to stage a comeback, the Dodgers also need the Brewers to give them an opening, which seems unlikely given how well Milwaukee is playing right now.

item.content:encoded:
米大リーグのポストシーズン中継のテレビ広告が過激だとSNSで批判したドジャースのアレックス・コール外野手（32）が14日（日本時間15日）、ナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ第3戦の行われたドジャーススタジアムで声援を浴びた。
コールは13日、自身のSNSに「プレーオフの放送から『ソフトポルノ』のような広告を排除してくれないか」と投稿。「息子が父親と一緒に野球を見たがっている。だが、いつ画面に半裸の女性が映るかわからない状況を、どう子供に説明すればいいというのか。野球はアメリカの娯楽（過去の古き良き伝統）だ。親がこんな心配をすべきではない」と訴えた。
TBS、Fox、NBCなどの米テレビ局のポストシーズン中継のイニング間には、人気女優のシドニー・スウィーニーが出演するスポーツベットアプリ「Novig」のCMが繰り返し流れている。スウィーニーはアメフトのボール2個で胸元を隠すのみの姿で登場したり、バスケットゴールの上に全裸に近い状態で着座するなどの演出がある。
また、別のオンライン診療サービスのCMでは、女優ミーガン・フォックスが赤いボディースーツ姿で男性用医薬品「Ro Sparks」を宣伝しているほか、刺激の強いホラー映画の予告編なども同時間帯に放映されている。
コールの投稿をきっかけにネット上で論争が起き、「その広告収入が君たちの年俸を支えている」といった冷ややかな声も。一方、ブレーブスで2度の最優秀選手（MVP）に輝いたレジェンド、デール・マーフィー氏はコールと同様の意見をSNSに投稿した。
Novigは、株のようにスポーツの試合結果を金融商品として取引するアプリ。胴元（カジノ会社）が存在せず、ユーザー同士で取引が行われる。

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers' Miguel Rojas slaps LA with reality check amid 3-0 NLCS deficit vs. Brewers appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are staring at the brink of elimination, and Miguel Rojas is not sugarcoating how they got there. Los Angeles fell 6-2 to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series on Wednesday at Dodger Stadium, putting the two-time defending champions in a 3-0 series hole.
After the game, the veteran infielder offered a blunt explanation for the deficit. "To win championships, you've got to win moments. We haven't been able to do that in this series. They have," Rojas said, via MLB Network. "That's why we're 0-3 right now."
Game 3 was a perfect example. The Dodgers grabbed a 2-1 lead in the sixth inning when Will Smith lined a two-run double off Abner Uribe, and Blake Snell had retired 14 straight batters at one point after allowing a leadoff home run to Jackson Chourio on the first pitch of the game.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Milwaukee flipped it in the seventh. With a runner on, Jake Bauers won an 11-pitch battle against Snell and drilled a two-run homer to put the Brewers back in front. Garrett Mitchell followed with a solo blast, and Milwaukee tacked on runs in the eighth and ninth to pull away.
The big moments have gone the Brewers' way all series. Milwaukee won Game 1 by a 2-1 margin before taking Game 2 7-4, with its bullpen retiring all 15 Dodgers it faced to close out the second game.
The Dodgers' offense, meanwhile, has gone cold. Los Angeles has yet to hit a home run in the series, and it has struggled badly with runners in scoring position throughout the postseason.
Rojas knows the value of a big moment better than most. The 37-year-old is playing his final MLB season after returning to the Dodgers on a one-year deal, and he was one of the heroes of last year's World Series run.
Now, Los Angeles needs a lot of them in a hurry. The Dodgers have trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series only once before, when the Baltimore Orioles swept them in the 1966 World Series.
They will try to stave off elimination in Game 4 on Thursday at Dodger Stadium, with the Brewers looking to complete a sweep and clinch their first National League pennant.
Related: Dodgers' Kyle Tucker makes 1 thing clear with LA facing NLCS elimination

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Slumping star Shohei Ohtani singled after being dropped to sixth in the batting order for the Los Angeles Dodgers, whose 6-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series put them on the brink of postseason elimination Wednesday night.
It's the lowest the left-handed-hitting Ohtani has batted since joining the Dodgers three years ago on a $700 million, 10-year contract. Los Angeles manager Dave Roberts wanted to alternate right- and left-handed hitters throughout the lineup against Milwaukee's left-handed starter, Robert Gasser.
”Shohei’s all on board," Roberts said before the game. “Whatever it takes to win.”
It wasn't enough, and now the two-time defending World Series champions trail 3-0 in the best-of-seven series.
Ohtani flied out in the second inning, got hit by a pitch in the fourth and walked in the sixth before singling with two outs in the eighth. The Dodgers had runners on base in all but three innings.
“We’re just not getting those timely hits,” Roberts said afterward. “We’ve had some opportunities with guys on base, but can’t get that hit.”
Ohtani, the designated hitter, is typically atop the order, but Roberts has dropped him lower during a slump that has extended into the postseason. Ohtani has been struggling with left knee and right biceps issues for a few months, preventing the two-way star from pitching, and said before the Division Series against Atlanta that he wasn't 100% healthy.
During his six years with the Los Angeles Angels, Ohtani started games batting sixth or lower 19 times, all during the 2020 season or earlier.
Ohtani is hitting .182 (4 for 22) over seven postseason games. He has seven strikeouts, four walks and one stolen base with no RBIs and an OPS of .533.
He hasn’t homered since Aug. 18 at Colorado.
“I couldn’t imagine really kind of having the expectations that he has and falling short in a way that it’s not normal for him,” teammate Mookie Betts said before the game. “Then having to come back and be present in this postseason knowing how important he is to the boys.”
Roberts said he saw a more focused Ohtani during off-day batting practice Tuesday.
“He was determined, and that’s an understatement,” the manager said. “He was here late last night working on his swing, out with the guys and talking about things on how we're going to beat these guys.”
Dodgers pitcher Tyler Glasnow, set to start Game 4 on Thursday, said Ohtani's demeanor doesn't deviate regardless of how well he's performing.
“I think most people put in that situation, you’d have a lot more emotional volatility, so it’s just impressive to see him just be a good dude always,” Glasnow said. “I don’t think he needs reassurance or anything. He’s confident in himself. It’s just business as usual and a lot of smiles and the same laugh.”

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers' Blake Snell Explains What Went Wrong in Pivotal 7th Inning
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Blake Snell detailed what went wrong in that all-important seventh inning that turned what had been an excellent outing into disaster against the Milwaukee Brewers in the 2026 National League Championship Series. How did Blake Snell play in the NLCS? Snell started the game by giving up a home run on his first pitch, but after that, he was absolutely dominant, striking out nine batters in the next six innings. That seventh inning, though, was one to forget. The Dodgers
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Blake Snell detailed what went wrong in that all-important seventh inning that turned what had been an excellent outing into disaster against the Milwaukee Brewers in the 2026 National League Championship Series.
How did Blake Snell play in the NLCS?
Snell started the game by giving up a home run on his first pitch, but after that, he was absolutely dominant, striking out nine batters in the next six innings.
That seventh inning, though, was one to forget.
The Dodgers had just gained their first lead of the night on a two-RBI double by Will Smith in the bottom of the sixth inning, but in the top of the seventh, Snell began by walking Andrew Vaughn.
After that, Snell took on Jake Bauers for an 11-pitch at-bat that ended with a monster two-run home run.
The next batter, Garret Mitchell, also homered, quickly turning the Dodgers’ advantage into a 4-2 Brewers lead.
Snell was then pulled from the game, and Milwaukee would only add to the lead from there, creating a 3-0 series lead that will be nearly impossible for the Dodgers to overcome.
It also created a lot of questions among Dodgers fans, including how Snell’s performance yo-yoed so wildly over the course of his start.
Blake Snell breaks down what went wrong against Brewers
After the game, Snell told reporters that it’s “pretty frustrating” to give up three home runs, especially seeing as he hadn’t even given up one homer in his limited playing time this season.
“It’s something I’ve got to learn from, it’s part of their journey too, and it’s only going to make me better in the long run,” he said from the clubhouse.
Snell also discussed the Bauers at-bat, noting that he’s known Bauers for years and after the Brewer’s up-and-down career, “he’s earned it.”
“Hats off to him. What an at-bat,” he said. “I threw everything I had. Fastball down the middle, if I could locate that better, who knows what would have happened? This is the best I’ve ever seen him play. It’s a good at-bat. Hats off to him.”
Snell also addressed the Dodgers facing elimination and a possible sweep at Dodger Stadium on Thursday.
The game will begin at 5 p.m. PT, not 6 p.m. PT as originally announced.
“Yeah, it sucks, but it’s part of it,” he said. “How do we bounce back, how do we fight? I think that’s the most important thing, us coming together and finding a way to win.”

item.content:encoded:
山本由伸との「１２球・７分間」の熱闘の２日後、今度は１１球粘って逆転２ラン…バウアーズの粘り腰
完了しました
米大リーグのポストシーズン（ＰＳ）ナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ（４戦先勝方式）は１４日（日本時間１５日）の第３戦で、ブルワーズ（中地区１位）がドジャース（西地区１位）を６－２で破って３連勝とし、ワールドシリーズ進出に王手をかけた。
六回に１－２と逆転されたブルワーズは七回表無死一塁で、５番のバウアーズが好投を続けていたドジャース先発のスネルからファウルで粘って１１球目を右翼席に放り込み、この逆転２ラン本塁打が決勝弾となった。
バウアーズの殊勲の伏線は２日前の試合にあった。１２日（同１３日）の第２戦の三回、この試合で４番に入っていたバウアーズは、２走者を置いた場面でドジャースの先発、山本由伸に対して１２球粘って四球を選び、チャンスを広げて続くイエリチの逆転２点適時打を呼び込んだ。
この打席、バウアーズはフルカウントからファウルで６球粘り、緩急を織り交ぜる山本の多彩な投球にくらいついた。ＭＬＢ公式ページによると、１２球の対戦に要した時間はおよそ７分間。球数がかさんだ山本は逆転打を喫したこの回途中に７５球、３失点で降板し、間違いなく試合の流れを変えるシーンとなった。
今年３１歳のバウアーズは２０１３年のドラフト７巡目、全体２０８番目でパドレスに指名された。１８年にメジャー昇格し、ブルワーズが５球団目。主に一塁と外野を守り、ブルワーズ３年目の今季はレギュラーシーズンでメジャー自己最多の２６本塁打を打っている。（デジタル編集部）

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Dodgers collapse again, tumble into 3-0 NLCS hole against surging Brewers

item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
Blake Snell stood on the mound with his hand on his hip, waiting for Jake Bauers to cross the plate before punching in his pitch call for the next batter.
The Dodgers left-hander had just given up the lead on Bauers’ two-run homer, spoiling what had been a stellar start Wednesday night at Dodger Stadium. But Snell was ready to move on.
Two pitches later, he watched another ball fly over the fence, this time off Garrett Mitchell’s bat.
The Dodgers’ 6-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series, after the visitors regained the lead with back-to-back home runs in the seventh inning, gave the Brewers a commanding 3-0 lead and set up an elimination game Thursday. After setting their sights on a history-making three-peat, the Dodgers will have to win the next four games just to advance to the World Series.
The Dodgers showed signs of life during Game 3 of the NLCS, but Bill Plaschke writes the reigning champs can’t survive their crushing collapse.
For five innings, the only run on the board was the one the Brewers scored on the first pitch of the game.
Snell zipped a 97.6-mph fastball over the center of the plate, and Brewers leadoff hitter Jackson Chourio sent it into the first row of the stands in right-center.
For much of Snell’s start, however, that aggressive approach worked. He dotted the upper rail with his fastball, threw his curveball for both swings and misses and called strikes, and mixed in his changeup to right-handed batters.
Unlike Snell’s last postseason start, when he issued five walks and lasted just 3-2/3 innings against the Atlanta Braves, his efficiency got him through six-plus innings Wednesday, with just two walks.
And while Snell’s fastball averaged 97 mph in his last start — something he’d done only twice before in his career, regular season or postseason, and not since 2022, according to Statcast — he threw even harder on Wednesday: 97.3 mph.
After Chourio’s home run, Snell retired 18 of the next 20 batters, including 14 in a row, to get through six innings. His nine strikeouts were one shy of a postseason career high, which he recorded against the Brewers last year in Game 1 of the NLCS.
Then in the seventh inning, he issued a leadoff walk to Andrew Vaughn and surrendered back-to-back homers, and suddenly the game had flipped.
With the way the Brewers’ bullpen pitched in the first two games, it seemed the Dodgers would have to score against the Brewers’ starters to have a chance to pull themselves out of the hole they’d dug.
They failed to do so in Game 3, logging just three hits off left-hander Robert Gasser.
Luckily for them, pitching every game of the postseason seemed to finally have caught up to hard-throwing right-handed Abner Uribe in his seventh appearance.
Uribe took over for Gasser in the sixth inning and walked the first two batters he faced.
Then Dodgers manager Dave Roberts had left-handed-hitting Max Muncy pinch-hit for Andy Pages. Muncy struck out, and the biggest moment of the game fell to two Dodgers who have had the worst postseason production on the team.
Roberts had moved Shohei Ohtani down to sixth in the batting order and put Will Smith behind him. Naturally, the game found them.
Ohtani drew a five-pitch walk without taking a swing. With the bases loaded, it was up to Smith, who had gone one for 25 in the postseason to that point.
He ambushed a first-pitch sinker and drove it into the left-field gap for a two-run double and the lead.
The rally halted there. Roberts burned rookie Josue De Paula as a pinch-hitter, swapping him out for Kiké Hernández when the Brewers brought in left-hander DL Hall. Hernández and Tommy Edman struck out to end the inning.
The Dodgers could not keep pace with the Milwaukee Brewers, falling 6-2 Wednesday night in Game 3 of the NLCS and dropping to 3-0 in the series.
Then, three Brewers batters into the seventh, the Dodgers were down 4-2.
Snell hadn’t allowed a home run all year — not in his nine regular-season starts, or in his NLDS appearance. Three on Wednesday defined his start.
The next inning, the Brewers added an insurance run with back-to-back singles against right-handed reliever Roki Sasaki and a wild pitch from left-hander Justin Wrobleski. They tacked on another in the ninth with a pair of singles and a stolen base off Wrobleski.
With the flash of red tail lights flickering outside of the stadium, a sign of Dodgers fans already heading for the exits, Dodgers hitters went down in order in the final half inning.

item.title: [FanSided] 3 mistakes the Dodgers made with their money that cost them a chance at a three-peat
item.dc:creator: Zachary Rotman
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have won back-to-back World Series titles thanks largely to historic spending. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have won back-to-back World Series titles thanks largely to historic spending. A full14 players on the Dodgers' roster are making eight figures this season, and Tarik Skubal (who is making $32 million overall, but $9.5 million prorated after the Dodgers acquired him) isn't far behind from making that 15. For reference, the Mets, the team closest to L.A. payroll-wise, ended the year with just eight players making eight figures this season.
Most of those deals are ones the Dodgers would sign off on again. Even guys who have struggled this postseason, like Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts, Shohei Ohtani and Will Smith, have done so much for this team in recent years that it's hard to say the Dodgers should regret paying them. These three deals, though, are ones that the Dodgers should regret offering, now that their three-peat dreams are officially on life support.
OF Kyle Tucker
This is the obvious one. The Dodgers, even after winning back-to-back World Series titles, elected to give Kyle Tucker a four-year, $240 million deal in free agency. When that deal was signed, most MLB fans practically handed the World Series title to L.A., knowing how good Tucker had been in Houston. Instead, Tucker wound up having the worst year of his career.
He slashed .233/.330/.385 with 17 home runs and 70 RBI. He was better down the stretch and has been arguably their best hitter in the postseason, but he's just 2-for-8 in the NLCS. That's not good enough for a player making $60 million a year on average. For reference, Juan Soto's AAV is at $51 million, and he's performed at an MVP level. If the Dodgers got to do it again, they almost certainly wouldn't have made this kind of investment in Tucker.
RHP Edwin Diaz
Tucker wasn't the only high-end free agent the Dodgers signed. They gave Edwin Diaz a three-year, $69 million deal to be their closer, one year after giving Tanner Scott a four-year, $72 million deal to perform in that same role. Scott's first year in L.A. was one to forget, and Diaz followed that same path, posting an 8.68 ERA in 21 games and missing much of the season due to injury.
Diaz was better in the postseason, but given how well Scott performed this season and how lackluster this Dodgers lineup proved to be, wouldn't Andrew Friedman have preferred to give that kind of major money to a big bat? Hindsight is 20/20, but had they known the offense would look this bad in October, they likely would've spent their resources on another bat and let Diaz sign elsewhere.
OF Teoscar Hernandez
Teoscar Hernandez had a huge year in 2024, leading to the Dodgers re-signing him on a three-year, $66 million deal that offseason. That contract made some sense, but handing a power-hitting corner outfielder over the age of 30 a hefty multi-year deal has the risk of backfiring — and this one did almost immediately. Hernandez's 103 OPS+ in 2025 was his worst in a full season in his career, and while he was a bit better overall in 2026, his streakiness and his numbers against righties (.695 OPS) left a lot to be desired.
Those struggles have continued into the playoffs, with Hernandez going 5-for-26 overall and 2-for-10 in the NLCS thus far. Dave Roberts has consistently hit him in the heart of the Dodgers' order, but Hernandez has not been able to come through. There're plenty of other players making the $20+ million that Hernandez is who could've come through for L.A. offensively. With another guaranteed year on his deal, this contract feels like another one that the Dodgers regret.

item.title: [Orange County Register] Brewers push Dodgers to the brink, hit 3 homers off Blake Snell for 3-0 NLCS lead
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Reach out and feel the drywall. The Dodgers’ backs are up against it. The plucky little team that doesn’t hit home runs hit three of them off of Blake Snell on Wednesday night. The Milwaukee Brewers handed the Dodgers a 6-2 defeat in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series, pushing the back-to-back champions to the brink of elimination with the possibility of a sweep to avenge the one the Dodgers handed them last year. “It’s a pretty simple answer,” Max Muncy said when as
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Reach out and feel the drywall. The Dodgers’ backs are up against it.
The plucky little team that doesn’t hit home runs hit three of them off of Blake Snell on Wednesday night. The Milwaukee Brewers handed the Dodgers a 6-2 defeat in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series, pushing the back-to-back champions to the brink of elimination with the possibility of a sweep to avenge the one the Dodgers handed them last year.
“It’s a pretty simple answer,” Max Muncy said when asked how the Dodgers find themselves in this position. “We’re playing like (profanity). They’re playing great. It’s as simple as that. No need to overcomplicate it.”
Dreams of a three-peat on life support, the Dodgers’ thoughts now have to be on a ‘four-peat’ – it will take four consecutive victories for them to become just the second team in MLB history to come back from a 3-0 deficit to win a best-of-seven series. The 2004 Boston Red Sox (featuring a key stolen base by a reserve outfielder acquired at midseason from the Dodgers) did it in the American League Championship Series against the New York Yankees.
“If we lose, we’re done. We’ve got to go on one-game winning streaks four games in a row,” Kike’ Hernandez said.
“At the beginning of this year, we set out to do something historic,” Muncy said. “It looks like we’re going to have to make a little more history along the way if we want to accomplish that. That’s the task ahead of us. We still have the pitching staff to be able to do it. We just have to get some hits. If we can back our pitching staff then I know that, like I said, we have the pitching staff to do it.”
Tyler Glasnow is scheduled to start Game 4 on Thursday and try to save the Dodgers’ season. Muncy is correct — Glasnow won’t be able to do it without someone applying paddles to the Dodgers’ flatlining offense.
The Dodgers might not be going down without a fight. But so far, they are going down without any of the things it takes to make an offense successful in the postseason.
They are 2 for 16 with runners in scoring position in this series, 3 for 32 in the postseason. They have just two two-out hits in the three NLCS games (both singles) and only two extra-base hits (both doubles). The Dodgers hit 204 home runs in the regular season (tied for fourth in the National League) and eight more in their four-game National League Division Series victory over the Atlanta Braves (the most in the postseason to that point). They have hit none in the NLCS.
“They’re really good pitchers,” Miguel Rojas said. “A lot of their pitchers throw three different fastballs. They throw hard. They’ve been locating the ball really well. They haven’t really given us too many opportunities to build momentum.
“They’ve been attacking the zone. They trust their stuff in the zone. With all three fastballs, with a lot of guys that have a cutter, a sinker and a four-seam fastball, it’s really hard to kind of put barrels on the ball. So you’ve got to build some momentum that you can create with hits, but we haven’t been able to get a big hit.”
The Brewers have grabbed any momentum right back from the Dodgers. The Dodgers have scored in just five of the 27 innings so far. Four of those five times, the Brewers responded by scoring in the next half-inning themselves.
It happened again to turn Game 3.
Snell hadn’t give up a home run this year but Jackson Chourio sent the first pitch he threw Wednesday into the right-field pavilion. Snell thoroughly dominated the Brewers through six innings after that. He retired 18 of 20 batters after Chourio’s home run, striking out nine. Through the first five innings, the Brewers swung at 32 of Snell’s pitches and missed (17) more times than they made contact.
But the Dodgers’ lifeless offense did nothing against the Brewers’ second consecutive rookie starter, Robert Gasser, who held them scoreless on three hits and a walk through five innings.
Brewers manager Pat Murphy went to his bullpen after that, calling on Abner Uribe for the seventh time in their seven postseason games. When Uribe took the mound, the Brewers’ relievers had pitched 9⅔ scoreless innings in the NLCS and had allowed just one earned run in 28⅔ innings this postseason.
But Uribe walked the bases loaded, retiring just one batter. That brought up Will Smith – 1 for his first 25 this postseason. Smith jumped on a first-pitch fastball from Uribe and lined it off the wall in left-center field for a two-run double and a 2-1 lead.
It was the kind of clutch hit that Smith has provided time and time again over the years and had the stadium rocking.
Murphy made his next move, bringing in left-hander DL Hall with runners at second and third. Hall struck out pinch-hitter Kiké Hernandez and Tommy Edman as the Dodgers failed to capitalize on a chance to break the game open.
Snell went back out for the seventh inning having retired 14 in a row. But he walked Andrew Vaughn to start the inning and bring up Jake Bauers whose 12-pitch walk in the third inning of Game 2 was a critical turning point against Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
He did it again, extending his at-bat against Snell for 11 pitches and sending the last one, a fastball over the heart of the plate, into the right-field seats for a two-run home run. Two pitches later, Snell floated a changeup over the middle and Garrett Mitchell sent it on the same flight path as Bauers’ drive.
In 1,200⅔ career innings (regular season), Snell has only given up 15 home runs to left-handed hitters. Bauers and Mitchell did it back-to-back. The Brewers hit 154 home runs during the regular season, the fewest in the National League. They have outhomered the Dodgers 5-0 in the NLCS.
“I mean three home runs in a game — I didn’t give up one the whole year,” Snell said. “To have three in a game is pretty frustrating.”
The Brewers added single runs in the eighth and ninth innings to pull away.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- The Dodgers' dreams of winning a third straight World Series are quickly fading.
The defending champion Dodgers are in danger of being swept by the Brewers after Milwaukee beat Los Angeles 6-2 to take a 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series.
After a Will Smith double gave the Dodgers a 2-1 lead in the sixth inning, the Brewers immediately answered in the seventh with two home runs off Blake Snell: a two-run blast by Jake Bauers, followed by a solo shot by Garrett Mitchell.
Milwaukee added a run in the eighth after a wild pitch that brought in a runner from third base. The Brewers added another run in the ninth.
Jackson Chourio hit a solo homer on the first pitch of the game.
Los Angeles now faces a must-win game Thursday at Dodger Stadium. Tyler Glasnow is set to pitch for the Dodgers.
This is a developing story. This article will continue to be updated as more information becomes available.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are running out of games to lose if they want to advance to the World Series for a third straight season.
LA is currently down 2-0, but the NLCS has shifted to Los Angeles, which could the Dodgers a slight edge over the next two games (at home).
Moments before the huge Game 3 between the Brewers and Dodgers, a piece of off-field news surrounding Will Smith emerged.
More MLB on Heavy: Max Muncy News Emerges Before Pivotal Brewers-Dodgers NLCS Game 3
Will Smith Becomes Dad to Third Child!!
Just moments before the pivotal Game 3 against the Brewers, Will Smith's wife, Cara, announced a major piece of life news for the Smith family.
She has successfully given birth to her and Will's third child!
Here is the post the two share on Instagram, and they hint that their new daughter's name is 'Carter':
Perhaps this huge piece of life news can get Will Smith going at the plate in the NLCS, as the Dodgers' 2025 World Series hero has slumped since the beginning of the MLB playoffs.
Perhaps being at home will help wake Will Smith regardless.
However, either way, huge congrats to the Smith family for adding a new member to their growing family.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Quietly Announce Roster News on 6-Year MLB Player
Taking a Quick Look at Will Smith's MLB Career
Will Smith is a 3X World Series champion with the Los Angeles Dodgers. He's also been named to the MLB All-Star team three times.
Since making his MLB debut in 2019, Smith has spent his entire 8-year career with the Dodgers.
Over 795 total games played in his career, Smith has 138 home runs, 137 doubles, 476 RBI, and a lifetime OPS+ of 127.
He's been a lifeline for the Dodgers offense in many big moments in his career, and the Dodgers will continue to call his name during the playoffs.

item.title: [New York Post] Blake Snell’s seventh-inning meltdown turns Dodgers’ lead into a nightmare
item.dc:creator: Thomas L Murray
item.description: For as good as Blake Snell was in Game 3 of the NLCS on Wednesday night, it was the long ball that got the best of him. Snell, who came into the postseason without giving up a home run during the regular season, gave up three to the Brewers. item.content:encoded:
For as good as Blake Snell was in Game 3 of the NLCS on Wednesday night, it was the long ball that got the best of him.
Snell, who came into the postseason without giving up a home run during the regular season, gave up three to the Brewers.
Snell spent most of the night playing from behind, as he put himself in a 1-run deficit after Jackson Chourio blasted a solo shot over the right center field wall, from a 97.6 mph fastball.
Snell went ahead and settled in afterward striking out nine batters and giving up two hits before disaster struck in the seventh.
After his catcher Will Smith got him his first lead of the night in the sixth inning, Snell immediately gave it back up.
When Snell took the mound in the seventh, he opened the inning by giving up a walk to Andrew Vaughn.
Brewers manager Pat Murphy quickly removed him from the game and put in Christian Yelich as a pinch runner.
Murphy’s move wouldn’t end up being a factor as Jake Bauers had other plans.
Bowers and Snell had a long 11-pitch at-bat, where he showed plenty of muscle, including on the 10th pitch when he hooked a ball foul, resulting in it landing just outside of a home run.
On the 11th pitch, he made up for the previous swing by launching a 97.8 mph four-seam fastball over the right field fence for a 412-foot home run.
In the next at-bat, Milwaukee tacked on an insurance run when Snell left a changeup hanging in the center of the strike zone — landing 428 feet over the center field fence to give Los Angeles a 4-2 deficit.
Snell was replaced after the home run and finished the night giving up only four hits, four runs and two walks.

Betts was the best player on the 2020 championship team. He finished in the top five in National League MVP voting three of his first four seasons with the Dodgers.
