item.title: [DodgersBeat] Roberts Calls Yoshinobu Yamamoto's Preparation "Spectacular"
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WI — Dave Roberts has watched Yoshinobu Yamamoto prepare for enough big starts to know how much work goes into his calm on the mound. Before Monday’s Game 2 in Milwaukee, Roberts called that preparation “spectacular” and compared his care for each detail with Clayton Kershaw’s. With the Dodgers trailing the series 1–0, Yamamoto gets the ball against Logan Henderson. Roberts also made a change to the batting order, moving Teoscar Hernández up and Will Smith to fifth. “Everything he doe
item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE, WI — Dave Roberts has watched Yoshinobu Yamamoto prepare for enough big starts to know how much work goes into his calm on the mound. Before Monday’s Game 2 in Milwaukee, Roberts called that preparation “spectacular” and compared his care for each detail with Clayton Kershaw’s. With the Dodgers trailing the series 1–0, Yamamoto gets the ball against Logan Henderson. Roberts also made a change to the batting order, moving Teoscar Hernández up and Will Smith to fifth.
“Everything he does is for a purpose”
Asked what helps Yamamoto thrive in big moments, Roberts began with the person behind the pitches.
“Part of it is who he is, as far as his makeup, his toughness, the work ethic, the culture piece of it,” Roberts said. “Everything he does is for a purpose, really. When you work and prepare the way he does, I’ve never seen anyone prepare like him. No one.”
“When you take it into a game, that’s why he is so unflappable and continues to make pitches when he needs to. Obviously, the pitch mix is next level. The delivery is next level. He has pitches to get left and right out. The command is next level.”
Roberts sees that work as a foundation for how Yamamoto handles pressure.
“The moment never gets too big. He manages his heartbeat,” he said. “I had Clayton Kershaw for 10 years, and no one did it like him until Yamamoto, in the sense of every single thing he does and what it takes to prepare for a day. It’s spectacular.”
Teoscar moves up, Smith hits fifth
Roberts moved Smith down two spots, giving Hernández an earlier turn against Henderson’s fastball, changeup and cutter.
“With this pitcher in particular, I like Teo. For Teo to get three cracks at this guy, I like it,” Roberts said. “Teo’s swinging well. But that five spot, as we talked about in the DS, the game falls to the five spot a lot.”
“Will’s going to have a chance to get a couple two-out hits that can change the game. Moving down two spots, but it’s still a very, very important spot.”
Smith said earlier that his swing feels better than his results. Roberts has seen signs of that, too.
“The last couple games, it’s been better. He still takes a good at-bat. It just hasn’t lined up yet,” Roberts said. “In this moment in time, everything rightfully is more magnified. It’s five games. All it takes is squaring one ball up, and it flips.”
“I still trust him in the batter’s box.”
A different test against Henderson
The Dodgers expect a different challenge from Henderson than they faced against Jacob Misiorowski in the opener.
“Good young pitcher. We’ve seen him a couple times,” Roberts said. “It’s a really good fastball that plays up with the characteristics, low slot. He’s got a good changeup that runs, misses the bat. Good versus right and left, and a good athlete.”
“It’s going to be a tough battle. It’s going to be a different approach than a Misiorowski kind of thing. He’s really good. Very, very good young pitcher.”
Roberts liked the work of his lineup Sunday. Now he wants more of those at-bats to end with hits.
“I like the intent, one through nine. I like the fight, seeing pitches, winning pitches,” he said. “Now it gets to finishing off the at-bat with some hits, hitting some outfield grass and trying to get more line drives versus the fly balls.”
“I think that’s inches, centimeters. I’ll bet on how we go about taking at-bats to then expect a good result. We’ve got to go out there with the same intent, and then we’ll put up some runs.”
Taking their shots
Roberts believes the Dodgers can use their power against Henderson while still finding ways to move runners and bring them home.
“We’re built to slug. Henderson’s a heck of a pitcher, but we’ve got to be able to take some shots and see if we can knock the ball out of the ballpark,” he said.
“You still need to take those at-bats and be able to get a base hit, hit behind a runner, like Andy did yesterday to drive in a run. That’s baseball.”
“As far as the bunt, the hit-and-run, stuff like that, you also have to have the right personnel.”

item.title: [Reviewing the Brew] Dave Roberts’ exposed Game 1 strategy reveals key NLCS matchup for Brewers
item.dc:creator: Owen Jonas
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers set the series tone on Sunday night with a narrow victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 1 of the NLCS. Powered by excellent infield defense, which produced three ground-ball double plays, an incredible swing from Brice Turang that led to a game-tying home run off Tarik Skubal, and another dominant performance from their bullpen, Pat Murphy's squad built a key 1-0 series lead in their quest to knock off the reigning back-to-back World Series champs. After Turang's gam
item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers set the series tone on Sunday night with a narrow victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 1 of the NLCS. Powered by excellent infield defense, which produced three ground-ball double plays, an incredible swing from Brice Turang that led to a game-tying home run off Tarik Skubal, and another dominant performance from their bullpen, Pat Murphy's squad built a key 1-0 series lead in their quest to knock off the reigning back-to-back World Series champs.
After Turang's game-tying solo shot in the fourth, the Brewers took the lead in the bottom of the fifth thanks to an RBI single from rookie right fielder Luis Lara. The Brewers maintained that narrow one-run lead through the final four innings of the series opener, but they certainly had opportunities to add on to their run total.
Milwaukee's best scoring opportunity came in the bottom of the eighth inning. Jackson Chourio led off the inning with a single to right field off right-handed reliever Evan Phillips. After the leadoff hit, Dodgers manager turned to southpaw Tanner Scott to face Brice Turang, who promptly laid down a sacrifice bunt to advance Chourio to second base, setting up an RBI opportunity for William Contreras.
However, with the left-handed Scott on the mound, Roberts elected to intentionally walk Contreras, setting up a tough left-on-left matchup for Jake Bauers. Scott struck out Bauers on six pitches, which brought lefty-crusher Andrew Vaughn to the plate. Once again, Roberts elected to intentionally walk the righty to set up a left-on-left matchup with Garrett Mitchell. In doing so, however, Roberts moved a key insurance run to third base, where a passed ball or wild pitch would have given the Brewers a two-run lead, and a single would have given them a three-run advantage.
It was undoubtedly a risk for Roberts and the Dodgers -- loading the bases for Mitchell -- but one that paid off on Sunday night. However, in doing so, Roberts exposed a strategy he may use throughout the remainder of the series: prioritizing matchups between his left-handed relievers and the Brewers' left-handed hitters. Such a strategy means the Brewers lefties will have to find ways to produce against Los Angeles' tough bullpen southpaws throughout the series.
The pressure is on the Brewers' left-handed hitters to produce against Dodgers' tough lefty relievers
Left-on-left matchups are something the Brewers are bound to see a lot of throughout the NLCS. From starters Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell to a quartet of lefty relievers in Alex Vesia, Tanner Scott, Kris Bubic, and Justin Wrobleski, Milwaukee can expect to see plenty of southpaws throughout their rematch with the Dodgers.
Clearly, based on last night's strategy, Roberts is going to prioritize matching those lefties up with the Brewers' left-handed hitters by any means necessary. That means there will likely be situations, like last night, where Bauers, Mitchell, Brice Turang, and Christian Yelich will be asked to produce against a same-side pitcher. Concerningly for the Brewers, of that group only Bauers (.901 OPS vs. LHP) had an OPS better than .668 against left-handed pitching during the regular season.
Bauers commented on his improved success against left-handed pitching this year during his pre-game press conference on Monday morning, saying, "A lot of it just has to do with getting the opportunity to see them more often, and then I think I've really focused on developing an approach that gives me the best chance."
On the topic of opportunities, Bauers set a new career-high with 160 plate appearances against left-handed pitchers this year, and already that practice against lefties is coming in handy in the NLCS. Bauers acknowledged the difficult southpaws on the Dodgers' NLCS roster, saying, "Some of these guys, obviously it's not easy, whether it be high arm slot coming from behind you or someone throwing from the side," but in four at-bats in Game 1 last night, all of which came against left-handed pitchers, Bauers went 1-for-3 with a walk and a hard-hit single. Pair that with Turang's impressive blast off Skubal, and the Brewers' left-handers are off to a strong start against same-side pitchers in the NLCS.
Assuming Roberts continues to prioritize these matchups, even if it means intentionally putting runners on base, the pressure will be on Bauers, Turang, and the rest of the Brewers' lefties to continue putting together strong at-bats in these situations. If they can find success against southpaws early in the series, it will certainly complicate Roberts' pitching plan going forward.

item.title: [Yardbarker] MLB Legend Derek Jeter Doesn’t Hold Back About Dodgers’ Shohei Ohtani

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers fell 2-1 to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series on Sunday night, as Shohei Ohtani continued to struggle at the plate during the 2026 postseason.
Ohtani went 1-for-3 with a walk and scored the Dodgers’ only run in the opener. Through five playoff games, he has three hits in 16 at-bats for a .188 average, two runs scored, three walks, no home runs and no RBIs, along with a .188 slugging percentage and roughly a .503 OPS.
Those numbers sit well below what the Dodgers have come to expect from their two-way star. He finished the regular season hitting .275 with 30 home runs, 81 RBIs and an .889 OPS in 135 games, though injuries limited him late in the year.
Left knee soreness and right biceps inflammation forced Ohtani onto the injured list for about two weeks in September. He did not pitch after early July and has said he will need to manage the issues through the playoffs rather than play at full strength.
Derek Jeter, speaking on the MLB on FOX postgame show with Alex Rodriguez and David Ortiz, pointed to how much the Dodgers rely on Ohtani even when he is not at his peak.
“In a seven game series Shohei Ohtani’s probably going to win you at least one game,” Jeter said. “By himself, usually historically that’s what he’s done. If you take that game away and flip it to the other team now all of the sudden we have a great series. And as he goes, the Los Angeles Dodgers go. The hitters in front of him do better, the hitters behind him are hitting with him on base all day long. So I definitely think they need Shohei Ohtani if we’re going to see the Dodgers at full strength.”
The Brewers entered the series with baseball’s best regular-season record at 103-59, a franchise high, after holding the top spot for much of the year. They swept the Padres in the Division Series and now hold a 1-0 lead over Los Angeles.
The Dodgers finished 100-62 and are chasing a third straight World Series title, something no team has done since the New York Yankees from 1998 to 2000. They still possess a deep lineup and strong pitching, but the early loss underscored how different the series can look without Ohtani producing.
Los Angeles has experience in these matchups. The Dodgers swept the Brewers in last year’s NLCS, part of a stretch in which Milwaukee had dropped seven straight postseason games to them entering Sunday.
Game 2 is set for Monday afternoon at American Family Field. The Dodgers will start right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who is 1-0 with a 1.29 ERA in one postseason start this year and owns a strong career playoff track record. The Brewers counter with right-hander Logan Henderson.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts kept Ohtani in the cleanup spot for Game 2 after some earlier lineup shuffling. The team has scored only 15 runs across its five postseason games so far and has struggled with runners in scoring position.
Even at less than full health, Ohtani remains the player most likely to change the series by himself. The Brewers’ regular-season dominance and early lead have made them the clear favorite if the Dodgers’ offense stays quiet.
The series shifts to Dodger Stadium for Games 3 through 5 later in the week if it continues that long. Both clubs know a long series would favor the team that gets more from its biggest bats.
Ohtani’s recent history includes big October moments, including an NLCS MVP performance last year. Whether that version returns in time will likely decide how far the Dodgers go.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Yankees Could Find Their Bullpen Fix in Dodgers’ Run
item.dc:creator: Alvin Garcia
item.description: The New York Yankees need more dependable bullpen innings in 2027, and one possible answer is still pitching in October. Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Alex Vesia deserves consideration as New York evaluates its offseason options. Vesia appeared in NLCS Game 1 on October 11, when MLB highlighted his pickoff of Jake Bauers. His postseason role provides a timely opportunity to assess a pitcher who could strengthen the Yankees’ relief corps. The connection remains an analysis of roster fit. The so
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees need more dependable bullpen innings in 2027, and one possible answer is still pitching in October. Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Alex Vesia deserves consideration as New York evaluates its offseason options.
Vesia appeared in NLCS Game 1 on October 11, when MLB highlighted his pickoff of Jake Bauers. His postseason role provides a timely opportunity to assess a pitcher who could strengthen the Yankees’ relief corps.
The connection remains an analysis of roster fit. The sources reviewed do not establish Yankees negotiations with Vesia, and New York has not announced an agreement.
However, his regular-season performance gives the idea substance. Vesia finished 2026 with a 2.64 ERA and 74 strikeouts in 58 innings, according to MLB’s statistics.
Alex Vesia Could Give the Yankees Another Late-Inning Option
That strikeout total translates to approximately 11.5 per nine innings. For a bullpen trying to escape jams without relying on its defense, the ability to miss bats offers a useful starting point.
Joe Najarian’s October 10 Yankees On SI assessment identified relief depth as an offseason concern. He also noted that Brent Headrick led MLB with 81 appearances.
That workload makes another dependable option valuable. A deeper group would give the manager more choices when Headrick needs rest or when an opponent presents a difficult stretch of hitters.
Vesia should be evaluated as a potential complement to Headrick. Adding another left-hander would make sense if he can handle the required matchups, rather than simply duplicate a role New York already fills.
The Yankees should also examine walk rate, performance against right-handed hitters and availability on consecutive days. A strong ERA does not answer every question about how a reliever fits.
That should include inherited runners. A reliever who strands traffic can offer different value from one whose best work starts with an empty inning.
The Yankees’ Closer Decision Still Comes First
David Bednar’s pending free agency creates a separate issue. Signing Vesia would not automatically resolve the ninth inning, and New York should avoid treating one successful addition as a complete bullpen rebuild.
The cleaner plan would address the closer job while strengthening the innings that lead to it. That could involve retaining Bednar and pursuing another experienced arm, depending on contract demands.
MLB lists Vesia among the upcoming free agents. His market could develop differently from New York’s preferred timetable, so the Yankees need alternatives rather than a plan tied to one pitcher.
Price matters, too. There is no verified contract forecast establishing that Vesia would be cheaper than other prominent relief options. His value to the Yankees should determine their offer, with room remaining for additional needs.
For now, the Dodgers’ postseason run gives New York another useful offseason name to evaluate. Vesia’s strikeouts make him an intriguing candidate, but the strongest argument is how he could distribute responsibility across the bullpen.
The Yankees need several trustworthy paths through the late innings. Vesia could help create one of them.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers look to even up the NLCS in Game 2 against the Milwaukee Brewers. Last night, they fell 0-1 in the series after a 2-1 pitching duel.
The Dodgers offense was nearly nonexistent, leaving nine runners on base and going 1-for-6 with RISP.
In today’s 2:00 P.M. PST game, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made a lineup change involving their best postseason hitter.
Kiké Hernández Out, Tommy Edman In vs. Brewers
Per Los Angeles Dodgers reporter David Vassegh, Kiké Hernández will sit tonight with Tommy Edman taking his place at second and batting ninth.
In five games this postseason, Edman has yet to record hit.
In Game 3 against the Atlanta Braves, Hernández hit a towering two-run home run ultimately lifting the Dodgers to victory.
Aside from that home run, both Edman and Hernández’s bats have been awfully quiet.
But, the NLCS is where Edman shines. In 2024, he won NLCS MVP. Recording 11 RBIS–tying a franchise record–with a home run, and a .407 batting average which included a hit in each game.
Last year against Milwakuee in the NLCS, Edman tallied five hits and three RBIs.
Tonight, the Dodgers need at least one bat to breakout and shift the momentum of the series before heading home for Games 3 through 5.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers Trailing Early: Is Shohei Ohtani Ready To Flip The Switch In Game 2?
Shohei Ohtani continues to struggle at the plate for the Los Angeles Dodgers, leaving the ballclub playing catch-up early after dropping Game 1 of the NLCS to the Milwaukee Brewers.
Ohtani is a four-time MVP — winning two in each league — but right when the Dodgers need him most his bat has gone cold. With Los Angeles already trailing by a game heading on the road for Game 2, he remains the make-or-break factor they need to overcome the Brewers.
On the "MLB on FOX" post-game show, Derek Jeter and Alex Rodriguez weighed in on Ohtani’s quiet postseason. Still, both analysts agreed that with or without his bat heating up, the Dodgers should be unfazed and fully capable of taking control in Game 2.
"They need Shohei Ohtani if we’re going to see the Dodgers at full strength," Jeter said. "I don’t think it’s easy to flip a switch, but they don’t have to flip a switch mentally because mentally you walk into that clubhouse, I bet they have the same demeanor as if they won Game 1 because they’ve been here before."
Rodriguez highlighted just how valuable Ohtani is to the Dodgers' lineup. It’s not just that his offense is struggling, but you miss his complete presence on the field, whether it's his raw power, high batting average or ability to create scoring opportunities on the basepaths.
The numbers tell the story. Ohtani is hitting just .188 with three hits across 16 postseason at-bats, leaving a massive void at the top of the Dodgers' lineup.
"As far as Ohtani goes, the thing why he’s so valuable is you’re not just missing power or batting average or running the bases or stealing bases," Rodriguez said. "You’re missing all of it. Plus his presence in the lineup."
Even with Ohtani’s struggles, Rodriguez believes the Dodgers can still win the series if they drop him lower in the batting order to take off the pressure. But if he can’t turn things around and regain his usual form, it only increases the urgency for the rest of the lineup to step up.
"So can they win? Maybe you can kind of hide him in the fourth and fifth slot," Rodriguez continued. "He did go first to third today, but that’s one very hard person to replace. You’re gonna have the other guys to step up and make up for it."

item.content:encoded:
ナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ第1戦（ブルワーズ−ドジャース、11日、ミルウォーキー）米大リーグ、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手（32）がブルワーズとのリーグ優勝決定シリーズに「4番・DH」で出場し、第3打席まで本塁打がなく、メジャー自己ワーストを更新する105打席ノーアーチとなった。
大谷はこの日、二回先頭で四球で出塁し、その後に先制ホームを踏むと、三回の第2打席は空振り三振、六回は救援右腕ウリベと対戦し、左前打だった。大谷は8月18日ロッキーズ戦から105打席ノーアーチで、2022年9月11日アストロズ戦の第2打席から翌23年4月2日アスレチックス戦の第2打席までの104打席を超え、メジャー最悪の数字に伸びた。
9月上旬に「右上腕二頭筋の炎症」で負傷者リスト（IL）入りした大谷は復帰後のレギュラーシーズンで22打席で21打数5安打8三振で、長打1本。地区シリーズでは4試合で13打数2安打で長打ゼロと本塁打の気配が漂っているとは言い難い状況。この日を含め直近17試合で長打は1本しかない。ポストシーズンでは打順も降格し、暗いトンネルを抜ける光明は見えていない。

item.title: [Mediotiempo] Dodgers recupera a Edwin Díaz para la Serie de Campeonato
item.dc:creator: Editorial Mediotiempo
item.description: De cara a su tercera Serie de Campeonato consecutiva en la postemporada de las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol (MLB), los Dodgers tendrían una de las mejores noticias posibles para su relevo con el boricua Edwin Díaz de regreso en su mejor forma, lo que eventualmente le permitirá tomar la mayor cantidad de oportunidades como el cerrador del equipo que busca un tricampeonato en la Serie Mundial. Sugar endulza el relevo de Dodgers para la SCLN Díaz, que tuvo una tropezada temporada de debut con los Dodge
item.content:encoded:
De cara a su tercera Serie de Campeonato consecutiva en la postemporada de las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol (MLB), los Dodgers tendrían una de las mejores noticias posibles para su relevo con el boricua Edwin Díaz de regreso en su mejor forma, lo que eventualmente le permitirá tomar la mayor cantidad de oportunidades como el cerrador del equipo que busca un tricampeonato en la Serie Mundial.
Sugar endulza el relevo de Dodgers para la SCLN
Díaz, que tuvo una tropezada temporada de debut con los Dodgers por una lesión en el codo y otra más en el cuello, tuvo números atípicos para uno de los mejores cerradores de los últimos años en las Grandes Ligas. De regreso en la Serie de Campeonato, el Sugar completó oportunidades de salvamento consecutivas en el Juego 3 y el Juego 4.
“Las últimas dos noches... esa es la razón por la que adquirimos a alguien como Edwin Díaz”, dijo Roberts después de que los Dodgers ganaran la Serie Divisional. “Es uno de los grandes cerradores del juego. Que esté lanzando a su mejor nivel justo ahora es lo que uno espera, y le doy mucho mérito por ello”.
Si bien Roberts y los Dodgers no ha designado nuevamente a Díaz como su cerrador nuevamente, sí le da una opción más para situaciones de alta exigencia con 8 juegos más por ganar para conquistar el tricampeonato del Clásico de Otoño.
“Creo que eso fue lo más importante para mí: que el equipo confía en mí”, dijo Díaz después del último juego de la SDLN. “Me dan la pelota todos los días... Por eso vine aquí, para ganar partidos y cerrar encuentros como este. Así que estoy muy contento en este momento”.
¿Qué opciones tiene Dodgers en el relevo?
Con Díaz volviendo a su nivel élite, los Dodgers pueden barajear las opciones en juegos de alta exigencia, especialmente con Tanner Scott (25 salvamentos en la temporada regular) y Evan Phillips (un rescate en la campaña).
Scott tiene tiempo para reponerse luego del golpe que puede representar recibir un jonrón de dos carreras en el Juego 1 de la Serie Divisional y después registrar holds –ventajas de 3 o menos carreras sostenidas en relevo intermedio– durante el octavo episodio del Juego 3 y 4. Phillips relevó a Scott para quedarse con el salvamento del Juego 1.
Esas dos opciones sirviendo como preparadores le permiten a los Dodgers jugar a Alex Vesia y Edgardo Henriquez como relevo intermedio; Vesia en duelos de zurdo contra zurdo y el venezolano Henriquez en diestro contra diestro.

item.description: LA 다저스가 11일 밤(미국 현지시간) 아메리칸 패밀리 필드에서 열리는 NLCS 1차전을 앞두고 26인 로스터를 확정하면서 13번째 투수를 추가했습니다. 좌완 저스틴 로블레스키가 불펜진에 합류한 반면, 대주자 요원인 김혜성은 로스터에서 제외되었습니다. 예상대로 미겔 로하스(허리 하부 통증)는 NLDS 이후 실시된 훈련과 밀워키 원정길 비행 이후 상태가 양호하다고 판단되어 로스터에 포함되었습니다. 그는 1차전 선발 라인업에는 이름을 올리지 못했으나, 벤치에서 출전 대기했습니다. 7전 4선승제로 치러지는 NLCS를 앞두고 데이브 로버츠 감독은 LA 다저스가 마운드 과부하를 막고 투수진 깊이를 더하기 위해 투수 한 명을 추가로 보강하고자 한다고 밝혔습니다. 올해 처음으로 올스타에 선정되었던 로블레스키가 가장 합리적인 선택지 중 하나였습니다. 그는 지난해 짧은 이닝을 소화하는 구원 등판 경험을 쌓았으나, 필요에 따라 다중 이닝을 책임질 수 있는 스테미너도 여전히 갖추고 있었습니다. 로버츠
item.content:encoded:
LA 다저스가 11일 밤(미국 현지시간) 아메리칸 패밀리 필드에서 열리는 NLCS 1차전을 앞두고 26인 로스터를 확정하면서 13번째 투수를 추가했습니다. 좌완 저스틴 로블레스키가 불펜진에 합류한 반면, 대주자 요원인 김혜성은 로스터에서 제외되었습니다.
예상대로 미겔 로하스(허리 하부 통증)는 NLDS 이후 실시된 훈련과 밀워키 원정길 비행 이후 상태가 양호하다고 판단되어 로스터에 포함되었습니다. 그는 1차전 선발 라인업에는 이름을 올리지 못했으나, 벤치에서 출전 대기했습니다.
7전 4선승제로 치러지는 NLCS를 앞두고 데이브 로버츠 감독은 LA 다저스가 마운드 과부하를 막고 투수진 깊이를 더하기 위해 투수 한 명을 추가로 보강하고자 한다고 밝혔습니다. 올해 처음으로 올스타에 선정되었던 로블레스키가 가장 합리적인 선택지 중 하나였습니다. 그는 지난해 짧은 이닝을 소화하는 구원 등판 경험을 쌓았으나, 필요에 따라 다중 이닝을 책임질 수 있는 스테미너도 여전히 갖추고 있었습니다.
로버츠 감독은 “단연 이닝 소화 능력이 고려되었습니다”라며, “그는 이미 '큰 무대를 경험해 본' 투수이고, 지난해 우리 팀을 위해 대단히 뛰어난 포스트시즌 피칭을 보여주었습니다. 따라서 상대 타선의 특정 좌타자들을 상대로 그를 등판시킬 수 있게 되어 든든하게 생각하고 있습니다”라고 말했습니다.
김혜성은 활성 로스터에서 로블레스키의 자리를 마련하기 위해 제외된 아쉬운 선수가 되었습니다. 김혜성은 빠른 발을 인정받아 NLDS 로스터에 포함되었으나, LA 다저스는 그를 대주자로 활용하지 않았습니다. 지난 시리즈에서 그의 유일한 출전은 로하스의 부상 여파로 인한 대수비 출전이었습니다.
벤치에 남은 마지막 두 명의 야수는 김혜성과 LA 다저스 최고 유망주(MLB 파이프라인 전체 4위) 호수에 데 파울라였습니다. 데 파울라 역시 김혜성과 마찬가지로 단 하나의 명확한 목적을 가지고 있었습니다: 그는 벤치에서 출전하는 핵심 좌완 대타 요원이었으며, 절대적으로 필요한 상황이 아닌 이상 수비에 투입되지는 않을 것이었습니다. 데 파울라는 NLDS 4차전 당시 앤디 파헤스의 역전 적시타로 이어진 반격 과정에서 대타 볼넷을 골라냈으며, 타석에서 보여준 꾸준한 타격 생산성을 고려할 때 LA 다저스가 NLCS에서도 그를 유지하는 것이 더 타당했습니다.
로버츠 감독은 “내야 수비 측면에서는 키케 [에르난데스], 토미 [에드먼], 미기(로하스)가 있고 외야 유틸리티 자원도 갖추고 있습니다”라며, “벤치에서 나오는 데 파울라의 타석에서의 뛰어난 품질을 포기하기는 대단히 어려웠습니다. 그것이 우리가 결단을 내린 부분이었습니다”라고 말했습니다.
다음은 최종 26인 로스터입니다:
포수 (2): 윌 스미스, 헌터 페두시아
1루수 (1): 프레디 프리먼
2루수 (1): 토미 에드먼
유격수 (1): 무키 베츠
3루수 (1): 맥스 먼시
외야수 (3): 테오스카 에르난데스, 앤디 파헤스, 카일 터커
유틸리티/벤치 (3): 키케 에르난데스, 미겔 로하스, 호수에 데 파울라
투타겸업 (1): 오타니 쇼헤이
선발 투수 (4): 타릭 스쿠발, 야마모토 요시노부, 블레이크 스넬, 타일러 글래스노우
구원 투수 (9): 에드윈 디아스, 태너 스캇, 에드가르도 엔리케스, 알렉스 베시아, 에반 필립스, 사사키 로키, 크리스 부비치, 브록 스튜어트, 저스틴 로블레스키
출처 : " Sonja Chen " 기자 " Dodgers add lefty Wrobleski to NLCS roster, leave off speedster Kim " < MLB.com > " 2026년 10월 11일 "(미국 현지시간)

item.title: [日刊スポーツ] 敵将マーフィー監督、不振の大谷翔平でも「トップレベルの状態にあると思って戦う」 - ＭＬＢ : 日刊スポーツ
item.description: ブルワーズのパット・マーフィー監督が、今ポストシーズン（PS)でまだ調子の上がらないドジャース大谷翔平投手（32）について、試合前の会見で言及した。 大谷はシーズン終盤で左ひざの炎症と右上腕二頭筋の炎症を抱え、負傷者リスト（IL）入り。復帰後も本調子とはいかず、ブレーブスとの地区シリーズでは4試合で13打数2安打の打率1割5分4厘で長打はまだなく、打点もまだ挙げていない。 マーフィー監督は、第1戦前の会見で大谷はスランプに陥っているがそれでもまだ危険な打者だと思うかと問われ「何だって。冗談を言っているのか」と苦笑い。「あの男は、シーズンのこの時期にどんなパフォーマンスをすべきか知っている。そして彼は、とんでもない才能の持ち主だ。野球というのは、28打数1安打という状態でも、突然変わることがある」と話した。 さらに「オオタニは、それだけの選手。私は今も彼を尊敬しているし、私の選手たちもそうだ。彼はトップレベルの状態にあると思って戦う」と話した。
item.content:encoded:
ブルワーズのパット・マーフィー監督が、今ポストシーズン（PS)でまだ調子の上がらないドジャース大谷翔平投手（32）について、試合前の会見で言及した。
大谷はシーズン終盤で左ひざの炎症と右上腕二頭筋の炎症を抱え、負傷者リスト（IL）入り。復帰後も本調子とはいかず、ブレーブスとの地区シリーズでは4試合で13打数2安打の打率1割5分4厘で長打はまだなく、打点もまだ挙げていない。
マーフィー監督は、第1戦前の会見で大谷はスランプに陥っているがそれでもまだ危険な打者だと思うかと問われ「何だって。冗談を言っているのか」と苦笑い。「あの男は、シーズンのこの時期にどんなパフォーマンスをすべきか知っている。そして彼は、とんでもない才能の持ち主だ。野球というのは、28打数1安打という状態でも、突然変わることがある」と話した。
さらに「オオタニは、それだけの選手。私は今も彼を尊敬しているし、私の選手たちもそうだ。彼はトップレベルの状態にあると思って戦う」と話した。

item.title: [이투데이] 김혜성, 다저스 NLCS 26인 명단 제외⋯로블레스키 합류
item.dc:creator: 장영준

item.content:encoded:
김혜성(LA 다저스)이 미국프로야구 메이저리그(MLB) 내셔널리그 챔피언십시리즈(NLCS) 출전 명단에서 제외됐다. 다저스가 투수진을 보강하면서 김혜성 대신 좌완 투수 저스틴 로블레스키를 선택했다.
12일(한국시간) MLB 공식 홈페이지에 따르면 다저스는 밀워키 브루어스와의 NLCS를 앞두고 26인 로스터를 확정했다. 다저스는 디비전시리즈(NLDS)와 비교해 야수를 14명에서 13명으로 줄이고 투수를 12명에서 13명으로 늘렸다.
로스터에서 빠진 선수는 김혜성이다. 다저스는 7전 4승제로 치러지는 NLCS에서 투수 운용에 여유를 확보하기 위해 여러 이닝을 소화할 수 있는 로블레스키를 추가했다.
김혜성은 애틀랜타 브레이브스와의 NLDS에서 대주자와 수비 교체 자원으로 명단에 포함됐지만 출전 기회는 제한적이었다. 4차전에서 부상당한 미겔 로하스를 대신해 수비수로 출전한 것이 유일한 경기 출전이었다. 대주자로는 기용되지 않았다.
다저스는 허리 통증을 겪었던 로하스를 NLCS 명단에 그대로 포함했다. 여기에 대타 자원인 유망주 호수에 데 파울라까지 잔류하면서 김혜성이 로스터에서 밀려났다.
데이브 로버츠 다저스 감독은 내야와 외야에서 활용할 수 있는 선수들이 충분하다는 점을 설명하면서 데 파울라의 타격 능력을 높이 평가했다. 데 파울라는 NLDS 4차전에서 대타로 출전해 볼넷을 골라내며 역전 기회를 만드는 데 기여했다.
새롭게 합류한 로블레스키는 정규시즌 28경기에서 12승 5패, 평균자책점 3.66을 기록했다. 22경기에 선발 등판했고 9월부터는 불펜으로도 활용됐다. 올해 처음 올스타에 선정된 로블레스키는 여러 이닝을 책임질 수 있다는 점에서 다저스의 선택을 받았다.
로버츠 감독은 로블레스키의 합류 배경에 대해 포스트시즌 경험과 긴 이닝을 소화할 수 있는 능력, 상대 좌타자 대응 등을 고려했다고 밝혔다.
김혜성은 올해 정규시즌 43경기에 출전해 타율 0.259, 출루율 0.323, 장타율 0.328을 기록했다. NLDS에 이어 NLCS까지 출전 명단에 이름을 올리지는 못하면서 다저스의 포스트시즌 일정에도 당분간 벤치 밖에서 대기하게 됐다.
다저스는 11일(현지시간) 미국 위스콘신주 밀워키 아메리칸패밀리필드에서 밀워키와 NLCS 1차전을 치른다. 7전 4승제에서 승리한 팀은 월드시리즈에 진출한다.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Yoshinobu Yamamoto Keeps His Approach Steady for NLCS
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb

item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE, WI — Yoshinobu Yamamoto will take the ball Monday against a Brewers lineup he sees as strong from top to bottom. Speaking in Japanese ahead of his Game 2 start, he stressed staying focused, limiting runs and working through hitters one at a time. He also explained how his daily routine helps him get ready to pitch even as his body feels different from day to day. In his third MLB postseason, Yamamoto believes experience can help while his approach to each start stays the same.
Staying sharp against the Brewers
Yamamoto expects Milwaukee to make the Dodgers earn their outs.
“My impression is that they’re a team with very few weaknesses,” he said. “I want to stay focused and pitch well so that we’re careful about making mistakes on our side first.”
Asked about the importance of pitching deep into games, Yamamoto put the focus on the work that gets him there.
“In the postseason, I put more weight on keeping runs to a minimum and retiring each batter one at a time,” he said. “That’s something I value especially in October. I think that leads to pitching deeper into games as a result.”
His aim is to bring the same care to a regular-season start that he brings to an October game.
“I pitch every game during the season with the same mindset as an important game like this,” he said. “For an important postseason game, my mindset is to do what I always do.”
“I’ve valued that approach for years and years. There are failures along the way, but little by little, I feel the number of games in which I’m able to pitch well has grown.”
A routine built over years
Yamamoto’s training routine has drawn plenty of interest. For him, its value comes from the years he has spent following it.
“I’ve been doing the same training since I became a professional at 18,” he said. “I still value it just as much today.”
“I think it’s very important to keep doing the same things every day with the same mindset and the same intensity.”
That steady work helps him prepare through the daily changes in how his body feels.
“Your physical condition is different every day,” Yamamoto said. “Of course, sometimes the differences are small and sometimes they’re large, but your condition changes every day.”
“My routine is about getting myself into the same condition by the time I’m ready to play.”
Experience grows, the mindset stays
Asked about his strong road results, Yamamoto gave a modest answer.
“I’m not doing anything different in particular, and even I don’t really know the exact reason,” he said. “For some reason, the results have been good.”
A reporter also brought up the determination Yamamoto had expressed before last year’s Game 2 against Milwaukee and asked whether another year of experience had changed how he felt.
“My mindset going into a game is always the same,” Yamamoto said. “There’s last year’s experience, and this is my third postseason here, so of course there will be situations where that experience helps.”
“But in terms of how I feel going into the game, it’s the same.”

A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.content:encoded:
「難しく考える必要はない」スクバル、山本由伸でブルワーズを圧倒 ド軍サイトが描く“理想のシナリオ”「本拠地決着を」
敵地では山本とスクバルが先発予定だ(C)Getty Images
今季も世界一の座に向け、着実にポストシーズンを勝ち上がっているドジャース。ブレーブスとの地区シリーズ（NLDS）を3勝1敗で制し、現地時間10月11日からはブルワーズとのリーグ優勝決定シリーズ（NLCS）がスタートする。昨季と同じカードとなったNLCSでは、ドジャースはタリク・スクバル、山本由伸がそれぞれ敵地での1、2戦目の先発予定として発表されている。7戦4勝制のシリーズにおいて、序盤の先発マウンドが託される球界屈指の両先発投手への期待は膨らむばかりだ。
NLDSでは3戦目に先発した山本が、このブルワーズとのNLCSでは2戦目に先発する。現在のドジャース先発陣において、もっとも信頼出来るスクバルと山本の2人を立てることで、昨年の4連勝突破再現の可能性も高まる。
ドジャース専門サイト『DODGERS NATION』も10日配信のトピックで、スクバル、山本を2戦目までに並べる先発起用に対し、敵地で連勝も狙える「強力な組み合わせ」と評価。さらに、「ドジャースとデーブ・ロバーツ監督は、この決断について難しく考える必要はなかっただろう」と綴っている。
また、初戦先発予定のスクバルがシーズンを通して、敵地で好結果を残していると説明。同メディアは、「2026年シーズン、スクバルは本拠地での14試合の先発で防御率3.63だった一方、敵地での12試合では防御率1.70を記録している」と今季の成績を紹介し、その上で、「仮に第1戦が思い通りの結果にならなかったとしても、ドジャースには敵地で行われる第2戦に、とっておきのエースが控えている」と論じている。

item.title: [New York Post] Brewers manager on Dodgers’ Tarik Skubal: ‘I just want to step on his throat’
item.dc:creator: Valentina Martinez
item.description: Brewers manager Pat Murphy made his intentions for Game 1 of the National League Championship Series clear. “I just want to step on his throat,” Murphy said of Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal. “I mean that respectfully.” The Brewers lineup will be looking to exploit any mistakes from Skubal in Sunday’s game at American Family Field. item.content:encoded:
Brewers manager Pat Murphy made his intentions for Game 1 of the National League Championship Series clear.
“I just want to step on his throat,” Murphy said of Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal.
“I mean that respectfully.”
The Brewers lineup will be looking to exploit any mistakes from Skubal in Sunday’s game at American Family Field. A few months ago, Skubal wasn’t even donning Dodger blue.
The two-time Cy Young winner was highly-coveted at the trade deadline and it was the back-to-back World Series champions who managed to land Skubal in a blockbuster trade with the Tigers. Since his arrival to LA, Skubal is sporting a 2.61 ERA with 70 strikeouts across 61 innings pitched.
Now, the left-hander has been given the honor of starting NLCS Game 1 for the Dodgers.
It won’t be an easy feat as Skubal will have to fend off a Brewers lineup that is one of the best offenses in baseball. As Murphy hopes, Milwaukee looks to suffocate Skubal on the mound with their quality at-bats and small ball fundamentals.
Opposite Skubal is National League Cy Young candidate Jacob Misiorowski, who is bound to give the Dodgers lineup some trouble.
The matchup will be the Dodgers’ biggest test of October thus far and the competition will be much, much tougher than it was in 2025, when LA swept the Brewers in four games in the NLCS.
Sunday starts with the Dodgers’ crown jewel of the trade deadline — Skubal.

item.content:encoded:
Brewers' Pat Murphy sends warning to Tarik Skubal before NLCS Game 1 appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Milwaukee Brewers are getting ready to take on the Los Angeles Dodgers, in the National League Championship Series. Brewers manager Pat Murphy is sending a message to Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal, before Game 1.
That message is a powerful one.
"I want to step on his throat," Murphy said, per WFRV-TV in Wisconsin.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
The Dodgers and Brewers play Game 1 on Sunday night. Milwaukee's players are ready to go.
"Coming into the postseason, you had a feeling you were going to have to go through L.A.," Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich said, per MLB.com. "They're back-to-back champs, and they're a great team. We have a lot of respect for those guys.
"At the same time, we feel like we can play with anybody when we play our game. When we play our brand of baseball, when we play clean and execute, we're a really hard team to beat. We're going to go in there and grind."
It will be a tough challenge for the Brewers against Skubal. Skubal famously was traded to Los Angeles this season from the Detroit Tigers, ahead of the MLB trade deadline.
"Skubal showed exactly why the Dodgers swung big to acquire him from the Tigers ahead of the Trade Deadline in his NLDS Game 1 start, when he struck out seven across six innings of one-run ball against the Braves. Now, he will take the hill as L.A. begins the next stage of its title defense," MLB.com added.
The Brewers had an outstanding season in the National League. The team won the NL Central, and won 103 games. Milwaukee has done just about everything the last few years but make a World Series.
That is because the Dodgers have always stood in the way. Los Angeles is looking for their third consecutive World Series title this season.
Time will tell if this is finally the year that the Brewers break through that glass ceiling.
Related: Is Christian Yelich in NLCS Game 1 starting lineup vs. Tarik Skubal, Dodgers?
Related: Dodgers' Miguel Rojas injury update for NLCS is absolutely crucial

item.title: [Heavy.com] Milwaukee Brewers Manager Takes Shot at Tarik Skubal Before NLCS Game One
item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers are set for a battle in the National League Championship Series. Game One kicks off the potential seven-game series with perhaps the best pitching matchup of the entire MLB season between 2X Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal and likely NL Cy Young winner Jacob Misiorowski. Ahead of the star-studded pitching matchup, Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy took a shot at Skubal in a bizarre way. More MLB on Heavy: Anthony Volpe Sounds Off On New York Ya
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers are set for a battle in the National League Championship Series.
Game One kicks off the potential seven-game series with perhaps the best pitching matchup of the entire MLB season between 2X Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal and likely NL Cy Young winner Jacob Misiorowski.
Ahead of the star-studded pitching matchup, Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy took a shot at Skubal in a bizarre way.
More MLB on Heavy: Anthony Volpe Sounds Off On New York Yankees with 2-Word Message
Pat Murphy Takes Jab At Tarik Skubal
There’s no doubt that Tarik Skubal is a very stingy pitcher, and it’s very hard to string together success against him, especially in the playoffs.
Skubal has rounded into postseason form over his last handful of starts (Which included a strong Game 1 start against the Atlanta Braves in the NLDS), and looks to be at his peak at the right time.
Per @DodgersNation, Pat Murphy said this about how to beat Skubal:
“Step on his throat… Respectfully.”
“I mean that respectfully because I really like Tarik. My brain can’t go any place else. Go to work, that’s the only mentality I can have.”
It’s a pretty bizarre statement to make before facing a pitcher, but it shows how intense Murphy is and how fired up he is for this matchup.
More MLB on Heavy: Pat Murphy Sounds Off On Tarik Skubal Before Dodgers-Brewers NLCS
Dodgers Set for Battle In NLCS with Brewers
The Milwaukee Brewers are clearly coming into this NLCS with a bit of an edge in terms of being fired up for the matchup.
That’s not to say that the Dodgers aren’t amped up, because they very much are, but after LA swept the Brewers in the 2025 NLCS, it’s hard to think that the Brewers haven’t been thinking about that all year, and in terms of regular-season wins, Milwaukee had an even better campaign in 2026.
However, this Dodgers team is absolutely battle-tested, and they are set up perfectly for another World Series run.
Having Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitching games one and two, and once the series shifts to LA after two games, will allow some comfort for starters Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow to pitch at home, which might be a huge boost in the series for the Dodgers.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Kyle Tucker Decision Before NLCS Game 1

item.content:encoded:
Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy has one thing on his mind as his team faces Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Tarik Skubal in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series on Sunday.
"I just want to step on his throat," Murphy told reporters. He added, "I mean that respectfully, because I really like Tarik, but I just want to beat him."
The Brewers were unable to land Skubal at the trade deadline despite reportedly making a handsome offer to the Detroit Tigers. Instead, the Dodgers acquired the two-time Cy Young winner.
"I just think about, get it done right now," Murphy said. "He's going to be fine. I'm sure he's going to be able to feed his family and be a great dad. He can lose tonight and be fine."
Skubal starts Game 1 of the NLCS opposite Jacob Misiorowski for the Brewers.
